options.C: Prepare additional Division 01 sections as necessary
options.D: Refuse the engagement until the owner relinquishes Division 01

questions.explanation: When the owner supplies Division 01, the A/E should still add whatever further Division 01 sections are needed to carry out its own contractual duties, coordinating them with the related sections, alternates, allowances, and unit prices.
questions.source: preliminary review of the project manual

questions.question: Two abbreviation tables in a drawing set list 'WT.' as both WEIGHT and WINDOW. The most direct consequence the A/E should anticipate from such inconsistency is that it can:

options.A: Shift document precedence to the specifications by default
options.B: Void the contractor's obligation to follow the drawings
options.C: Require the owner to issue the entire procurement documents again
options.D: Raise construction costs, cause delays, or cause faulty work

questions.explanation: An abbreviation that means two different things is exactly the inconsistent terminology that confuses readers. Left uncorrected it can push up costs, slow the schedule, and lead to work being built wrong.

questions.question: In a sample abbreviation legend, the existing condition is conveyed several different ways at once. Counting how many distinct ways one condition is shown is an exercise in:

options.A: Verifying contractor compliance with a tested fire-rated assembly
options.B: Coordinating allowance quantities with the project bid form prices
options.C: Establishing the order of precedence among all the contract documents
options.D: Enforcing consistent terminology and abbreviations across documents

questions.explanation: Tallying the different ways one condition is labeled makes the point about enforcing consistent terminology and abbreviations: using several labels for the same thing confuses the reader, which is the problem consistent terminology prevents.

questions.question: A curb detail labels the insulation only 'RIGID INSULATION,' while Section 07 21 00 lists three rigid types (XPS, polyiso, mineral wool). Based on the intended answer, the type to be installed is:

options.A: Unclear; the terminology must be coordinated
options.B: Polyisocyanurate, because it is foil-faced
options.C: Mineral wool, because it is noncombustible
options.D: Extruded polystyrene, because it is listed first

questions.explanation: A generic 'rigid insulation' note cannot be matched to any one of the three specified types, so it is impossible to tell which is intended. The terminology between the drawing and the specification needs to be coordinated.

questions.question: An engineer wants to add Section 22 00 05 - Firestopping for Plumbing because the architect already prepared 07 84 13 - Penetration Firestopping. The best-practice guidance is to:

options.A: Keep both sections so each discipline controls its own firestopping
options.B: Reference both sections from a Division 01 summary
options.C: Coordinate all firestopping into Division 07 under one section
options.D: Move all firestopping into the plumbing division for that trade

questions.explanation: Creating a second, duplicate firestopping section is not good practice. The plumbing firestopping requirements should be coordinated into the single Division 07 section so the same work is not specified two different ways.

questions.question: CSI's 'say it once and in the right place' principle exists chiefly to prevent which defect that an addendum is especially likely to create?

options.A: An allowance amount omitted from the bid form
options.B: A correction made in one location but missed in the duplicate
options.C: Use of an out-of-date standard agreement form
options.D: A precedence conflict between the drawings and specifications

questions.explanation: Duplicated requirements invite discrepancies because an addendum can fix one copy and overlook the other. Stating each requirement just once, in its proper place, removes the duplicate that an addendum might miss.

questions.question: A specification's owner-furnished article simply lists 'Soap Dispenser, Paper Towel Dispenser, Toilet Paper Dispenser' as owner-provided for the contractor to install. Is this sufficient for the contractor to bid?

options.A: No; the products are not identified well enough to price the install
options.B: Yes; owner-furnished items carry no installation cost to the bidder
options.C: Yes; the accessory schedule already lists the required install method
options.D: No; the only missing detail is the accessory manufacturer brand names

questions.explanation: Just naming the owner-furnished items is not enough to bid. Without identifying the products in enough detail, the contractor cannot reliably price the installation work, even though the owner is supplying the products themselves.

questions.question: Construction documents are nearly complete; the owner has repeatedly failed to provide the contractor's required insurance limits and tells the architect to 'use whatever you usually use.' The architect's BEST action is to:

options.A: Insert the insurance limits the architect used on a similar prior project file
options.B: Omit the owner's insurance limits from the documents entirely until provided
options.C: Request the owner confirm limits with their legal counsel and insurance agent
options.D: Set the limits at the highest amount any of the architect's past projects required

questions.explanation: Insurance limits are the owner's call, informed by the owner's own legal and insurance advisers. Rather than borrowing limits from another project or leaving them out, the architect should ask the owner to confirm the limits with their counsel and insurance agent.

questions.question: An owner's geotechnical report is needed by the A/E, its consultants, and the contractor. This report should be:

options.A: Referenced in Division 00 as Available Project Information
options.B: Issued only on request after the contract is signed
options.C: Attached to the agreement as a numbered contract exhibit
options.D: Bound into Division 01 as a general administrative requirement

questions.explanation: The owner is normally responsible for the geotechnical report, and it is provided to all parties by including or referencing it in Division 00 as available project information.

questions.question: An owner's commissioning agent and security adviser will interact with the contractor during construction. The project specifications should therefore:

options.A: Name those owner's consultants as additional signatory parties to the agreement
options.B: Address the contractor's responsibilities in working with the owner's consultants
options.C: Exclude those owner's consultants because the owner, not the A/E, retained them
options.D: Shift coordination of those owner's consultants entirely onto the prime contractor

questions.explanation: Where the owner's consultants have duties that involve working with the contractor, the specifications should spell out the contractor's responsibilities in that interaction so the relationship is defined.

questions.question: A product representative, upset that proprietary language was edited out of a section, contacts the OWNER directly during bidding to complain. Contacting the owner was:

options.A: Inappropriate, and the A/E of record owns the project specifications
options.B: Appropriate, because the owner ultimately funds the entire project
options.C: Appropriate, since the rep authored the original guide specification
options.D: Inappropriate only when the project is a publicly funded contract

questions.explanation: Going directly to the owner was not appropriate. The specifications are the A/E of record's responsibility, and the A/E may properly edit a guide specification to open the section up to competition.

questions.question: On a CMAR or IPD project where the contractor is engaged early in design, the recommended practice is that the contractor should be:

options.A: Included in the project manual coordinating group
options.B: Given precedence over the A/E in resolving conflicts
options.C: Asked to prepare the procurement requirements
options.D: Limited to reviewing the drawings only

questions.explanation: When a delivery method like CMAR or IPD brings the contractor into the design stage, the contractor should be part of the group coordinating the project manual, since it is contributing while the documents are still being shaped.

questions.question: A curtain wall installer provides framing and glazing calculations and installation details to help develop the documents. This early involvement is identified as a:

options.A: A design-assist role contributing information to the specifications
options.B: A substitution request requiring formal A/E evaluation and approval
options.C: A value-analysis proposal submitted under Section 01 24 00 procedures
options.D: A voluntary alternate offered against the project's base-bid scope

questions.explanation: A subcontractor lending its expertise on one part of the design, such as an installer supplying calculations and installation details, is acting in a design-assist role that helps develop the documents.

questions.question: For multiple-prime work, the recommended practice is to use Section 01 12 00 - Multiple Contract Summary, which (unlike 01 11 00) must further define scope by including owner-furnished material and equipment to be installed and:

options.A: the order of precedence among the installed contract documents
options.B: the allowance amount carried for owner-furnished items in each package
options.C: by which contractor each owner-furnished item is to be installed
options.D: the liquidated-damages rate applied to each installed work package

questions.explanation: On multiple-prime work, Section 01 12 00 has to define scope by listing the owner-furnished material and equipment to be installed and identifying which contractor installs each item. That contractor-by-contractor breakdown is what distinguishes it from the single-contract 01 11 00.

questions.question: Per a coordination matrix, the specifier should coordinate primarily with which team member to verify whether a contractor has been selected and a contract is in place?

options.A: The owner
options.B: The consultant
options.C: The product representative
options.D: The architect/engineer

questions.explanation: Whether a contractor has been selected and a contract signed is something only the owner knows, because the owner holds that contractual relationship. So the specifier confirms it with the owner.

questions.question: A fire-resistance design lists specific sprayed fire-resistive manufacturers; the spec's 'one of the following' list includes a manufacturer that is NOT named in the tested design. Per the intended answer, a base-bid product from that manufacturer is:

options.A: Not acceptable for that assembly, since it is absent from the tested design
options.B: Acceptable only if the contractor offers a five-percent price reduction at bid
options.C: Acceptable, because it appears in the specification's listed manufacturers
options.D: Acceptable if the architect waives the tested-design listing requirement at bid

questions.explanation: Because that manufacturer is not named in the tested fire-resistance design, its product is not acceptable for that indicated assembly, even though the specification's manufacturer list happens to include it. The tested design controls.

questions.question: During construction, a contractor submits a cost-saving substitution with documentation that the product is listed in a DIFFERENT tested assembly. Per the intended answer, the specifier should compare the proposed assembly to the specified tested design and:

options.A: Reject it outright because the manufacturer is not listed in the specified design
options.B: Forward it to the building official for that official's sole determination
options.C: Approve it if appropriate, assisting the architect in the evaluation
options.D: Approve it automatically on the basis of the owner's cost savings

questions.explanation: The specifier should compare the contractor's proposed tested assembly against the one specified and, if it is appropriate, approve it while assisting the architect. The request is neither rejected solely because of the manufacturer list nor approved on cost alone.

questions.question: When mechanical engineers each insert a 'Submittal Procedures' section into their own divisions, the coordination guidance for the Division 01 lead is to:

options.A: permit each division to keep its own submittal procedures
options.B: relocate submittal procedures from Division 01 to the conditions
options.C: fold the unique elements into the common Division 01 section
options.D: delete the engineers' added sections without any discussion

questions.explanation: Duplicate submittal-procedure sections conflict with the common Division 01 section. The reviewer should figure out what unique requirement prompted each separate section and merge those elements into the single Division 01 submittal section.

questions.question: An abatement consultant's Section 02 82 13 directs both the 'Abatement Contractor' and the 'window replacement contractor' to perform parts of the work. Naming a second contractor in this section is:

options.A: appropriate, because it clarifies the specialist interface for the second contractor
options.B: not appropriate, because one section must not assign work to another contractor
options.C: appropriate only when both named contractors sign the very same prime agreement
options.D: not appropriate unless the owner is self-performing the window-replacement work

questions.explanation: A specification section should not hand work to a separate contractor. Directing the window-replacement contractor inside the abatement section is not appropriate; that kind of cross-contractor coordination belongs in Division 01 and the broader contract documents.

questions.question: An abatement spec article directs a 'fine spray mist' applied until the material is 'sufficiently saturated, without causing excess dripping.' This execution language is:

options.A: clear, because the article cites both the OSHA and the NESHAP standards
options.B: clear, because the wetting and spray equipment is specified for the work
options.C: not clear, because it relies on vague, unmeasurable removal terminology
options.D: not clear only if the asbestos-containing material type is omitted here

questions.explanation: Phrases like 'fine spray mist' and 'sufficiently saturated' give the contractor no measurable benchmark to follow, so the procedure is not clear. Execution language for regulated work needs a definite, measurable standard.

questions.question: In an abatement section, one statement directs removal of all asbestos-containing material on the inventory/plans, and another directs removal of non-friable Transite panels with wetting. These two statements are best described as:

options.A: in conflict, because both statements address the same asbestos removal scope
options.B: out of place, because both statements belong in PART 1 — GENERAL instead
options.C: redundant, so the statement covering the Transite panels should be deleted
options.D: complementary, addressing different aspects of the asbestos removal work

questions.explanation: One statement defines the scope of material to be removed while the other gives the method for the non-friable Transite. They cover different aspects of the same job and so are complementary rather than conflicting.

questions.question: A demolition section states hazardous materials shall be removed 'in accordance with Document 00 31 26 - Existing Hazardous Material Information.' This is inappropriate chiefly because Document 00 31 26 is:

options.A: information that the selective-demolition section supersedes as a contract document
options.B: information provided for the bidder and is not itself a contract document
options.C: information given in a Division 01 section that cannot govern Division 02 work
options.D: information tied to an allowance whose abatement scope must be priced apart

questions.explanation: That document is furnished for the bidder's information and is expressly not a contract document. Work cannot be made part of the contract simply by referencing such informational material; abatement scope must be specified in its own enforceable sections.

questions.question: A contract sets liquidated damages at $750 per calendar day. Substantial completion was due April 10 and was achieved April 25, with damages running the day after the deadline through the date achieved. The amount assessed is:
questions.explanation: Counting from April 11 through April 25 inclusive gives 15 days of delay. At $750 per day, 15 × $750 = $11,250. The damages run from the day after the deadline through the date substantial completion was reached.

questions.question: An Invitation to Bidders provides that bids will be received sealed at a stated office and then 'publicly opened and read aloud.' A bidder proposes to email its bid instead. Emailing must be refused mainly because it would defeat the requirement that bids be:

options.A: notarized and sealed by the bidder, then opened privately before the deadline
options.B: received only from the prime bidder in person, at the stated office, never read aloud
options.C: accompanied by a separately sealed alternate price envelope, opened publicly
options.D: received sealed and then opened publicly and read aloud at one stated time

questions.explanation: The Invitation provides for sealed bids that are then opened publicly and read aloud at a single set time. An emailed bid cannot satisfy that sealed-and-publicly-opened process, so it must be refused.

questions.question: An Invitation to Bidders says printed documents may be purchased from one print shop, and may also be reviewed at three other named locations. In addition to the print shop, how many places are listed where documents may be obtained or reviewed?

options.A: One additional location besides the print shop
options.B: Four additional locations besides the print shop site
options.C: Two additional locations besides the print shop
options.D: Three additional locations besides the print shop

questions.explanation: Beyond the print shop, three more locations are named where the documents can be reviewed, giving three additional places.

questions.question: The Invitation states a Performance Bond and a Payment Bond will be required in the amount of 100% of the Contract Price. If the contract price is $4 million, the bond amount required is:

options.A: $4 million
options.B: $6 million
options.C: None
options.D: $8 million

questions.explanation: When the bonds are required at 100 percent of the contract price, a $4 million contract requires bonds of $4 million.

questions.question: An open pre-bid meeting states 'Prime Bidders interested in submitting a bid are required to attend.' A tile SUBcontractor interested in bidding to the primes asks if attendance is mandatory. The tile subcontractor is:

options.A: required to attend, the same as the prime bidders and all interested bidders
options.B: required to attend only when no prime bidder will represent the tile scope
options.C: not required to attend, because the requirement names only the prime bidders
options.D: not required to attend only when the pre-bid meeting of bidders is virtual

questions.explanation: The mandatory-attendance language is directed at prime bidders. A tile subcontractor is not a prime bidder, so it is not required to attend.

questions.question: Section 01 21 00 - Allowances should identify both items covered by an allowance and cost items NOT covered. The purpose of this second list is so that, for example, delivery, installation, overhead, and profit are:

options.A: deducted from the cash allowance at closeout
options.B: included in the contract sum rather than the allowance
options.C: priced as separate unit prices on the bid form
options.D: carried as a contingency in the conditions of the contract

questions.explanation: Listing the costs an allowance does not cover (delivery, handling, installation, overhead, profit, and the like) makes clear that those costs belong in the contract sum, not in the allowance amount.

questions.question: A design firm is drafting a project management procedure and wants its stated purpose for the coordination process to match industry guidance. Which statement should it adopt?

options.A: To establish which contract document governs when requirements conflict
options.B: To assign each consultant sole responsibility for its discipline's documents
options.C: To manage dependencies between tasks and parties, adding value to delivery
options.D: To limit which stakeholders may supply information to the design team

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states the coordination process exists to add value to project delivery and improve efficiency by dealing with dependencies between project tasks and parties, summarized as "managing dependencies between activities." Deciding which document governs is a precedence question that industry guidance handles separately and discourages. Coordination integrates the parties rather than isolating each discipline or restricting who may supply information.

questions.question: After a claim arises from inconsistencies between the drawings and the project manual, the A/E firm's principal asks where ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents should have rested. It should have rested with:

options.A: the specifier, whether in-house or independent, who prepared the project manual
options.B: the A/E's project manager, who may delegate coordination to a team member
options.C: the owner's project manager, who reviews the documents before issue
options.D: the general contractor, who must report discrepancies it discovers

questions.explanation: Industry guidance places ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents with the A/E's project manager, who may assign the coordination task to another design team member. The specifier works with the A/E on the drawings and project manual but is not named as the party ultimately responsible. The owner's project manager and the contractor are outside the design team, and coordination of the documents is an A/E function.

questions.question: To limit rework as the design changes, an A/E's project manager asks when the specifier should start preparing the project manual. What is the recommended approach?

options.A: Start as design begins, and keep it coordinated continuously as the design develops
options.B: Start once the owner approves the design development drawings and product selections
options.C: Start when the drawings are substantially complete, then hold a coordination review
options.D: Start midway through construction documents, once most product selections are settled

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says project manual preparation should proceed concurrently with design, and coordination should be a continuous process from the beginning of the project; a preliminary project description or outline specifications serve as a checklist when design starts. Each distractor delays the project manual to a later milestone (design development approval, mid-construction documents, or near-complete drawings), treating coordination as a late check rather than a continuous process.

questions.question: The owner's counsel asks the specifier to add a clause stating that the specifications govern over the drawings whenever the two conflict. How should the specifier respond?

options.A: Add the clause to Division 01 so that it governs throughout construction
options.B: Add an order-of-precedence listing to the supplementary conditions
options.C: Have the conditions state that the more stringent requirement governs
options.D: Have the conditions state that the A/E makes a documented interpretation

questions.explanation: Industry guidance does not recommend precedence statements in the project manual because drawings and specifications are complementary. The conditions of the contract should only state that the A/E makes a documented interpretation when the two conflict. A precedence listing may be prepared, if necessary, for bidding purposes only, so placing one in the supplementary conditions, where it would govern the contract, is not appropriate. A Division 01 clause or a "more stringent governs" rule is still a precedence rule that industry guidance does not endorse.

questions.question: An independent specifier receives product selections from several designers on the prime A/E's team, and some selections contradict each other. Which communication method best addresses the problem?

options.A: Have product representatives send product data directly to the specifier for each section
options.B: Have all product information reach the specifier only from designated individuals
options.C: Have each designer keep sending selections directly to the specifier, who reconciles them
options.D: Have the specifier select products and send the selections to the designers for approval

questions.explanation: Industry guidance advises setting up a protocol so that the specifier receives product information only from one or more designated people, typically the project manager and/or the project A/E. Letting product representatives send data, or continuing to take selections from each designer, still leaves the specifier with several sources that may conflict. Having the specifier pick products for the designers to approve inverts the process industry guidance describes, where the design team makes product decisions and the specifier verifies their status.

questions.question: A prime A/E adopts a cloud-based collaboration tool that lets the design team access the specifications while they are being developed. What is the main benefit to the specifier?

options.A: Automatic reconciliation of terminology between the drawings and the specifications
options.B: Direct editing of sections by designers, reducing the specifier's drafting workload
options.C: Timely, accurate feedback that reduces section-by-section specification review meetings
options.D: Documented design team approval of each section before the project manual is issued

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says cloud-based tools that let the design team access the specifications during development give the specifier timely and accurate feedback, which minimizes time-consuming section-by-section review meetings. Coordinating terminology between drawings and specifications remains part of the specifier's regular reviews with the design team; the tool does not do it automatically. Industry guidance describes the design team accessing the specifications, not editing them in the specifier's place, and does not present the tool as a formal approval step.

questions.question: A prime A/E retains mechanical and electrical consultants to write their own sections. When should the prime A/E request the consultants' input for Division 01 sections?

options.A: When it gives them the project, contract, and Division 01 information, before they write
options.B: After the consultants submit first drafts, so Division 01 can be reconciled with them
options.C: At the construction documents review, when the A/E checks for duplications and omissions
options.D: During bidding, when bidders' questions reveal gaps between the disciplines' requirements

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says information on the project type, contract, specification formats, general conditions, and especially Division 01 should go to consultants before they prepare any sections. Input from them for Division 01 should be requested at the same time. Waiting for drafts, a CD review, or bidding questions invites the separate, conflicting discipline requirements this early exchange is meant to prevent.

questions.question: An electrical consultant's drawings include general notes on submittal procedures, warranties, and payment terms for the electrical work. What should the prime A/E direct?

options.A: Keep the notes on the drawings, since the consultant seals its own documents
options.B: Move the notes into a separate general requirements section for electrical work
options.C: Keep the notes, and add a statement that the drawings take precedence for electrical work
options.D: Move the requirements into Division 01 and the other appropriate contract documents

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says consultants must resist putting general notes on administrative matters and terms and conditions on their drawings; those belong in Division 01 and other contract documents. That keeps consultants from writing separate general requirements for their disciplines, which raises the risk of conflicts. Sealing requirements explain why consultants may write their own sections, not why administrative notes stay on drawings. A precedence statement does not cure misplaced requirements.

questions.question: Under AIA Document A201, when are addenda considered instruments of change?

options.A: Only during the procurement phase
options.B: Before execution of the agreement
options.C: After execution of the agreement
options.D: Before receipt of bids only

questions.explanation: A201 treats an addendum as something issued any time before the agreement is signed, which leaves room to negotiate up to that point. This is broader than the EJCDC approach, which cuts off addenda at bid opening.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, addenda must be issued by what point?

options.A: Before the time of substantial completion
options.B: Before receipt of bids
options.C: Before execution of the agreement
options.D: Before the pre-construction meeting

questions.explanation: EJCDC, geared toward public works, treats an addendum as a pre-bid instrument: it must go out before bids are received. That reflects the public-procurement rule against altering the documents once bidding has closed but the contract is not yet signed.

questions.question: Which document modifies the fixed, standardized provisions of AIA A201 for a specific project?

options.A: The bid form and bid schedule
options.B: The owner-contractor agreement
options.C: Supplementary conditions
options.D: Division 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: Supplementary conditions are the device for tailoring the standardized language of the general conditions to a particular project or jurisdiction, and they govern over the general conditions where the two differ.

questions.question: How many days before receipt of bids does AIA A701 require bidder questions to be submitted?

options.A: At least 14 days
options.B: At least 10 days
options.C: At least 4 days
options.D: At least 7 days

questions.explanation: AIA's Instructions to Bidders sets a minimum of seven days before bids are received for bidder questions to come in. The comparable EJCDC recommendation is a longer window of about ten days.

questions.question: Division 01 sections should be written in language broad enough to apply to the work of which divisions?

options.A: Divisions 01 through 33 (the original MasterFormat groups)
options.B: Only the technical divisions that are actually used on the project
options.C: Divisions 02 through 49 (all technical specification divisions)
options.D: Divisions 00 through 14 (procurement through conveying systems)

questions.explanation: Because Division 01 carries the general execution requirements for the whole project, its language must be broad enough to reach every technical section, that is, all of Divisions 02 through 49, so the same requirements need not be repeated.

questions.question: Which Division 01 section aligns with PART 2—PRODUCTS of SectionFormat?

options.A: Administrative Requirements
options.B: Product Requirements
options.C: Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.D: Quality Control (Field)

questions.explanation: SectionFormat's PART 2 deals with products, so the Division 01 groups that parallel it concern product and performance requirements and source-based quality control. Administrative and quality-assurance content instead lines up with PART 1—GENERAL.

questions.question: In the three-tier hierarchy of requirements, which level provides broadest provisions?

options.A: Division 01—General Requirements
options.B: General Conditions of the contract
options.C: Supplementary Conditions
options.D: PART 1—GENERAL of individual sections

questions.explanation: The general conditions speak in the broadest terms; Division 01 then refines those provisions for the project; and PART 1—GENERAL of each technical section gets very specific to the work of that section. Breadth decreases as you move down the tiers.

questions.question: Where should provisions applicable only during procurement (e.g., bid security) be stated?

options.A: Supplementary conditions
options.B: Procurement requirements
options.C: The agreement
options.D: Division 01 sections

questions.explanation: Anything that matters only while bidding is underway, such as how to obtain documents, bid security, or the bid opening date, belongs in the procurement requirements rather than in Division 01, which governs the construction phase.

questions.question: Each specification section affected by an alternate should:

options.A: Restate the full alternate text to avoid cross-refs
options.B: Be omitted from the base bid until 1 is accepted
options.C: Carry its own independent alternate number
options.D: Cross-reference Section 01 23 00 Alternates

questions.explanation: Alternates are described once in the alternates section, and each affected technical section simply cross-references that section rather than restating the alternate. Not every alternate is product-based, so this keeps the documents consistent.

questions.question: When the installed quantity of an item carried as a quantity allowance differs from the estimate in Section 01 21 19, the difference is reconciled by:

options.A: Carrying the variance to closeout as a punch-list credit item
options.B: Absorbing the variance entirely within the contractor's overhead and profit
options.C: A change order adjusting the contract sum for the measured over/under-run
options.D: Re-bidding the affected scope as a deduct alternate to the contract sum

questions.explanation: A quantity allowance fixes an estimated quantity of installed work. When the measured quantity differs, the contract sum is adjusted by change order at the established rate for the over-run or under-run, much like unit-price reconciliation.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, after receiving a substitution request the architect will request any additional information or documentation needed for evaluation within:

options.A: 48 hours of receipt of the request
options.B: 15 days of receipt of the request
options.C: 30 days of receipt of the request
options.D: 7 days of receipt of the request

questions.explanation: A common substitution procedure gives the architect seven days from receipt of the request to ask for any further information needed to evaluate it. The fifteen-day figure is instead the window for notifying the contractor whether the substitution is accepted or rejected.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, the architect will notify the contractor of the decision to accept or reject a proposed substitution within:

options.A: 15 days of receipt of the request
options.B: 10 days of receipt of the request
options.C: 7 days of receipt of the request
options.D: 20 days of receipt of the request

questions.explanation: A representative substitution procedure has the architect notify the contractor of acceptance or rejection within fifteen days of receiving the request. The seven-day period applies only to asking for additional information, not to the decision.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, a Substitution for Cause must be submitted immediately on discovery of the need for change, but no later than:

options.A: 15 days after the related submittal package is logged
options.B: 20 days prior to the time required for preparation and review of related submittals
options.C: 60 days after the Notice to Proceed
options.D: 7 days before the related submittal is logged, reviewed, and returned by the architect

questions.explanation: A substitution for cause is raised as soon as the need is discovered and, in any event, far enough ahead, on the order of twenty days, that it does not interfere with preparation and review of the related submittals. The sixty-day-after-notice-to-proceed limit applies to convenience requests.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, the architect will consider a Substitution for Convenience only if the request is received:

options.A: At any time during construction if it benefits the owner
options.B: Within 20 days prior to preparation of related submittals
options.C: Within 7 days of the Notice to Proceed
options.D: Within 60 days after the Notice to Proceed

questions.explanation: A convenience substitution, one offered for advantage rather than necessity, is considered only when the request comes in within sixty days after the notice to proceed. The twenty-day rule governs substitutions for cause instead.

questions.question: A contractor's substitution request that is incomplete or does not comply with Section 01 25 00 will typically be:

options.A: Forwarded to the owner for a discretionary waiver
options.B: Logged as approved-as-noted pending a resubmittal
options.C: Held by the architect until the 15-day clock expires, then approved by default
options.D: Returned without action, except to record noncompliance

questions.explanation: A substitution request that is incomplete or fails to follow the section's requirements is returned without action, except to note the noncompliance. There is no approval by default if the architect simply lets time pass.

questions.question: During the procurement (bidding/negotiating) phase, the standardized CSI substitution request form is:

options.A: AIA Document G701, the change order form
options.B: CSI Form 1.5C, the pre-award substitution request
options.C: CSI Form 13.1A, the post-award substitution request
options.D: CSI Form 13.2A, the request for information

questions.explanation: CSI provides a substitution request form for use during the bidding and negotiating phase, Form 1.5C. A different CSI form, 13.1A, is used after that phase once the project is under construction.

questions.question: A construction-phase substitution request on a typical Section 01 25 00 project should use:

options.A: CSI Form 1.5C, the bidding-phase substitution request
options.B: CSI Form 13.2A, the request for information
options.C: AIA Document G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions
options.D: CSI Form 13.1A, the post-bid substitution request

questions.explanation: Once construction is under way, substitution requests use the post-bid CSI form, 13.1A. Form 1.5C is the bidding-phase substitution form, and 13.2A is the RFI form.

questions.question: Including 'Basic Requirements' or 'Special Provisions' sections within individual technical divisions is:

options.A: Preferred when Division 01 is incomplete, since it may fill procedural gaps
options.B: Required by MasterFormat whenever a division contains more than one section
options.C: Not recommended, because such sections can create conflicts with Division 01
options.D: Mandatory on multiple-prime projects to assign division-specific responsibilities

questions.explanation: Tucking general-purpose 'basic requirements' or 'special provisions' sections into individual technical divisions is discouraged, since the procedural language there can collide with what Division 01 already states.

questions.question: A contractor proposes a tile by a different manufacturer instead of the specified product, citing only a cost saving and no project condition. This is a:

options.A: Comparable product submittal, requiring no substitution review
options.B: Minor change in the work, by architect's supplemental instructions
options.C: Substitution for Cause, because a different product is involved here
options.D: Substitution for Convenience, offering advantage but not required

questions.explanation: A change that the project does not require but that the contractor offers for an advantage like cost is a substitution for convenience, which is considered only if requested within the sixty-day window after the notice to proceed.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the owner and contractor have not agreed on the cost and time impact of a directed change, but the work must proceed now. The proper instrument is the:

options.A: Construction change directive (AIA G714)
options.B: Architect's supplemental instructions (AIA G710)
options.C: Change order (AIA G701)
options.D: Minor change in the work

questions.explanation: A construction change directive is the instrument for ordering a change to begin before the parties have agreed on its effect on contract sum or time. A change order requires that prior agreement, and a minor change carries no cost or time impact at all.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, a construction change directive is prepared by the architect and signed by:

options.A: The owner, architect, and contractor
options.B: The owner and contractor only
options.C: The owner and architect
options.D: The architect only

questions.explanation: Because a construction change directive orders work before the contractor has agreed to the adjustment, it is prepared by the architect and signed by the owner and architect. A change order, by contrast, carries all three signatures.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, which document requires the signatures of the owner, contractor, AND architect?

options.A: AIA G704 Certificate of Substantial Completion
options.B: AIA G701 Change Order
options.C: AIA G714 Construction Change Directive
options.D: AIA G710 Architect's Supplemental Instructions

questions.explanation: The change order is prepared by the architect and signed by the owner, contractor, and architect, recording their agreement on the change and on the related adjustments to sum and time.

questions.question: An architect directs the contractor to make a clarifying change that involves no adjustment to contract sum or time. Under AIA A201, the architect may issue this as a minor change because:

options.A: It must be priced by the contractor before it becomes binding
options.B: The owner's countersignature converts it into a change order
options.C: It does not require the owner's signature and is within the architect's authority
options.D: The contractor may decline to perform it until a priced change order has been negotiated

questions.explanation: A201 gives the architect authority to order minor changes that are consistent with the documents' intent and affect neither sum nor time. Such a change, issued in writing, is binding without the owner's signature.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, the instrument that orders a change before agreement on price or time, signed only by the owner, is the:

options.A: Field order issued with no standard form
options.B: Work change directive, EJCDC C-940 form
options.C: Written amendment to the agreement terms
options.D: Change order, the EJCDC C-941 form

questions.explanation: In the EJCDC system the work change directive is signed by the owner and directs additions, deletions, or revisions before the effect on price or time is settled. The EJCDC change order, by contrast, is signed by the engineer, owner, and contractor.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the contract sum or contract time can be adjusted ONLY by:

options.A: A directive in the meeting minutes acknowledged by the contractor
options.B: A written change order
options.C: A field order issued by the architect
options.D: Architect's supplemental instructions

questions.explanation: Under A201 the only instrument that actually adjusts the contract sum or time is a written change order. A construction change directive can start the work before agreement, but the adjustment itself is later recorded by change order.

questions.question: The distinguishing factor that separates a purchasing (goods) contract from a construction contract is that the goods contractor:

options.A: Is involved in little or no on-site activity such as construction or installation
options.B: Always provides a performance bond, while the construction contractor does not
options.C: Is selected by negotiation, while the construction contractor is competitively bid
options.D: Is governed by AIA A201 rather than by the Uniform Commercial Code

questions.explanation: What sets a goods contract apart is that the supplier performs little or no work at the site. If the supplier must take part in installation, the arrangement becomes a furnish-and-install subcontract rather than a pure purchasing contract.

questions.question: Products the owner buys and supplies for the contractor to install are most appropriately specified in:

options.A: Section 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products
options.B: Section 01 26 00—Contract Modification Procedures
options.C: Section 01 73 00—Execution
options.D: Section 01 23 00—Alternates

questions.explanation: When the owner provides products for the contractor to install, the owner-furnished products section is used to set the administrative rules, covering the items' essential characteristics, coordination, scheduling, and receiving.

questions.question: Under UCC Article 2, a written contract for the sale of goods is enforceable if it provides evidence of a sale, is signed by the party to be charged, and:

options.A: Includes an express warranty of fitness
options.B: States a delivery date certain
options.C: Specifies a quantity
options.D: Recites the agreed unit price

questions.explanation: For a goods contract to satisfy the UCC writing requirement it must evidence a sale, bear the signature of the party to be held to it, and state a quantity. The UCC can fill in a missing price or delivery term, but quantity generally has to be agreed.

questions.question: Under the UCC, contracts for the sale of goods must be in writing to be enforceable when the goods cost more than:
questions.explanation: The UCC's statute of frauds for goods requires a writing once the sale exceeds $500. The $2,000 figure is the trigger for the federal Davis-Bacon prevailing-wage rule, a different matter entirely.

questions.question: In the EJCDC procurement documents, the party that furnishes the goods is referred to as the Seller and the owner is referred to as the:

options.A: Principal
options.B: Constructor
options.C: Obligee
options.D: Buyer

questions.explanation: EJCDC procurement documents use sale terminology: the supplier of the goods is the Seller and the owner is the Buyer. Principal and obligee are bond terms, not purchasing terms.

questions.question: Which EJCDC procurement document is the Agreement Between Buyer and Seller for Procurement?

options.A: EJCDC P-700
options.B: EJCDC P-520
options.C: EJCDC P-200
options.D: EJCDC P-400

questions.explanation: Among the core EJCDC procurement documents, the agreement between buyer and seller is P-520. The others in the set are the instructions to bidders, the general conditions, and the bid form.

questions.question: The EJCDC procurement (purchasing) documents are NOT intended for use where:

options.A: The goods are competitively bid using a standard goods bid form
options.B: The manufacturer or supplier must participate in on-site installation
options.C: Multiple deliveries of the same engineered item are anticipated
options.D: The owner purchases engineered materials directly from the goods provider

questions.explanation: The purchasing documents are not meant for situations where the supplier must take part in installation. That looks more like a construction contract, so construction forms, or purchasing documents modified for the purpose, should be used instead.

questions.question: The AIA standard form used for purchasing goods, which references the UCC, is:

options.A: AIA A101, the standard stipulated-sum agreement between owner and construction contractor
options.B: AIA A152 Purchase Order, with its companion A152 Exhibit A Terms and Conditions
options.C: AIA A312 Performance and Payment Bond
options.D: AIA A701 Instructions to Bidders

questions.explanation: The AIA purchase order form (A152, with its Exhibit A terms and conditions) is used for buying goods and references the UCC, though it does not declare that its own terms prevail in a conflict.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 26 13, how soon after discovering the need for clarification must the contractor prepare and submit an RFI?

options.A: Within 48 hours of discovery
options.B: Within 7 days of discovery of the need for additional information
options.C: Within 5 days of discovery
options.D: Immediately on discovery of the need for additional information

questions.explanation: A representative RFI procedure requires the contractor to prepare and submit the RFI immediately upon discovering the need for additional information, clarification, or interpretation, using the specified form.

questions.question: Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions is primarily intended to address:

options.A: Schedule of values and payment-application requirements
options.B: Requirements for independent testing laboratories
options.C: Limitations on the contractor's use of the premises
options.D: Construction progress photographs and documentation

questions.explanation: The work restrictions section places limits on how the contractor may use the site, which matters most when the building remains occupied during the work. Owner protection, access, and similar topics belong to other Division 01 sections.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 26 13, the architect is allowed how long to respond to each RFI?

options.A: 3 days
options.B: 14 days
options.C: 7 days
options.D: 5 days

questions.explanation: A common RFI procedure allows the architect five days to respond to each RFI, and an RFI received late in the day is typically treated as received the next working day.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 26 13, when the architect requests further information needed to answer an RFI, the architect's response period:

options.A: Is automatically forfeited if the contractor delays the data
options.B: Is suspended only with the owner's prior written consent
options.C: Begins when the architect receives the requested information
options.D: Keeps running from the date the original RFI was submitted

questions.explanation: If answering an RFI requires the architect to ask for more information, the response period starts over and runs from the time the architect actually receives that additional information.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 26 13, which RFI would the architect return WITHOUT action?

options.A: A request for approval of a proposed substitution
options.B: A request to interpret an ambiguity between two detail callouts
options.C: A request to clarify a dimension missing from the drawings
options.D: A request to confirm which of two referenced standards governs

questions.explanation: RFIs seeking approval of a substitution or a submittal, approval of means and methods, coordination already shown in the documents, a change in time or sum, or an interpretation of the architect's submittal actions, as well as those that are incomplete or inaccurate, are returned without action. Genuine requests for interpretation, such as clarifying a missing dimension, are answered.

questions.question: A contractor submits an RFI asking the architect to approve a substitution. The proper outcome is that the request is:

options.A: Granted if the substitution window has not yet closed
options.B: Answered as an ordinary interpretation, since an RFI is a request that seeks information
options.C: Returned without action, because RFIs cannot be used for substitution approvals
options.D: Forwarded to the owner for a discretionary decision

questions.explanation: A request to approve a substitution is returned without action because the RFI process is not the proper vehicle for it. The contractor must use the substitution procedure in Section 01 25 00 instead.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 26 13, an RFI submitted to the architect by a subcontractor (an entity controlled by the contractor) will be:

options.A: Logged and answered in parallel with the prime contractor's own request-for-information submittals
options.B: Accepted only if the prime contractor countersigns it
options.C: Returned without response, because such RFIs must route through the contractor
options.D: Answered if it concerns shop-drawing coordination

questions.explanation: An RFI from a subcontractor or other entity controlled by the contractor is returned without a response. RFIs have to flow through the prime contractor to keep the contractual line of communication intact.

questions.question: The standardized CSI form used for a request for information is:

options.A: AIA Document G716
options.B: CSI Form 1.5C
options.C: CSI Form 13.1A
options.D: CSI Form 13.2A

questions.explanation: CSI's standard RFI form is Form 13.2A. The 1.5C and 13.1A forms are CSI's substitution request forms, used in the bidding phase and after award respectively.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, where the contract documents require the contractor to design a portion of the work (delegated design), the contractor:

options.A: Furnishes them through a licensed design professional who seals the submittals
options.B: Is relieved of responsibility because the architect retains design liability
options.C: May proceed only after the architect re-stamps and adopts the design as its own
options.D: Must first obtain the owner's written waiver of the licensing requirement

questions.explanation: A201 does not require the contractor to perform design services unless the documents call for it. Where they do, the contractor must use a properly licensed design professional who signs and seals the related calculations, drawings, and submittals, on which the owner and architect are entitled to rely.
questions.source: delegated design under the general conditions

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the architect reviews and approves the contractor's shop drawings, product data, and samples:

options.A: To substantiate the contractor's means, methods, and installation procedures
options.B: To assume responsibility for fabrication and field coordination
options.C: Only for the limited purpose of checking conformance with the design concept and information given
options.D: To verify the accuracy and completeness of all dimensions, quantities, and installation details shown

questions.explanation: The architect's submittal review under A201 has one narrow aim: to confirm conformance with the information given and the design concept. It is not a check of dimensions or quantities and does not substantiate the contractor's means, methods, or installation.
questions.source: submittal review under the general conditions

questions.question: In the three-party surety bond relationship, the contractor is the principal, the owner is the obligee, and the surety:

options.A: Indemnifies the contractor against the owner's default
options.B: Holds primary, not secondary, liability for the work
options.C: Pays the A/E's professional liability claims
options.D: Guarantees the contractor's obligations to the owner

questions.explanation: In a surety bond the contractor is the principal and the owner is the obligee, and the surety backs the principal's obligations to the obligee. The surety's liability is secondary, coming into play only when the principal defaults.

questions.question: An owner requires a 100% performance bond on a contract with a contract price of $4,000,000. The penal sum of the performance bond is:
questions.explanation: A 100 percent performance bond has a penal sum equal to the full contract price. For a $4,000,000 contract that penal sum is $4,000,000, which is the most the surety guarantees toward completing the work if the contractor defaults.

questions.question: Which bond guarantees that subcontractors, material suppliers, and others furnishing labor and material will be paid, protecting the owner against mechanic's liens?

options.A: Payment bond
options.B: Maintenance bond
options.C: Bid bond
options.D: Performance bond

questions.explanation: The labor and materials payment bond assures that subcontractors and suppliers are paid, which shields the owner from mechanic's liens. The performance bond instead guarantees that the work itself is completed.

questions.question: The AIA bond form that combines the performance bond and the labor-and-materials payment bond in a single document is:

options.A: EJCDC C-610, the Performance Bond form
options.B: EJCDC C-615, the Payment Bond
options.C: AIA A312, Performance and Payment Bond
options.D: AIA A310, the Bid Bond form

questions.explanation: AIA combines the performance bond and the payment bond in one document, A312. The EJCDC and ConsensusDocs systems, by contrast, provide a separate form for each bond.

questions.question: Which insurance provides no-fault coverage for an employee injured on the job and is statutorily required in most jurisdictions?

options.A: Workers' compensation
options.B: Builder's risk property insurance
options.C: Professional liability (errors and omissions)
options.D: Commercial general liability

questions.explanation: Workers' compensation is the no-fault coverage for on-the-job employee injuries and is required by statute in most jurisdictions. It is separate from general liability, builder's risk, and professional liability coverage.

questions.question: A specifier is placing the team's value-analysis (value-engineering) requirements. Without relying on the section title, which Division 01 section NUMBER is correct?
questions.explanation: Value Analysis is Section 01 24 00. The 01 2x family: 01 21 00 Allowances, 01 22 00 Unit Prices, 01 23 00 Alternates, 01 24 00 Value Analysis, 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures, 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures.

questions.question: When multiple-prime contracts are used, which Division 01 section is most likely required instead of (or in addition to) Section 01 11 00?

options.A: Section 01 12 00—Multiple Contract Summary
options.B: Section 01 35 00—Special Procedures
options.C: Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices
options.D: Section 01 79 00—Demonstration and Training

questions.explanation: When the work is split among several contracts, as with multiple-prime arrangements, construction management, or some design-build setups, the multiple contract summary section is used to describe how those separate contracts fit together.

questions.question: Performance-type green requirements where means and methods are left to the contractor would best appear in:

options.A: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals and design records
options.B: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures for design data
options.C: Section 01 81 13—Sustainable Design Requirements
options.D: Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices for sustainable products

questions.explanation: Where a sustainability target is written as a performance outcome and the contractor is free to decide how to reach it, the right home for that requirement is the sustainable design section, 01 81 13. The other listed sections handle closeout records, submittal logistics, or pricing rather than green performance goals.

questions.question: Under AIA A201 and ConsensusDocs 200, what does the cash allowance typically cover?

options.A: All labor, materials, overhead, and the contractor's profit
options.B: Materials and equipment delivered to site, including taxes
options.C: Sitework, demolition, and related earthwork operations only
options.D: Only the contractor's overhead and profit on the item

questions.explanation: Under these standard documents the cash allowance is confined to the materials and equipment delivered to the site, taxes included. The associated labor, handling, installation, overhead, and profit are carried separately within the contract sum.

questions.question: Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices must clearly define which of the following?

options.A: The contractor's allowable overhead-and-profit mark-up on unit-price work
options.B: Who is responsible for measuring the actual unit-price quantities
options.C: The minimum insurance limits the contractor must carry for unit-price work
options.D: The total contract sum to be carried for all unit-price line items combined

questions.explanation: The unit prices section has to make clear who measures the quantities actually placed. If that responsibility falls to the owner or its representative, the section also needs to spell out how that measurement is administered and coordinated.

questions.question: Section 01 29 00 specifies requirements for the contractor's submittal of:

options.A: The schedule of values and payment applications
options.B: Shop drawings, product data, and physical samples
options.C: Closeout submittals, warranties, and required bonds
options.D: Substitution requests and product-option proposals

questions.explanation: The payment procedures section governs how the contractor submits its schedule of values and its applications for payment, including the forms to use, the number of copies, and the timing.

questions.question: Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures should address substitutions during which time frame(s)?

options.A: Only during the procurement (bidding) stage, before the contract is awarded
options.B: Only after contract award, since procurement substitutions go through addenda
options.C: Only after substantial completion, as part of closeout and warranty resolution
options.D: Both procurement and after contract award, where each phase allows them

questions.explanation: A single substitution section can carry the rules for both the bidding stage and the post-award stage when substitutions are permitted in each. The procurement documents then simply point to that section rather than repeating the procedure.

questions.question: Section 01 25 00 should also include procedures for substitution of:

options.A: A specified installer
options.B: The surety company
options.C: The owner's representative
options.D: The architect/engineer of record

questions.explanation: Substitutions are not limited to products. The section should also spell out how a request to use an installer other than the one specified is to be handled.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the substitution review process under Section 01 25 00?

options.A: To determine whether a proposed product is equivalent to the specified product
options.B: To document the basis for an automatic extension of the contract time
options.C: To establish the unit price adjustment when quantities differ from estimates
options.D: To transfer responsibility for product selection from the A/E to the contractor

questions.explanation: The substitution section sets out the ground rules for evaluating a contractor's proposed alternative, the central question being whether the offered product is genuinely equivalent to what was specified. It does not shift selection responsibility or adjust time or unit prices.

questions.question: Which instrument is commonly used to accept substitutions after the owner-contractor agreement is executed?

options.A: Bid bond furnished with the bidder's proposal
options.B: Schedule of values submitted with the application
options.C: Addendum issued before the agreement is signed
options.D: Change order, the ConsensusDocs 202 form

questions.explanation: Once the agreement is signed, changes to the work, including accepting a substitution, are formalized through a change order, which also records any adjustment to price and time. An addendum can no longer be used at that point because it is a pre-signing instrument.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, how are shop drawings, product data, and samples best characterized?

options.A: Procurement requirements that become enforceable upon execution of the owner-contractor agreement
options.B: Contract documents that, once reviewed, bind the owner to the means and methods shown
options.C: Contract documents only for the portions of the work that are delegated-design submittals
options.D: Not contract documents; they show how the contractor proposes to meet the design intent

questions.explanation: A201 treats these submittals as something other than contract documents. They exist to show the way the contractor intends to satisfy the design intent, so reviewing them does not transfer responsibility for the design to the reviewer or make the submittals part of the contract.

questions.question: By submitting shop drawings under AIA A201, the contractor represents to the owner and architect that it has:

options.A: Waived its right to claim additional contract time arising from the submittal
options.B: Obtained pre-approval of any product substitutions contained in the submittal
options.C: Reviewed them, verified field measurements, and coordinated them with the work
options.D: Transferred responsibility for the design's adequacy to the architect of record

questions.explanation: Submitting a shop drawing under A201 is itself a representation by the contractor that it has reviewed and approved the submittal, confirmed materials and field dimensions, and coordinated the information with the contract documents.

questions.question: Which Division 01 section establishes general submittal procedures?

options.A: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals procedures
options.B: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.C: Section 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination
options.D: Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements and procedures

questions.explanation: The general rules for submittals, including the submittal schedule, shop drawings, product data, samples, sustainable-design reporting, formatting, and required copies, are set in Section 01 33 00.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the architect's review of submittals is for the limited purpose of:

options.A: Approving the contractor's means, methods, sequences, and safety precautions
options.B: Determining the accuracy and completeness of all dimensions and quantities shown
options.C: Substantiating the contractor's installation and equipment-performance instructions
options.D: Checking conformance with information given and the design concept

questions.explanation: A201 narrows the architect's submittal review to one thing: confirming that what is submitted lines up with the information furnished and with the overall design concept in the contract documents. It is not a check of dimensions, quantities, means, or methods.
questions.source: submittal review under the general conditions

questions.question: Section 01 33 00 should specify minimum review times to cover at least how many submittal cycles?

options.A: Unlimited resubmittals over the project duration
options.B: Three full resubmittal cycles after the first
options.C: At least the first submittal and one resubmittal
options.D: Only the first submittal, with no resubmittals

questions.explanation: Because submittal turnaround is important to the procurement process, the submittal section should give the A/E a stated minimum review period that covers at least the initial submittal plus one resubmittal.

questions.question: Which Division 01 section addresses BOTH contract-modification procedures and the RFI clarification process?

options.A: Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation
options.B: Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices and pricing procedures
options.C: Section 01 26 00—Contract Modification Procedures
options.D: Section 01 75 00—Starting and Adjusting procedures

questions.explanation: The contract modification section is where the documents set up a way for either party to ask for a clarification through an RFI and for the A/E to answer it without altering the contract sum or time. The other sections cover documentation, pricing, or startup.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the contractor is generally not obligated to furnish professional design services unless:

options.A: The contract documents specifically call for such professional services
options.B: The architect requests the services in writing after reviewing submittals
options.C: The delegated portion exceeds a stated dollar threshold in the agreement
options.D: The contractor voluntarily retains a design professional for those services

questions.explanation: A201 does not make the contractor responsible for services amounting to the practice of architecture or engineering. That obligation arises only where the contract documents expressly require such design services for some portion of the work.
questions.source: delegated design under the general conditions

questions.question: Under delegated design in AIA A201, the owner and architect are entitled to:

options.A: Receive a royalty or fee share from the delegated design professional's services
options.B: Independently redesign the delegated portion and back-charge the contractor for it
options.C: Reject every submittal originating from the delegated design professional without cause
options.D: Rely on the adequacy and completeness of the delegated professional's certifications

questions.explanation: When the documents call for the contractor to furnish professional design services and supply the related certifications, A201 lets the owner and architect treat those services and certifications as reliable, complete, and accurate rather than re-checking them.
questions.source: delegated design under the general conditions

questions.question: Under AIA A201, a Construction Change Directive (G714) is used when:

options.A: The contract has been terminated and the work is being closed out by the surety
options.B: The owner and contractor have not agreed on the proposed change in contract sum or time
options.C: Only a minor change consistent with the documents and without cost/time impact is needed
options.D: The owner, contractor, and architect have already agreed on all terms of the change

questions.explanation: The construction change directive is the tool for moving a change forward when the owner and contractor have not yet settled on its effect on price or time. The contractor must proceed with the directed work even though the adjustment remains unresolved.

questions.question: Which AIA document is used for minor changes in the work that do not require an adjustment in contract sum or time?

options.A: AIA G701, Change Order, signed by all parties
options.B: AIA G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions
options.C: AIA G612, Owner's Instructions to the architect
options.D: AIA G714, Construction Change Directive

questions.explanation: The Architect's Supplemental Instructions form is the standard vehicle for a minor change that stays within the intent of the documents and alters neither the contract sum nor the time. Because nothing financial or scheduling changes, the owner's signature is not needed.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, a field order is:

options.A: An engineer's directive used only when price and time changes cannot yet be agreed upon
options.B: A written order by the owner that always extends the contract time for the changed work
options.C: A written order by the engineer for minor changes not affecting contract price or time
options.D: An owner-signed instrument required before a formal change order can be executed

questions.explanation: In the EJCDC system a field order lets the engineer direct small changes in writing without touching the contract price or the contract time. Because nothing financial or scheduling changes, it needs neither the owner's signature nor a full change order.

questions.question: Under the UCC, contracts for the sale of goods must generally be in writing to be enforceable when the price exceeds:
questions.explanation: The UCC's statute of frauds for goods sets the writing threshold at sales of more than $500. To be enforceable, that writing must show a sale was made, be signed by the party being held to it, and state a quantity.

questions.question: In EJCDC procurement documents, the manufacturer or vendor furnishing the goods is referred to as:

options.A: The Seller
options.B: The Contractor
options.C: The Subcontractor
options.D: The Manufacturer of Record

questions.explanation: EJCDC purchasing documents use commercial-sale vocabulary: the party supplying the goods is the Seller and the owner is the Buyer. The term 'work,' typical of construction agreements, is not used in these goods documents.

questions.question: Under the FAR Buy American restriction, for non-iron/steel construction materials, the cost of domestic components must generally exceed what percentage of all components?

options.A: 95 percent
options.B: 55 percent
options.C: 75 percent
options.D: 25 percent

questions.explanation: For construction materials that are not predominantly iron or steel, the FAR Buy American rule generally requires that more than 55 percent of total component cost be domestic. The separate iron-and-steel test instead caps foreign content at under five percent.

questions.question: In the three-tier hierarchy of general requirements, which tier provides the BROADEST provisions?

options.A: Division 01
options.B: AIA A201 General Conditions
options.C: MasterFormat division headers
options.D: Individual technical specification sections

questions.explanation: The general conditions sit at the top of the hierarchy and provide the broadest legal and administrative framework. Division 01 then narrows that to project-specific procedures, and the technical sections supply the most detailed work requirements.

questions.question: A bid option adding scope must be coordinated across the Invitation to Bid, the Bid Form, and which Division 01 section?

options.A: 01 23 00 Alternates
options.B: 01 22 00 Unit Prices
options.C: 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures
options.D: 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures

questions.explanation: A priced option that adds scope is an alternate, so the Division 01 alternates section is where each alternate is described and kept consistent with the matching entries on the invitation and the bid form.

questions.question: Which item is NOT one of the basic components normally found in a properly composed addendum?

options.A: Changes to the procurement and contracting requirements, in sequence
options.B: The addendum number and the date of the addendum
options.C: A liquidated-damages calculation for late completion of the work
options.D: Identification of the project and the name and address of the A/E

questions.explanation: A typical addendum carries its number and date, identifies the project and the A/E, lists who receives it, sets out the changes in order, notes attachments, and is signed. A liquidated-damages calculation is not an addendum component; that subject lives in the agreement and supplementary conditions.

questions.question: Who typically authors the conditions of the contract?

options.A: The architect-of-record, while preparing the technical specifications
options.B: The specifier, by editing the firm's Division 01 master guide specification text
options.C: The owner or owner's attorney, frequently using a form such as AIA A201
options.D: The contractor, at the time of contract award and bond procurement

questions.explanation: The conditions of the contract are a legal instrument, so they are normally prepared by the owner or the owner's attorney, very often by adopting a published standard form such as AIA A201 or an EJCDC document.

questions.question: Which item is typically NOT included in the Invitation to Bid itself?

options.A: Detailed product specifications
options.B: Bid security requirements
options.C: Project name and brief description
options.D: Time and place for bid receipt

questions.explanation: The invitation summarizes key bidding information, such as the project name and description, where and when bids are received, and any bid security required. Detailed product specifications are not part of the invitation; they belong in the technical sections.

questions.question: Alternates listed on the bid form must:

options.A: Always be priced as a deduct from the base bid amount
options.B: Be left blank by any bidder that declines to price them
options.C: Match the alternate numbering and descriptions in Section 01 23 00
options.D: Replace any conflicting language in the Section 00 11 13 invitation

questions.explanation: Each alternate on the bid form must line up with the Division 01 alternates section and the rest of the procurement documents, using the same numbering and descriptions so bidders price the same items the documents define.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, a Substitution for Cause must be submitted:

options.A: Immediately on discovery, before related submittals are prepared
options.B: At any time during construction, whenever the contractor can justify it
options.C: Within 60 days after the Notice to Proceed, the convenience-request window
options.D: Only during the bidding period, as part of procurement-phase review

questions.explanation: A substitution driven by a genuine project condition (a substitution for cause) must be raised as soon as the need is discovered and, in any event, early enough that it does not disrupt preparation and review of the related submittals. The 60-day-after-notice-to-proceed window applies to convenience requests, not cause requests.

questions.question: When separate pricing is added for one specific floor-tile product, the documents to edit include:

options.A: Only Division 01, since pricing procedures live in the general requirements
options.B: The bid form, the Division 01 pricing section, and the affected technical section
options.C: Only Section 09 30 13 Ceramic Tile, since just one specified product is involved here
options.D: Only the general conditions, which govern price and payment for the contract

questions.explanation: Setting up separate pricing for one product touches three places that must agree: the bid form where the price is entered, the Division 01 alternates or unit-prices section that establishes the procedure, and the technical section that specifies the product itself.

questions.question: LEED Gold certification as a project goal would be most directly addressed in which Division 01 Level 2 section?

options.A: 01 10 00 Summary
options.B: 01 81 13 Sustainable Design Requirements
options.C: 01 33 00 Submittal Procedures
options.D: 01 50 00 Temporary Facilities and Controls

questions.explanation: A green-certification goal and the administration of its credits belong in the sustainable design requirements section, 01 81 13, which sits within the performance requirements group of Division 01.

questions.question: Quality control requirements, including mockups and field testing, are best addressed in which Division 01 Level 2 section group?

options.A: 01 40 00 Quality Requirements
options.B: 01 70 00 Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.C: 01 30 00 Administrative Requirements
options.D: 01 45 00 Quality Control and assurance
