questions.explanation: Project-wide quality matters, references, mockups, quality control, and testing, are gathered in the 01 40 00 Quality Requirements group of Division 01.

questions.question: Per typical Division 01 RFI procedural rules, a subcontractor is:

options.A: Prohibited from submitting RFIs directly; the A/E returns them unanswered
options.B: Permitted to submit RFIs to the A/E, but only for shop-drawing matters
options.C: Required to route its RFIs to the A/E through the owner's project representative
options.D: Permitted to submit RFIs directly to the A/E, parallel to the prime contractor

questions.explanation: RFIs must move through the prime contractor to preserve the contractual chain of communication. A subcontractor, not being a party to the prime contract, cannot send RFIs straight to the A/E; such RFIs are returned without an answer.

questions.question: An RFI submitted to request a different product than the one specified is:

options.A: Improper; substitution requests must use the Section 01 25 00 procedure
options.B: Permitted, but only after the contract is awarded and the NTP has issued
options.C: The proper procedure, since an RFI seeks 1 interpretation, not a product change
options.D: Permitted, but only during bidding before bids are received by the owner

questions.explanation: An RFI is for interpreting the documents, not for proposing a different product. A request to use another product has to go through the formal substitution procedure in Section 01 25 00.

questions.question: When the A/E receives an incomplete or inaccurately prepared RFI, the A/E is generally:

options.A: Obligated to forward the RFI to the owner, who may then supply the response
options.B: Obligated to fill in the missing information and respond for the contractor
options.C: Not obligated to respond, and can return the RFI to the contractor to complete
options.D: Obligated to respond within the standard time frame in spite of the deficiencies

questions.explanation: The A/E is not required to answer an RFI that is incomplete or inaccurate and may send it back to be corrected. The response time does not begin to run until a proper RFI is received.

questions.question: Per a typical Section 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures, within how many days after receipt of a substitution request must the A/E request additional information needed to complete the review?

options.A: 14 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 7 days
options.D: 21 days

questions.explanation: A common substitution procedure gives the A/E a seven-day window after receiving the request to ask for any further information or documentation needed to evaluate it. The longer periods listed apply to other steps in the process, not to this request for additional data.

questions.question: Per AIA A701 Instructions to Bidders, procurement-phase substitution requests must be submitted no later than:

options.A: At least 30 days before the bid opening
options.B: At least 14 days before the bid opening
options.C: At least 7 days before receipt of bids
options.D: On the day fixed for the bid opening

questions.explanation: The AIA Instructions to Bidders requires that bidder questions and substitution requests reach the A/E at least seven days before bids are received, leaving time to issue any needed addenda before the deadline.

questions.question: When the A/E requests additional information needed to respond to an RFI, the A/E's response time clock typically:

options.A: Continues to run from the original RFI date
options.B: Resets and runs from receipt of the requested additional information
options.C: Is forfeited if the additional information is not provided within 48 hours
options.D: Is suspended only with written owner consent

questions.explanation: If the A/E has to ask for more information before answering an RFI, the response period restarts and is measured from the date that additional information is received, not from the date of the original RFI.

questions.question: Per a typical Section 01 26 13 Request for Information, within how many days after receiving an RFI must the architect respond with the requested information or interpretation?

options.A: 5 days
options.B: 3 days
options.C: 7 days
options.D: 14 days

questions.explanation: A representative RFI procedure has the contractor submit immediately on discovery and gives the architect five days from receipt to respond. The seven-day figure does not apply to either of these steps.

questions.question: AIA Document G701 (Change Order) requires signatures from:

options.A: The architect and the contractor only
options.B: The owner, architect, and contractor
options.C: The owner and the contractor only
options.D: The owner and the bonding surety only

questions.explanation: Because a change order records mutual agreement on a scope change and its cost and time effects, the AIA change order form is signed by all three parties: owner, architect, and contractor.

questions.question: An owner asks the A/E whether a critical scope change may be issued after bids are opened but before the contract is signed. Under AIA Document A201, addenda may be issued up until:

options.A: Receipt of bids, after which only change orders may modify the contract documents
options.B: Substantial completion, provided the contractor consents in writing
options.C: The end of the bidding period fixed in the Invitation to Bid notice
options.D: Execution of the agreement, per the private owner's freedom to negotiate

questions.explanation: A201 lets addenda be issued any time before the agreement is executed, which reflects a private owner's freedom to keep negotiating up to signing. The EJCDC approach is stricter, ending addenda at the receipt of bids.

questions.question: On a public works project governed by EJCDC C-700, the latest point at which an addendum may be issued is:

options.A: Receipt of bids, per public-works limits on post-opening changes
options.B: The pre-bid conference, after which the procurement documents freeze
options.C: Award of the contract to the lowest responsive bidder
options.D: Execution of the owner-contractor agreement

questions.explanation: Under the EJCDC public-works model an addendum is a pre-bid instrument, so the last point to issue one is the receipt of bids. Public procurement policy generally forbids changing the documents after opening but before execution. The AIA's later cutoff reflects the private-owner view.

questions.question: A bidder submits a written question nine days before bid opening on a project using AIA A701 Instructions to Bidders. The A/E should treat the question as:

options.A: Timely only if accompanied by a formal substitution request form
options.B: Timely, because A701 requires questions 7 days before receipt of bids
options.C: Untimely, because A701 requires questions 10 days before opening
options.D: Untimely, because questions may be raised only at the pre-bid meeting

questions.explanation: The AIA Instructions to Bidders sets a minimum of seven days before bids are received for questions and substitution requests, so a question submitted nine days out is within the window and timely. The ten-day figure comes from the EJCDC recommendation, not A701.

questions.question: Procurement documents are obtained at the A/E's office upon a $100 deposit per set. A firm that obtains documents but does not submit a bid, then returns them in good condition, is typically entitled to:

options.A: The full $100 deposit, identical to a returning bidder
options.B: A partial refund of $75, less than a returning bidder receives
options.C: A credit toward documents on the owner's next advertised project
options.D: No refund, because only actual bidders may recover the deposit

questions.explanation: It is common for a bidder that returns documents in good condition after bid opening to recover the full deposit, while a non-bidder that returns documents recovers only a reduced amount. With a $100 deposit, that reduced refund here is $75.

questions.question: Which item is NOT a standard component of a properly composed addendum?

options.A: The changes to the procurement and contracting requirements, in sequence
options.B: A statement of the contractor's anticipated overhead and profit markup
options.C: The addendum number and date
options.D: Identification of the project and the A/E's name and address

questions.explanation: A properly composed addendum carries its number and date, identifies the project and the A/E, names the recipients, lists the changes in sequence, notes attachments, and is signed. A statement of the contractor's overhead and profit is a change-order pricing matter, not part of an addendum.

questions.question: A specifier must locate a provision establishing the legal relationships, rights, and remedies among the owner, contractor, and A/E. This belongs in:

options.A: The conditions of the contract, such as AIA A201, not Division 01
options.B: Each affected technical section under its own Part 1 General article
options.C: Division 01 General Requirements, Section 01 10 00 Summary
options.D: The Invitation to Bid issued during the procurement phase

questions.explanation: Legal relationships, rights, and remedies among the parties are the province of the conditions of the contract, such as AIA A201. Division 01 instead carries project-specific administrative and procedural requirements, not the legal framework.

questions.question: A requirement governing the contractor's schedule of values and applications for funds is most properly placed in:

options.A: Section 01 29 00 Payment Procedures
options.B: Section 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures
options.C: The agreement between the owner and contractor
options.D: Section 01 22 00 Unit Prices

questions.explanation: The payment procedures section is the home for requirements on the schedule of values and the applications for payment, including the forms, copies, and timing involved.

questions.question: Which characteristic is typical of Division 01 but NOT of the conditions of the contract?

options.A: The rights and remedies of the parties upon default or dispute
options.B: The legal obligations among the owner, A/E, and contractor
options.C: Detailed, project-specific administrative and procedural rules
options.D: Definitions of basic contract terms used throughout the documents

questions.explanation: The conditions of the contract supply definitions, legal relationships, and rights and remedies. Division 01 is where the detailed, project-specific procedures live, covering submittals, meetings, quality, and closeout.

questions.question: Who typically prepares the conditions of the contract for a project?

options.A: The contractor, at the time of bond and insurance procurement
options.B: The specifier, by editing the firm's Division 01 master guide
options.C: The owner or owner's attorney, commonly adopting A201 or C-700
options.D: The architect-of-record, as part of the technical specifications

questions.explanation: Being a legal document, the conditions of the contract are normally prepared by the owner or the owner's attorney, frequently by adopting a published standard form such as AIA A201 or an EJCDC document.

questions.question: A project sets a LEED Gold goal. The credit administration, documentation, and certification submittals are most directly specified in:

options.A: Section 01 45 00 Quality Control
options.B: Section 01 33 00 Submittal Procedures
options.C: Section 01 91 13 General Commissioning Requirements
options.D: Section 01 81 13 Sustainable Design Requirements

questions.explanation: Green-certification goals and the administration of their credits are specified in the sustainable design requirements section, 01 81 13, which falls within the performance requirements group of Division 01.

questions.question: General requirements for the start-up acceptance process, including the agent's role, are specified in Division 01 under:

options.A: Section 01 94 00 Facility Decommissioning
options.B: Section 01 91 00 Commissioning
options.C: Section 01 79 00 Demonstration and Training
options.D: Section 01 77 00 Closeout Procedures

questions.explanation: Commissioning the facility, the role of the commissioning agent, and coordination of the commissioning process are specified in the commissioning section, 01 91 00 (with its general commissioning requirements). Decommissioning, by contrast, is covered in 01 94 00.

questions.question: Per CSI SectionFormat, an Action Submittal differs from an Informational Submittal in that it:

options.A: Requires responsive review by the A/E, while an informational one does not
options.B: Is submitted at closeout, while an informational one is submitted during work
options.C: Is reviewed by the owner, while an informational one is reviewed by the A/E
options.D: Is required only on public projects, while an informational one is optional

questions.explanation: An action submittal, such as product data, a shop drawing, or a sample, is one the A/E must act on by reviewing and responding. An informational submittal is provided for the record and does not call for that responsive action. Both categories are defined in Division 01.

questions.question: An owner adds an MBE/DBE participation goal during procurement. The requirements are best located in:

options.A: Each affected technical section, organized trade by trade
options.B: The bid form alone, where each bidder lists its participation percentage
options.C: An informal A/E memorandum issued to the bidders during the 1 procurement phase
options.D: The supplementary conditions plus a Division 01 section, with bid-form support

questions.explanation: A participation goal is addressed in the supplementary conditions and a Division 01 administrative section, with the bid form capturing the bidder's documentation. It is not spread across the technical sections.

questions.question: End-of-service-life shutdown requirements for a building are specified in:

options.A: Section 01 77 00 Closeout Procedures
options.B: Section 01 91 00 Commissioning of the facility
options.C: Section 01 94 00 Facility Decommissioning
options.D: Section 01 78 00 Closeout Submittals and records

questions.explanation: Activities for taking a facility out of service at the end of its life are specified in the facility decommissioning section, 01 94 00, which is distinct from commissioning and from the project closeout sections.

questions.question: A specifier must place general requirements and procedures for the team's value-analysis process. The correct Division 01 section is:

options.A: Section 01 22 00 Unit Prices
options.B: Section 01 24 00 Value Analysis
options.C: Section 01 21 00 Allowances
options.D: Section 01 23 00 Alternates list

questions.explanation: The general requirements and procedures for value analysis are set in the value analysis section, 01 24 00.

questions.question: An item whose exact quantity is unknown at bid time but whose rate can be fixed, paid as installed, is best handled as a:

options.A: Cash allowance under Section 01 21 13
options.B: Alternate under Section 01 23 00
options.C: Measured price under Section 01 22 00
options.D: Quantity allowance under Section 01 21 19

questions.explanation: When the quantity of an item is uncertain at bid time but a price per unit can be agreed, a unit price (Section 01 22 00) is the right device: the installed quantity is measured and paid at that agreed rate. A cash allowance instead fixes a dollar sum for a deferred selection.

questions.question: An owner wants a defined scope item priced separately so it can be accepted or declined at award. This is specified as a(n):

options.A: Unit price in Section 01 22 00
options.B: Alternate in Section 01 23 00
options.C: Contract modification in Section 01 26 00
options.D: Allowance in Section 01 21 00

questions.explanation: A defined scope item that the owner can take or leave at award, priced separately on the bid form, is an alternate (Section 01 23 00). Each affected technical section then cross-references that alternates section.

questions.question: A dollar sum is carried in the contract for finish hardware whose specific product the owner has not yet selected, to be reconciled against actual cost. This device is a:

options.A: Cash allowance under Section 01 21 13
options.B: Deduct alternate under Section 01 23 00
options.C: Quantity allowance under Section 01 21 19
options.D: Unit price under Section 01 22 00

questions.explanation: Carrying a stated dollar sum for a product whose selection is deferred, then reconciling it against the actual cost by change order, is a cash allowance (Section 01 21 13). A quantity allowance instead fixes an estimated quantity of installed work.

questions.question: A specifier is sorting draft Division 01 content into the categories industry guidance uses to describe the General Requirements. Procedures for eventually taking the completed facility out of service belong in which category?

options.A: Performance requirements
options.B: Temporary facilities and controls
options.C: Life cycle activities
options.D: Administrative and procedural requirements

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says life cycle activities relate to commissioning, facility operation, facility maintenance, and facility decommissioning, so procedures for taking the facility out of service fall there. Performance requirements relate to facility and system performance, temporary facilities and controls exist only during construction and are then removed, and administrative and procedural requirements concern contract administration and assignment of responsibilities.

questions.question: The fire protection engineer asks the specifier to add a special submittal review step that applies only to the fire-suppression sprinkler section. Where should this requirement be written?

options.A: In Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures, in a paragraph naming the sprinkler section
options.B: In the supplementary conditions, modifying the submittals article
options.C: In a Basic Requirements section at the start of that division
options.D: In the affected section itself, as a section-specific procedure

questions.explanation: Industry guidance directs that an administrative or procedural requirement peculiar to one section be written in that section, while Division 01 carries requirements broad enough to apply across Divisions 02 through 49. Placing a one-section procedure in Section 01 33 00 (even in a paragraph naming the section) or in the supplementary conditions puts it in the wrong document, and industry guidance says Basic Requirements sections within individual divisions are not recommended because they may conflict with Division 01.

questions.question: The section titles for Division 01 come from ____, and the arrangement of Division 01 numbers and titles approximates ____.

options.A: MasterFormat; the sequence of SectionFormat's three parts
options.B: SectionFormat; the order of the MasterFormat divisions
options.C: MasterFormat; the order of the general conditions articles
options.D: UniFormat; the sequence of SectionFormat's three parts

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that MasterFormat provides the section titles for Division 01, and industry guidance says the Division 01 numbers and titles are arranged to approximate the sequence of information in SectionFormat (PART 1, PART 2, PART 3). SectionFormat does not supply titles, UniFormat is not the source industry guidance names, and the order of general conditions articles is not the organizing basis.

questions.question: While reviewing a construction project manual, the owner's facility manager asks why Section 01 93 00—Facility Maintenance was not included in Division 01. Which response is consistent with industry guidance?

options.A: Facility life cycle activities fall outside Division 01 by definition
options.B: That title better suits a later stage, such as facility management
options.C: MasterFormat reserves that number solely for future expansion of Division 01
options.D: Maintenance topics belong in the general conditions instead

questions.explanation: Industry guidance cites Section 01 93 00—Facility Maintenance as a MasterFormat title that may never appear in a construction project manual, because specifications are created for the construction stage and some titles are more likely to appear in another stage, such as facility management. Life cycle activities are in fact one of the Division 01 categories, and industry guidance says nothing about reserved numbers or moving maintenance into the general conditions.

questions.question: Industry guidance names two MasterFormat sections as examples of titles that are especially relevant to project manuals because they address construction activities directly. Which pair does it name?

options.A: 01 14 00—Work Restrictions and 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.B: 01 50 00—Temporary Facilities and Controls and 01 93 00—Facility Maintenance
options.C: 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures and 01 93 00—Facility Maintenance
options.D: 01 14 00—Work Restrictions and 01 50 00—Temporary Facilities and Controls

questions.explanation: Industry guidance offers Work Restrictions (01 14 00) and Temporary Facilities and Controls (01 50 00) as its two examples of MasterFormat titles with particular relevance to project manuals, since both deal with construction activities. Facility Maintenance (01 93 00) is the example of a title that may never appear in a construction project manual, and Submittal Procedures (01 33 00) is not one of the examples given.

questions.question: Industry guidance aligns each Division 01 grouping with one of SectionFormat's three parts. Quality Control (Source) is aligned with the same part as which other grouping?

options.A: Quality Assurance
options.B: Performance Requirements
options.C: Quality Control (Field)
options.D: Temporary Facilities and Controls

questions.explanation: Product Requirements, Performance Requirements, and Quality Control (Source) are the groupings aligned with PART 2—PRODUCTS. Quality Assurance and Temporary Facilities and Controls are aligned with PART 1—GENERAL, and Quality Control (Field) with PART 3—EXECUTION, so the three quality groupings fall in three different parts.

questions.question: Which Division 01 grouping does industry guidance align with PART 1—GENERAL of SectionFormat?

options.A: Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.B: Performance Requirements
options.C: Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.D: Life Cycle Activities

questions.explanation: The Division 01 groupings aligned with PART 1—GENERAL are Summary, Price and Payment Procedures, Administrative Requirements, Quality Assurance, and Temporary Facilities and Controls. Performance Requirements aligns with PART 2—PRODUCTS, while Execution and Closeout Requirements and Life Cycle Activities align with PART 3—EXECUTION.

questions.question: For a small tenant fit-out, a specifier wants to combine the Division 01 procedural requirements into three sections instead of issuing a separate section for every applicable Level 2 title. This approach is:

options.A: Not acceptable, since every MasterFormat Level 2 title must be its own section
options.B: Acceptable only if the supplementary conditions list each omitted title
options.C: Acceptable; sections may be combined or divided to suit project complexity
options.D: Acceptable only for PART 1 sections; PART 3 sections must remain separate

questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that tying Division 01 to SectionFormat gives an organizing logic flexible enough to consolidate procedural requirements into a few sections or split them among many, depending on how complex the project is. Industry guidance does not require one section per Level 2 title, a list of omitted titles in the supplementary conditions, or any limit that confines combining to PART 1 groupings.

questions.question: The instructions to bidders state that the successful bidder must provide weekly drone photographs of progress. The requirement appears nowhere else in the project manual or drawings. During construction, the contractor declines to provide the photographs. The requirement is:

options.A: Enforceable, since the agreement incorporates the bidding documents by reference
options.B: Not enforceable, since procurement requirements are not contract documents
options.C: Not enforceable, since only the general conditions may impose documentation requirements
options.D: Enforceable, if the bid form acknowledged receipt of the instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: Under the AIA, EJCDC, and ConsensusDocs general conditions, procurement requirements are by definition outside the contract documents, so industry guidance holds that a provision appearing only there cannot be enforced while the construction contract is administered. The agreement incorporates the contract documents, not the procurement requirements, and submitting a bid or acknowledging the instructions on the bid form does not change that. The general conditions are not the only place such a requirement can go: Division 01 (Section 01 32 00, industry guidance) specifies photographic documentation, which is where this requirement belonged.

questions.question: Bidders need to know before pricing that the project has detailed substitution procedures in Division 01. How should the instructions to bidders address this?

options.A: Refer to the applicable Division 01 section by its number and title
options.B: Restate the substitution procedures in full so bidders cannot miss them
options.C: Summarize the procedures and state that the summary governs during bidding
options.D: Omit any mention, since procurement requirements cannot address Division 01

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says procurement requirements should point bidders to the relevant Division 01 sections, identified by number and title, instead of repeating Division 01 provisions. Restating or summarizing the procedures creates duplication and room for conflict, and saying nothing leaves bidders without a pointer to the governing section.

questions.question: The owner-contractor agreement notes that the owner will occupy completed portions of the building during construction. Which Division 01 section specifies the need to accommodate the owner's occupancy in more detail?

options.A: Section 01 20 00—Price and Payment Procedures
options.B: Section 01 50 00—Temporary Facilities and Controls
options.C: Section 01 10 00—Summary
options.D: Section 01 30 00—Administrative Requirements

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that Section 01 10 00—Summary specifies the owner's and contractor's responsibilities, including a summary of the work, other contracts, work restrictions, and the need to accommodate the owner's occupancy during construction. Section 01 20 00 expands on allowances, alternates, and unit prices, and the administrative and temporary facilities groupings are not where industry guidance places owner occupancy.

questions.question: An owner-contractor agreement includes stipulated unit prices and a list of alternates, and the project also carries several allowances. Which Division 01 section expands on these agreement provisions?

options.A: Section 01 10 00—Summary
options.B: Section 01 30 00—Administrative Requirements
options.C: Section 01 70 00—Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.D: Section 01 20 00—Price and Payment Procedures

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says Section 01 20 00—Price and Payment Procedures expands on related agreement provisions such as allowances, alternates, and unit prices. Section 01 10 00—Summary covers the summary of work, other contracts, work restrictions, and owner occupancy, and the administrative and execution/closeout groupings do not carry these pricing mechanisms.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the owner-contractor agreement and Division 01?

options.A: Division 01 supersedes the agreement wherever the two documents address the same topic
options.B: The agreement includes all contract documents by reference; Division 01 details some provisions
options.C: The agreement includes only the conditions of the contract; Division 01 restates its payment terms
options.D: The agreement includes the procurement requirements by reference; Division 01 then modifies them

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that the owner-contractor agreement includes by reference all other contract documents, and that some agreement provisions are supplemented by Division 01 sections defining the parties' responsibilities in greater detail. Division 01 does not supersede the agreement, the agreement is not limited to the conditions of the contract, and procurement requirements are not contract documents.

questions.question: A peer reviewer notes that cutting and patching is addressed in both the general conditions and Division 01 and calls this a violation of CSI's 'say it once and in the right place' principle. The best response is:

options.A: Disagree; the two state it at different levels of detail, without conflict
options.B: Agree; delete the Division 01 provisions and rely on the general conditions
options.C: Agree; move the general conditions text into the supplementary conditions
options.D: Disagree; Division 01 takes precedence over the general conditions in any case

questions.explanation: Industry guidance lists cutting and patching among the topics the general conditions cover only in broad terms, which Division 01 then details for the specific project. The principle is not violated because the requirements are stated at two different levels of detail, without duplication or conflict, so deleting or relocating either text is unwarranted, and industry guidance does not rest the answer on Division 01 taking precedence.

questions.question: Which set consists entirely of topics that industry guidance lists as usually covered, in broad terms, by the general conditions and then detailed in Division 01?

options.A: Property surveys, cutting and patching, cleaning, record documents
options.B: Bid security, warranties, submittals, progress schedules
options.C: Mock-ups, schedule of values, applications for payment, closeout procedures
options.D: Pest control, temporary utilities and services, warranties, cleaning

questions.explanation: The general conditions topics in industry guidance include property surveys, record documents, cutting and patching, and cleaning, along with warranties, submittals, progress schedules, temporary utilities and services, the schedule of values, applications for payment, and closeout procedures. Each other set contains one item from elsewhere: bid security is a procurement-stage provision, mock-ups are specified in Section 01 40 00, and pest control is specified in Section 01 57 00.

questions.question: The general conditions broadly permit the owner to use separate contractors and to coordinate them. When separate contractors are in fact used, what does Division 01 add?

options.A: The bid security amount and bid opening date for each contract
options.B: The owner's legal right to award separate contracts and provide coordination
options.C: The contracts, the scope of work in each, and each party's coordination role
options.D: The insurance limits and bond amounts required of each separate contractor

questions.explanation: In the example, the general conditions only broadly permit separate contractors, and Division 01 (for instance, Section 01 12 00—Multiple Contract Summary) then identifies each contract and its scope and defines how the owner, the A/E, and each contractor take part in coordination. Bid security and opening dates are procurement-stage items, the owner's right is already stated in the general conditions, and insurance limits and bond amounts are not part of the example.

questions.question: The only general reference to Division 01 that belongs in the supplementary conditions is:

options.A: A list of every Division 01 section number and title
options.B: A summary restating the key provisions of each Division 01 section
options.C: A statement that Division 01 applies only where the general conditions are silent
options.D: A statement establishing the authority of Division 01

questions.explanation: Industry guidance permits one general reference to Division 01 in the supplementary conditions: a statement that establishes Division 01's authority. A list or summary of Division 01 content would invite the duplication and conflicts that coordinating the two documents is meant to prevent, and a statement confining Division 01 to matters the general conditions leave open is not the authority statement industry guidance describes.

questions.question: A specifier adds a statement to the supplementary conditions that shop drawings, product data, and samples shall be prepared and submitted according to Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures. The owner's attorney asks whether the statement is required. It is:

options.A: Required, because Division 01 is unenforceable unless the supplementary conditions cite it
options.B: Improper, because the supplementary conditions may never cite a specific Division 01 section
options.C: Unnecessary, but it may help the user of the documents
options.D: Permitted, but only if it also summarizes the Section 01 33 00 requirements

questions.explanation: Industry guidance treats statements in the supplementary conditions that point to specific Division 01 sections as unnecessary but potentially helpful to the user, and it uses this very submittal statement as its example. Such a reference is neither required for enforceability nor prohibited, and summarizing Section 01 33 00 in the supplementary conditions would repeat Division 01 content that they should not encroach on.

questions.question: A draft of the supplementary conditions includes detailed procedures for locating the contractor's field office and sanitation facilities. What should the specifier do?

options.A: Keep them there, since supplementary conditions take precedence over Division 01
options.B: Relocate them to the general conditions, which govern temporary facilities
options.C: Relocate them to the instructions to bidders, so bidders can price them
options.D: Relocate them to Division 01, where construction facilities are specified

questions.explanation: Industry guidance cautions that supplementary conditions should neither repeat the general conditions nor take over subjects that more properly belong in Division 01; field offices and sanitation facilities are specified in Section 01 52 00—Construction Facilities. Precedence is no reason to leave Division 01 subject matter in the supplementary conditions, the general conditions are broad standard text, and the instructions to bidders are procurement requirements, which are not contract documents.

questions.question: Which pair of Division 01 subjects does industry guidance say usually requires extensive delineation on the drawings and close coordination with Division 01?

options.A: Submittals and quality requirements
options.B: Use of the site and phased construction
options.C: Use of the site and submittals
options.D: Phased construction and quality requirements

questions.explanation: Division 01 sections on use of the site, phased construction, and multiple prime contracts normally need extensive graphic delineation and close coordination between the drawings and Division 01. Submittals and quality requirements are purely procedural subjects that need no coordination with the drawings, so any pair that includes either one is wrong.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, the specifier has limited time to cross-check Division 01 against the drawings. Which section needs no coordination with the drawings?

options.A: Section 01 12 00—Multiple Contract Summary
options.B: Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions
options.C: Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements
options.D: Section 01 11 00—Summary of Work

questions.explanation: Purely procedural Division 01 sections such as submittals, quality requirements, and closeout procedures need no coordination with the drawings. Multiple prime contract sections and site-use restrictions usually require extensive delineation on the drawings, and the drawings graphically define the extent of work that the summary describes.

questions.question: The site plan for a single-contract project shows a future parking structure to be built later under a separate contract. A reviewer argues the drawings should show only work of this contract. Showing the parking structure is:

options.A: Appropriate, since drawings may define related work outside the contract
options.B: Improper, since drawings may depict only work included in this contract
options.C: Improper, since related work may be described only in Division 01 text
options.D: Appropriate only if the supplementary conditions expressly authorize it

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that drawings graphically show Division 01 subjects such as the extent of work, and that they may also show related work whether or not it is part of the contract. Drawings are therefore not limited to this contract's work, and industry guidance sets no rule confining related work to Division 01 text or requiring authorization in the supplementary conditions.

questions.question: In the recommended sequence of Division 01 coordination activities, the specifier first distributes an early draft to contributors and then prepares a list of requirements solicited from consultants. Which activity comes next?

options.A: Resolve overlapping requirements, omissions, and conflicts
options.B: Determine which requirements belong in Division 01 and which are section-specific
options.C: Compare the list of requirements with the Division 01 draft
options.D: Revise the Division 01 draft for review by specification contributors

questions.explanation: Industry guidance lists the coordination effort in order: distribute a Division 01 draft early, prepare a list of requirements solicited from consultants and contributors, compare that list with the draft, determine which belong in Division 01 versus individual sections, resolve overlaps, omissions, and conflicts, and revise the draft for review. Determining, resolving, and revising all follow the comparison.

questions.question: For an occupied hospital renovation, a specifier finds restrictions on the contractor's operations in occupied areas written in both Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions and Section 01 35 00—Special Procedures. The specifier should:

options.A: Keep both so each section is complete when read on its own
options.B: Verify the requirement is stated in one location that provides its basis
options.C: Move both into the supplementary conditions to give them contractual force
options.D: Add a Basic Requirements section to each affected technical division instead

questions.explanation: Industry guidance uses this very example: Section 01 14 00 restricts operations in an owner-occupied building, while Section 01 35 00 may establish similar restrictions by activity or project type, so the specifier should verify each requirement is in one location offering the basis for imposing it. Keeping duplicates invites conflict, and industry guidance says division-level Basic Requirements sections are not recommended and may conflict with Division 01.

questions.question: On a small retail project, the owner's representative asks the specifier to add extensive Division 01 requirements: daily reports, weekly coordination meetings, multiple photo sets, and elaborate temporary facilities. Which consideration from industry guidance should guide the specifier's response?

options.A: These items carry only direct costs, which bidders will identify and price
options.B: Detailed procedures reduce disputes, which lowers overall construction cost
options.C: Added requirements shift all administrative obligations from the A/E to the contractor
options.D: Overspecifying may raise costs and burden whoever administers the contract

questions.explanation: Industry guidance cautions that the administrative and procedural requirements and temporary facilities and controls in Division 01 carry both direct and indirect costs, so overspecifying can raise construction costs unnecessarily and impose excessive obligations on whoever administers the construction contract. The costs are not only direct, industry guidance does not present added procedures as a cost saving, and the caution concerns burdens on the administering entity rather than a shift of A/E duties to the contractor.

questions.question: For detailed examples of Division 01 sections, specifiers are referred to master guide specification systems. Which system-and-publisher pairing is correct?

options.A: MASTERSPEC, an AIA product published by Deltek
options.B: SpecLink, published by the AIA
options.C: SPECTEXT, published by Building Systems Design
options.D: Unified Facilities Guide Specifications, published by GSA

questions.explanation: Industry guidance refers readers to the American Institute of Architects' MASTERSPEC (published by Deltek), Deltek's SPECTEXT, Building Systems Design's (BSD) SpecLink, and DoD/NASA's Unified Facilities Guide Specifications. SpecLink is attributed to BSD, SPECTEXT to Deltek, and the UFGS to DoD/NASA, not GSA.

questions.question: The owner wants daily reports of site activity and recorded video of the work as it proceeds. The requirements for these belong in:

options.A: Section 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination
options.B: Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation
options.C: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.D: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals

questions.explanation: Industry guidance assigns to Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation the progress schedule, daily construction reports, and the type of photographic documentation, whether printed images, digital images, or video. Section 01 31 00 covers coordination and meetings, Section 01 33 00 covers shop drawings, product data, and samples, and Section 01 78 00 covers closeout submittals.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, Section 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination must address who is responsible for project meetings. The specifier determines whether that responsibility lies with:

options.A: the owner or the architect/engineer
options.B: the architect/engineer or the commissioning agent
options.C: the owner's project manager or the A/E's field representative
options.D: one of the contractors or the construction manager

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says that if the project is constructed under multiple prime contracts, the specifier determines responsibility for project meetings, whether one of the contractors or the construction manager, and specifies the frequency and location of meetings. The owner, the A/E, and the commissioning agent are not the alternatives industry guidance names for this decision.

questions.question: A specifier must state the testing laboratory's qualifications, the limits on its authority, the contractor's cooperation duties, and who pays for tests, along with site mock-ups that will serve as standards for installed work. These belong in:

options.A: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.B: Section 01 60 00—Product Requirements
options.C: Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements
options.D: Section 01 75 00—Starting and Adjusting

questions.explanation: Industry guidance places in Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements the construction, review, and use of site mock-ups and field samples as quality standards, plus testing laboratory qualifications, limitations of authority, contractor cooperation, payment responsibilities, and references to required tests. Section 01 33 00 governs shop drawings, product data, and samples, Section 01 60 00 governs product options, delivery, and storage, and Section 01 75 00 covers starting and adjusting equipment.

questions.question: A project needs temporary lots where construction workers can leave their cars, plus temporary drives into the site. Which section specifies these facilities?

options.A: Section 01 55 00—Vehicular Access and Parking
options.B: Section 01 53 00—Temporary Construction
options.C: Section 01 56 00—Temporary Barriers and Enclosures
options.D: Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions

questions.explanation: Industry guidance places temporary access and parking facilities in Section 01 55 00—Vehicular Access and Parking. Section 01 53 00—Temporary Construction is confined to structural components of temporary structures, Section 01 56 00 covers fences and noise and dust barriers, and Section 01 14 00 holds special restrictions on the contractor's access rather than the facilities themselves.

questions.question: The owner will let the contractor's delivery trucks onto the operating campus only through the north gate and only between 9:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. Where should this limitation on the contractor's access be specified?

options.A: Section 01 55 00—Vehicular Access and Parking
options.B: Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions
options.C: Section 01 57 00—Temporary Controls
options.D: Section 01 56 00—Temporary Barriers and Enclosures

questions.explanation: Industry guidance confines Section 01 55 00—Vehicular Access and Parking to maintaining and controlling access and sends special restrictions on the contractor's access to Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions; industry guidance likewise lists limitations on access to and use of the site among the work restrictions. Sections 01 56 00 and 01 57 00 cover barriers and enclosures and temporary controls such as erosion, sediment, and pest control.

questions.question: Which pairing of requirement and Division 01 section is correct for temporary facilities and controls?

options.A: Noise barriers—01 57 00 Temporary Controls
options.B: Temporary signs—01 52 00 Construction Facilities
options.C: Swing staging and scaffolding—01 53 00 Temporary Construction
options.D: Dust barriers—01 56 00 Temporary Barriers and Enclosures

questions.explanation: Industry guidance places fences, noise barriers, and dust barriers in Section 01 56 00—Temporary Barriers and Enclosures. Section 01 57 00—Temporary Controls covers surface water, erosion and sediment, and pest control rather than noise barriers, temporary signs belong in Section 01 58 00—Project Identification, and swing staging and scaffolding belong in Section 01 54 00—Construction Aids.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, the tower crane and personnel hoists furnished by one prime contractor will also be used by the other prime contractors. The requirements for sharing this equipment are indicated in:

options.A: Section 01 54 00—Construction Aids
options.B: Section 01 51 00—Temporary Utilities
options.C: Section 01 53 00—Temporary Construction
options.D: Section 01 52 00—Construction Facilities

questions.explanation: Industry guidance assigns temporary elevators, hoists, cranes, scaffolding, and swing staging to Section 01 54 00—Construction Aids and says to indicate requirements for sharing construction aids when multiple contracts are used. Section 01 51 00 covers temporary utilities, Section 01 52 00 covers field offices and sanitation facilities, and Section 01 53 00 covers structural components of temporary structures.

questions.question: The owner will purchase kitchen equipment for installation by the contractor, and Section 01 64 00 will be used. Where should the owner's list of these items be located, and where should it be cross-referenced?

options.A: Listed in 01 10 00—Summary; cross-referenced in 01 64 00
options.B: Listed in 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products; cross-referenced in 01 10 00
options.C: Listed in 01 73 00—Execution; cross-referenced in 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products
options.D: Listed in 01 65 00—Product Delivery Requirements; cross-referenced in 01 10 00

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says that if Section 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products is used, the list of owner-furnished products should be located there and cross-referenced in Section 01 10 00—Summary. Reversing the two contradicts that guidance, Section 01 73 00 covers installing owner-furnished products while referring to 01 64 00 for their characteristics, and Section 01 65 00 covers packing, shipping, and delivery.

questions.question: A specifier needs to state the basic rules the contractor follows when choosing among specified products, including the general procedure for deciding whether products are equivalent. This belongs in:

options.A: Section 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products
options.B: Section 01 65 00—Product Delivery Requirements
options.C: Section 01 62 00—Product Options
options.D: Section 01 66 00—Product Storage and Handling Requirements

questions.explanation: Industry guidance gives Section 01 62 00—Product Options the basic rules for the contractor's choices among products, including how to judge whether products are equivalent. Section 01 64 00 covers owner-furnished products, Section 01 65 00 covers packing, shipping, delivery, and acceptance, and Section 01 66 00 covers handling and storage at the site.

questions.question: In Section 01 73 00—Execution, industry guidance distinguishes among three possibilities for existing material and equipment. Which of the following is one of them?

options.A: Salvaged and retained by the contractor, with salvage value accruing to the contractor
options.B: Abandoned in place and concealed behind new construction
options.C: Salvaged and sold by the contractor, with proceeds shared equally with the owner
options.D: Salvaged and retained by the contractor, with salvage value accruing to the owner

questions.explanation: Industry guidance has Section 01 73 00—Execution distinguish three cases for existing material and equipment: salvaged and reinstalled in the work; salvaged and kept by the contractor, with the salvage value going to the owner; and salvaged and delivered to the owner. Value going to the contractor, a split of sale proceeds, and abandonment in place are not among the three.

questions.question: The mechanical engineer wants the HVAC systems run and adjusted again in the opposite season after initial start-up, with a defined method for reporting compliance. The basic requirement belongs in:

options.A: Section 01 75 00—Starting and Adjusting
options.B: Section 01 79 00—Demonstration and Training
options.C: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals
options.D: Section 01 76 00—Protecting Installed Construction

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that Section 01 75 00—Starting and Adjusting specifies the schedule for starting and adjusting equipment and systems, requirements for seasonal operation, and the method for reporting compliance. Demonstration and Training addresses training the owner's staff, Closeout Submittals addresses record documents and operation and maintenance data, and Protecting Installed Construction addresses protection of finished work.

questions.question: While other trades keep working, newly completed wall and floor work must be guarded, and the documents must state how damaged completed work will be remedied or replaced. These basic requirements belong in:

options.A: Section 01 56 00—Temporary Barriers and Enclosures
options.B: Section 01 76 00—Protecting Installed Construction
options.C: Section 01 74 00—Cleaning and Waste Management
options.D: Section 01 77 00—Closeout Procedures

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that Section 01 76 00—Protecting Installed Construction includes basic requirements for protecting finished work while construction continues and describes remedial and replacement requirements. Section 01 56 00 covers barriers that protect facility users and existing spaces, Section 01 74 00 covers cleaning and recycling, and Section 01 77 00 covers substantial and final completion and punch lists.

questions.question: An owner requires that the building earn particular, owner-selected credits (specific points) under a named green building rating system. Where in Division 01 should the specifier locate these requirements?

options.A: Section 01 81 00—Facility Performance Requirements
options.B: Section 01 81 13—Sustainable Design Requirements
options.C: A section in the range 01 82 00 through 01 89 00
options.D: Section 01 35 00—Special Requirements

questions.explanation: Industry guidance directs that when a project must earn specific points in a particular rating system, the requirements go in Section 01 35 00 or one of its Level 3 sections, such as 01 35 63 for sustainability certification requirements. Section 01 81 00 covers general facility-wide performance such as sustainability and energy goals, and industry guidance reserves 01 81 13 for cases where the contractor chooses which points to pursue. The 01 82 00 to 01 89 00 range covers performance shared by work in multiple sections, not rating-system points.

questions.question: The design team wants interior partitions, doors, and joint sealants, which are specified in several different sections, to jointly meet a minimum sound isolation rating. Where should this requirement be specified, and who is responsible for how it is achieved?

options.A: Section 01 81 00; the A/E details the assemblies that achieve the rating
options.B: Section 01 81 00; the contractor develops the means and methods
options.C: A section within 01 82 00 to 01 89 00; the contractor develops the means and methods
options.D: A section within 01 82 00 to 01 89 00; the A/E details the assemblies in each section

questions.explanation: Industry guidance assigns Sections 01 82 00 through 01 89 00 to overall performance requirements when work results in multiple sections must work together to reach a minimum level, and it makes the contractor responsible for developing the means and methods to reach it. Section 01 81 00 is for general facility-wide performance such as sustainability and energy, not a requirement shared by specific interior assemblies, and having the A/E detail the solution contradicts the contractor's stated responsibility.

questions.question: A specifier is drafting Section 01 21 00—Allowances for a door hardware cash allowance. Which other documents typically also carry allowance provisions that must be coordinated with that section?

options.A: The procurement requirements, the conditions of the contract, and Section 08 71 00—Door Hardware
options.B: The procurement requirements, the conditions of the contract, and the door hardware product submittals
options.C: The procurement requirements, Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices, and the door hardware product submittals
options.D: The schedule of values, the conditions of the contract, and the door hardware product submittals

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says allowance requirements typically appear in four coordinated places: the procurement requirements, the conditions of the contract, Division 01, and the individual specification section for the item the allowance covers, here 08 71 00. Submittals are not contract documents and do not carry allowance provisions, and neither the unit price section nor the schedule of values is among the documents industry guidance names.

questions.question: A school project is bid as a stipulated sum with just two unit prices, for rock excavation and unsuitable soil replacement. The project manager suggests skipping formal unit-price procedures because the contract is not unit-price based. How should the specifier respond?

options.A: Agree; formal unit price procedures are needed only for contracts based entirely on unit prices
options.B: Agree; the general conditions alone adequately govern a few unit prices in a stipulated sum contract
options.C: Disagree; unit price requirements and procedures must be defined in the procurement documents either way
options.D: Disagree; the two unit prices should instead be converted into allowances under Section 01 21 00

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that unit price requirements and procedures must be defined in the procurement documents, and it applies that rule equally to a stipulated sum contract carrying a handful of unit prices and to a contract priced wholly by unit prices. The share of unit-price work does not change that obligation, and industry guidance neither treats the general conditions as sufficient on their own nor suggests converting unit prices to allowances.

questions.question: The requirements and procedures for handling unit prices involve which two components, both of which must then be coordinated with the applicable technical specifications?

options.A: The agreement form and the supplementary conditions
options.B: The bid or proposal form and Division 01 sections
options.C: The instructions to bidders and the drawing schedules
options.D: The bid security form and the schedule of values

questions.explanation: Unit price requirements rely on the bid or proposal form together with carefully written Division 01 sections, and both must be coordinated with the applicable sections in Divisions 02 through 49. The agreement, supplementary conditions, instructions to bidders, bid security, and schedule of values are not the pair industry guidance identifies for this purpose.

questions.question: While writing Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices, a specifier plans to copy the unit-price paragraphs of the project's standard general conditions into the section word for word so all requirements sit in one place. What does industry guidance recommend instead?

options.A: Coordinate with the general conditions and expand on them without duplicating them
options.B: Delete the unit price paragraphs from the general conditions so Division 01 governs alone
options.C: Restate the general conditions in Division 01 and let the agreement resolve any conflict
options.D: Leave unit prices out of Division 01 since the general conditions already address them

questions.explanation: Industry guidance warns that unit price requirements must be coordinated with the conditions of the contract to prevent conflicts, duplication, or omission, noting that most standard general conditions already address unit prices and Division 01 usually expands on them. Copying the clauses creates the duplication industry guidance cautions against, deleting general-condition text is not the specifier's remedy, and leaving unit prices out of Division 01 risks omitting essential requirements.

questions.question: On an EJCDC C-700 project, the bid form listed an estimated quantity of 2,000 cubic yards of rock excavation, but only 1,400 cubic yards were actually excavated. The contractor argues the owner guaranteed the 2,000 cubic yard figure. Under C-700, which statement is correct?

options.A: The quantity is guaranteed because the bid is attached to the agreement as an exhibit
options.B: The quantity is guaranteed unless the owner issued a field order reducing it
options.C: Estimated quantities become guaranteed once the engineer accepts the bid form
options.D: Estimated quantities are not guaranteed; they serve to compare bids

questions.explanation: In the summary of EJCDC C-700, estimated quantities are expressly not guaranteed; they exist so that bids can be compared. Although C-700 counts the bid as a contract document when it is listed and attached to the agreement, that does not convert the estimates into guarantees, and neither a field order nor the engineer's acceptance of the bid form changes this.

questions.question: On a project using EJCDC C-700, the contractor and owner disagree about how much excavated material should be paid as rock rather than common excavation under the unit price schedule. Under C-700, who has the authority to determine the actual quantities and classifications?

options.A: The owner's representative
options.B: The contractor's licensed surveyor
options.C: The engineer
options.D: The independent testing agency

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that C-700 establishes the engineer's authority to determine the actual quantities and classifications of unit price work. The owner's representative, a surveyor, or a testing agency may provide information, but none of them holds that determining authority under C-700.

questions.question: Under an EJCDC C-700 contract, a contractor's pay application bills unit-priced pipe bedding at the bid unit price and then adds a separate 15 percent markup for overhead and profit. Under C-700, how should the engineer view the markup?

options.A: Acceptable, because unit prices are understood to cover only direct labor, materials, and equipment
options.B: Not acceptable, because unit price bids already include overhead and profit
options.C: Acceptable, provided the engineer has approved the contractor's schedule of values
options.D: Not acceptable, because overhead and profit on unit price work require a field order

questions.explanation: The summary of C-700 states that unit price bids include the contractor's overhead and profit, so an added markup would count those costs twice. The claim that unit prices cover only direct costs contradicts that provision, and neither an approved schedule of values nor a field order has anything to do with whether overhead and profit are already in the unit price.

questions.question: When the A/E helps the owner develop an overall procurement strategy, which factors are weighed in evaluating a general contractor, multiple contractors, or a particular project delivery method?

options.A: Owner financing sources, the contractors' bonding capacity, and the local insurance market
options.B: Applicable building codes, zoning restrictions, and the AHJ's permitting schedule
options.C: Design fee limits, consultant availability, and the A/E's documentation schedule
options.D: Local practices, the local labor market, and likely unfavorable site conditions

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the A/E helps the owner build a procurement strategy that weighs local practices, the local labor market, and the likelihood of unfavorable site conditions when choosing among a general contractor, multiple contractors, and delivery methods. Financing, bonding, codes, zoning, design fees, and A/E staffing are not the factors industry guidance lists for that evaluation.

questions.question: The A/E's production schedule has slipped. The project manager proposes releasing the bid documents on time despite several known coordination gaps, intending to fix them through addenda during bidding and change orders after award. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Release on time and correct the gaps through addenda issued early in the bidding period
options.B: Release on time and correct the gaps by change orders once the agreement is executed
options.C: Correct the gaps first; addenda and change orders should not be relied on to fix them
options.D: Correct the gaps first; addenda may not be issued after the bidding period begins

questions.explanation: Industry guidance holds that nothing replaces clear, complete, and carefully coordinated contract documents, and that relying on addenda and change orders to repair poorly prepared drawings and project manuals should be avoided. Both release-on-time choices knowingly issue deficient documents and plan to patch them later. The other correct-first choice gives a false reason: industry guidance describes addenda as modifications issued before receipt of bids, so they can be issued during bidding.

questions.question: A state agency owner requires the A/E to use the agency's own addendum and change order forms and procedures, which differ slightly from the commonly recommended ones. How should such differences be viewed?

options.A: They override the recommended principles, so agency procedures replace them entirely
options.B: They are procedural only and do not affect the underlying principles
options.C: They are acceptable only if the agency also adopts the AIA document forms
options.D: They must be reconciled by the specifier in the supplementary conditions

questions.explanation: Industry guidance acknowledges that many public agencies have their own addendum and change order forms and procedures that vary somewhat from its suggestions, but it states those variations are procedural and leave the underlying principles intact. Industry guidance does not say agency procedures override its principles, require AIA forms, or must be reconciled in the supplementary conditions.

questions.question: During bidding, the A/E accepts a bidder's request to use a different manufacturer's roof membrane. How should this acceptance be made part of the procurement documents?

options.A: Issue an addendum to all bidders listing the approved substitution
options.B: Issue a field order to all bidders identifying the approved product
options.C: Send a letter only to the requesting bidder confirming the approval
options.D: Defer the approval and process it by change order after award

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says addenda are used whenever the procurement documents must change in any way, and it lists adding qualified products or approved substitutions as an example. A letter to only the requesting bidder does not modify the documents everyone is bidding on, a field order is an EJCDC construction-phase instrument, and a post-award change order does not put the approval into the bidding documents.

questions.question: Besides the instructions for procurement and the bid/proposal form, which documents does industry guidance identify as containing references to addenda, their method of issue, and related facts?

options.A: Sections 01 25 00 and 01 26 00 in Division 01
options.B: The advertisement for bids and the bid bond form
options.C: The drawing index and the project manual table of contents
options.D: The agreement and the conditions of the contract

questions.explanation: Industry guidance lists four places where references to addenda, how they are issued, and related facts appear: the procurement instructions, the bid or proposal form, the owner-contractor agreement, and the contract conditions. Division 01 sections, the advertisement, the bid bond, and the drawing index or table of contents are not among the documents industry guidance names.

questions.question: After award and signing of the agreement, the contractor claims that Addendum No. 3, which revised a paragraph in Section 07 54 23, is not binding because addenda are only procurement documents. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The addendum lapsed at bid opening and binds no one unless it is reissued
options.B: The revision is binding only if it is reissued later as a change order
options.C: The revision became a contract document when the agreement was executed
options.D: The addendum remains a procurement document superseded by the agreement

questions.explanation: An addendum joins the procurement documents when issued, and once the agreement is executed, any portion of it that bears on the contract documents is incorporated into them. The revision therefore does not need to be reissued as a change order, did not lapse at bid opening, and is not superseded by the agreement.

questions.question: A public owner will award three prime contracts (general, mechanical, and electrical) that are bid at the same time. How does industry guidance recommend numbering the addenda?

options.A: Use one consecutive series of addenda numbers shared by all the contracts
options.B: Use a separate consecutive series of addenda numbers for each contract
options.C: Number addenda by their issue date rather than in consecutive sequence
options.D: Number addenda by the specification Division that each one affects

questions.explanation: Industry guidance recommends numbering addenda consecutively and, where separate contracts will be awarded, giving each contract its own series of addenda numbers. A single shared series, date-based numbering, or numbering by Division is not what industry guidance recommends; it separately suggests a simple numbering system for items within each addendum to ease cross-referencing.

questions.question: Five days before bid opening, the A/E finds that the structural framing for an entire wing must be redesigned, a significant change. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Advise the owner, issue a complete addendum, and if possible delay the bid date
options.B: Issue a short addendum with a few brief statements describing the change
options.C: Hold the change and issue it by change order after the agreement is executed
options.D: Issue a minor addendum, since four days' notice is the recommended minimum

questions.explanation: For a significant change late in bidding, industry guidance says to avoid a hastily prepared addendum built on a few inadequate statements; the owner should be advised and, where possible, the bid opening postponed. The four-day figure applies only to minor addenda, and deferring until after the agreement is executed is reserved for non-critical changes that do not affect cost or time, which a wing redesign plainly does.

questions.question: An addendum will include four items: a revision to Sheet A-201, a correction to an item in Addendum No. 1, a change to the instructions to bidders, and a change to Section 09 21 16. In what order should these items appear addenda format?

options.A: Instructions to bidders, Addendum No. 1 correction, Section 09 21 16, Sheet A-201
options.B: Addendum No. 1 correction, instructions to bidders, Section 09 21 16, Sheet A-201
options.C: Addendum No. 1 correction, Section 09 21 16, Sheet A-201, instructions to bidders
options.D: Instructions to bidders, Section 09 21 16, Sheet A-201, Addendum No. 1 correction

questions.explanation: The addenda format places changes to prior addenda first, then changes to procurement requirements such as the instructions to bidders, then contracting requirements, then specifications in sequence, and finally drawings. The other sequences move the procurement change or the prior-addendum correction out of that prescribed order.

questions.question: In a typical addendum, a correction to a prior addendum, a bidding-requirements change, a contracting-requirements change, and specification changes appear under separate headings. How are the individual items numbered?

options.A: Restarting at 1 under each heading
options.B: By the affected section or sheet number
options.C: With a letter per heading and a number per item
options.D: Consecutively from the first item to the last

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that each item in the sample addendum is numbered consecutively for ease of reference, and the figure runs items 1, 2, 3, 4 straight through the prior-addenda, procurement, contracting, and specification headings. Restarting at each heading, using section or sheet numbers, or a letter-number scheme does not match the sample.

questions.question: Which part of the standard AIA, EJCDC, ConsensusDocs, and DBIA document families spells out the procedures for issuing interpretations and for ordering minor modifications consistent with them?

options.A: Their contractor-subcontractor agreements
options.B: Their instructions to bidders
options.C: Their conditions of the contract
options.D: Their standard bid forms

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that the AIA, EJCDC, ConsensusDocs, and DBIA conditions of the contract expressly establish how the A/E or owner issues interpretations and orders minor modifications consistent with them. Instructions to bidders and bid forms govern the procurement stage, and subcontract agreements do not set the A/E's or owner's authority under the prime contract.

questions.question: The A/E issues a written interpretation of an ambiguous detail that requires the contractor to add blocking. The contractor believes the interpretation justifies an increase in the contract sum. Under the standard conditions of the contract, which statement is accurate?

options.A: Either the contractor or the owner may claim a change they consider justified
options.B: Only the owner may claim a change arising from an A/E interpretation
options.C: No claim is possible because A/E interpretations are final and binding
options.D: The contractor may claim only after a change order has been executed

questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that the standard conditions include provisions allowing both the contractor and the owner to claim a change in contract sum or time when they believe a written A/E interpretation justifies it. The right is not limited to the owner, interpretations do not foreclose claims, and a claim does not wait on an executed change order.

questions.question: During construction, the contractor asks for clarification of an ambiguous detail. Under the standard conditions of the contract, which parties have procedures to issue an interpretation and order minor modifications consistent with it?

options.A: The A/E or the contractor
options.B: The A/E or the owner
options.C: The owner or the contractor
options.D: The A/E or the building official

questions.explanation: The standard conditions of the contract give the A/E or the owner the procedures to issue interpretations and to order minor modifications consistent with them. The contractor receives interpretations and may claim changes based on them but does not issue them, and the building official is not a party to the contract.

questions.question: A change order revises the paint finish requirements in Section 09 91 23. How does this modification relate to the original contract?

options.A: It replaces the entire original contract with a new contract
options.B: It creates a separate contract covering only the revised work
options.C: It interprets the contract but does not change any of its terms
options.D: It substitutes for part of the contract; the rest stays in effect

questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that modifying a contract changes the original by adding, deleting, or correcting portions, but the modification does not replace the whole contract; it typically substitutes for a part of it. It does not create a separate contract, and a change order revising paint requirements alters terms rather than merely interpreting them.

questions.question: During construction, the manufacturer discontinues the specified rooftop air-handling unit model, and the contractor proposes a different product. Which frequent reason for contract modifications does this represent?

options.A: Changes in the owner's requirements
options.B: Unforeseen field conditions
options.C: Changes in market conditions
options.D: Correction of errors or omissions

questions.explanation: Industry guidance lists changes in market conditions as a frequent reason for modifications, explicitly including specified products that are no longer available and new products offering price or other advantages. Changes in owner requirements, unforeseen field conditions, and correction of errors or omissions are separate categories that do not describe a discontinued product.

questions.question: Midway through construction, the city adopts an amended fire protection ordinance that took effect after the contract documents were issued, and the fire marshal now requires an added sprinkler zone. Which frequent reason for contract modifications does this represent?

options.A: Changes in code provisions or AHJ requirements
options.B: Correction of errors, omissions, or discrepancies
options.C: Unforeseen field conditions discovered in the work
options.D: Changes in market conditions affecting products

questions.explanation: Industry guidance names changes in regulatory code provisions or other requirements of authorities having jurisdiction as a distinct reason for modifications. Because the ordinance took effect after the documents were issued, they were not in error, so correction of errors or omissions does not fit, and nothing was uncovered in the field or caused by product availability.

questions.question: The owner decides to upgrade the lobby flooring and asks whether to initiate the change now, early in construction, or wait until the lobby work is about to begin. What is the main advantage of initiating it early?

options.A: It avoids the need for a signed change order and cost proposal
options.B: It allows time to weigh proposals and alternatives without delaying progress
options.C: It lets the A/E process the change as an addendum to the documents
options.D: It shifts the cost of the change into the contractor's own construction contingency

questions.explanation: Industry guidance advises issuing contract modifications in a timely, orderly way, noting that a change started early in construction leaves time to consider proposals and alternatives and reach a mutually acceptable change without disrupting progress. Early initiation does not eliminate the change order, convert the change into an addendum, or shift costs to the contractor.

questions.question: An A/E is preparing a change order that revises several specification sections and adjusts the contract sum based on a lengthy pricing proposal from the contractor. How can the change order document itself be kept concise?

options.A: State only the net change in contract sum and omit the supporting pricing
options.B: Describe the changes in the work and defer pricing to the next pay application
options.C: List only the affected section numbers and have the contractor infer the revisions
options.D: Refer to attachments that describe the changes and cost breakdowns in detail

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that contract modifications can usually stay concise by referring to attachments that describe the changes and the cost breakdowns in detail. Omitting the pricing support or deferring pricing leaves the sum adjustment undocumented, and bare section numbers leave the revisions undefined, so none of these keeps the record both concise and complete.

questions.question: Section 01 26 00 specifies the procedural requirements for initiating and processing modifications. With which documents must that section be closely coordinated?

options.A: The conditions of the contract and the agreement
options.B: The instructions to bidders and the bid/proposal form
options.C: Section 01 25 00 and Section 01 31 00
options.D: The drawings and the schedule of values

questions.explanation: Industry guidance places the procedural requirements for initiating and processing modifications in Section 01 26 00 and calls for that section to be closely coordinated with the conditions of the contract and the agreement. The instructions to bidders and bid form govern procurement, and other Division 01 sections, the drawings, and the schedule of values are not the documents industry guidance names.

questions.question: When describing the revisions in a contract modification, which method does industry guidance suggest the A/E may follow?

options.A: The format used for a submittal review transmittal
options.B: The layout of the original bid or proposal form
options.C: An approach similar to the one used for an addendum
options.D: A narrative style like a field observation report

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that modifications to the contract documents can be described in much the same way an addendum is, and its addenda format orders items by project manual and drawing sequence.
