questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that builder's risk covers the value of the construction but not the tools and equipment used to build it, and that mobile equipment such as cranes, bulldozers, backhoes, and forklifts is outside the contractor's automobile insurance, so general property and equipment insurance covers these assets against vandalism and work accidents. Equipment breakdown insurance addresses accidents to equipment such as boilers, transformers, and HVAC units.
questions.source: contractor’s general property and equipment insurance

questions.question: Which of these losses would the contractor's general property and equipment insurance typically cover?

options.A: Generators stolen from the contractor's laydown yard over a weekend
options.B: A backhoe on the site damaged by vandals over a weekend
options.C: A forklift drive train worn out from normal heavy use
options.D: Chillers installed in the project damaged by a fire

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says this insurance pays for tools and equipment damaged by vandalism or a work accident but does not cover theft or normal wear and tear, so the vandalized backhoe is covered while the stolen generators and worn drive train are not. Installed chillers are part of the work protected by builder's risk, which covers the construction's value rather than the contractor's equipment.
questions.source: contractor’s general property and equipment insurance

questions.question: A well-capitalized contractor objects to buying insurance on its construction tools and equipment. What alternative may the owner accept, and why does the owner care?

options.A: Adding the tools to builder's risk, since equipment losses raise the owner's premiums
options.B: Naming the owner an additional insured, since the owner could be sued for losses
options.C: A waiver of subrogation, since the owner's insurer might otherwise pursue the contractor
options.D: Proof of ability to replace them, since such losses can affect progress and quality

questions.explanation: Industry guidance recommends that the owner require insurance on the contractor's construction tools and equipment or a showing of the financial ability to replace them, because losing them can affect the progress and perhaps the quality of the work. Builder's risk does not cover the contractor's tools, and additional insured status and subrogation waivers deal with liability and recovery among parties rather than replacing equipment.
questions.source: contractor’s general property and equipment insurance

questions.question: A lightning-caused fire during construction pushes back the opening of a new retail center, and the owner loses projected rental income. Which coverage is designed for this loss, and how is it typically provided?

options.A: Loss-of-use coverage, purchased as a separate residential policy
options.B: Delayed completion coverage, as an endorsement to builder's risk
options.C: Business interruption coverage, under the owner's existing CGL policy
options.D: Equipment breakdown coverage, as an extension of the boiler policy

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says delayed completion coverage gives the same kind of protection as loss-of-use and business interruption but is limited to construction delays from the perils insured under builder's risk, so it is usually added to that policy as an endorsement or extension. Loss-of-use is associated with residences, business interruption responds when an operating business cannot conduct normal operations, and equipment breakdown covers accidents to equipment.
questions.source: Loss-of-Use, business interruption, and delayed completion insurance

questions.question: A fire in an occupied apartment building undergoing renovation forces tenants out of their units for several weeks. Which coverage is typically associated with the tenants' temporary housing, food, and moving costs?

options.A: Loss-of-use coverage
options.B: Business interruption coverage
options.C: Delayed completion coverage
options.D: Equipment breakdown coverage

questions.explanation: Industry guidance ties loss-of-use coverage to residential buildings such as homes and leased apartments, paying living expenses like temporary housing, food, and moving costs when a residence becomes uninhabitable from a covered event. Business interruption compensates a business for lost income and expenses, delayed completion is limited to construction delays from builder's risk perils, and equipment breakdown covers damage to equipment.
questions.source: Loss-of-Use, business interruption, and delayed completion insurance

questions.question: An owner's project uses AIA Document A101 Exhibit A, and the owner is weighing delayed completion insurance that would continue after the new facility opens. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: The contractor must buy it, and it may run past completion only by Change Order
options.B: The owner must buy it, and coverage must end at substantial completion
options.C: The owner may buy it at its option and may extend it past construction
options.D: The owner may buy it at its option, but it must end when construction ends

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that A101 Exhibit A lets the owner purchase and maintain delayed completion insurance at its option, and that the owner may carry it through construction and extend it for a period afterward because a new facility's performance is untested. Nothing makes it mandatory for either party, and nothing limits it to the construction period.
questions.source: Loss-of-Use, business interruption, and delayed completion insurance

questions.question: After paying the owner's fire loss in full, the owner's property insurer finds that the electrical contractor installed the transformer contrary to the manufacturer's instructions and sues the contractor. In what role is the insurer acting?

options.A: Indemnitee
options.B: Subrogee
options.C: Additional insured
options.D: Indemnitor

questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that once the loss is paid, the subrogation clause transfers the owner's rights against other parties to the insurer, which becomes a subrogee able to sue the contractor or engineer. An indemnitee is the party held harmless under a contract, an indemnitor is the party providing that protection, and an additional insured receives benefits under someone else's liability policy.

questions.question: To keep one party's insurance settlement from becoming another party's lawsuit midway through a project, what does current contract practice suggest?

options.A: All parties waive claims against one another to the extent covered by insurance
options.B: All parties waive all claims against one another regardless of insurance coverage
options.C: Each party names every other party as a named insured on its liability policies
options.D: The contractor gives the owner and A/E a broad form hold-harmless agreement

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says current practice is for all parties to waive claims against one another to the extent those claims are covered by insurance, so the right of subrogation never arises. A waiver regardless of insurance goes beyond what industry guidance describes, cross-naming parties as named insureds is not the suggested approach, and a broad form hold-harmless shifts liability between parties rather than preventing an insurer's recovery suit.

questions.question: The owner proposes a mutual waiver of subrogation among the owner, contractor, and A/E. What should each party do before accepting it?

options.A: Name the other two parties as additional insureds on its own policies
options.B: Obtain the surety's written consent, since the waiver affects the bonds
options.C: Confirm the waiver does not violate any term of its own insurance policies
options.D: Have the owner's insurance advisor certify the waiver in the supplementary conditions

questions.explanation: Industry guidance cautions that each party to the construction contract should check whether the waiver violates any term or condition of its own insurance policies, since the waiver keeps the right of subrogation from arising. Naming additional insureds, obtaining surety consent, and having the owner's advisor certify the waiver are not steps industry guidance identifies.

questions.question: An owner using AIA contract forms decides to implement an owner-controlled insurance program (OCIP) for a large commercial project. What must happen to the standard forms?

options.A: Nothing; A101 Exhibit A already includes an optional OCIP provision
options.B: They must be significantly modified with insurance and legal advice
options.C: Only the insurance amounts in the supplementary conditions change
options.D: They must be replaced with ConsensusDocs forms, which include CIPs

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that none of the standard AIA, EJCDC, or ConsensusDocs forms include controlled insurance programs, so using one requires significant modification of the forms under the advice of an insurance advisor and legal counsel. Neither the A101 exhibit nor ConsensusDocs provides a built-in CIP option, and the change goes far beyond filling in insurance amounts.

questions.question: A health system plans a series of clinic projects that will start and finish at staggered times over several years and wants a single consolidated insurance program. Which arrangement fits this situation?

options.A: A contractor-controlled program purchased for each clinic
options.B: A reporting form builder's risk policy for each clinic
options.C: A difference-in-conditions policy held by each contractor
options.D: A rolling wrap-up that clinics move into and out of

questions.explanation: Industry guidance describes a rolling wrap-up CIP for owners with multiple construction projects, letting each project be rolled into the program as it starts and out as it is completed. A separate contractor-controlled program per clinic defeats the single consolidated program, a reporting form is a builder's risk valuation method, and difference-in-conditions coverage fills gaps in an owner's builder's risk program.

questions.question: An owner of a small project is considering a controlled insurance program. What is the principal benefit for a project of that size, as distinct from the main advantage on large commercial projects?

options.A: Significant premium savings from consolidating coverage
options.B: Elimination of builder's risk from the project's coverage
options.C: Simplicity and a streamlined process for handling claims
options.D: Use of standard contract forms without any modification

questions.explanation: Industry guidance identifies cost savings as the most significant CIP advantage on large commercial projects, while smaller projects benefit from the program's simplicity and streamlined claims process. CIPs consolidate the required coverages rather than eliminating property coverage, and industry guidance says the standard forms must be significantly modified to use one.

questions.question: The A/E was named an additional insured on the contractor's CGL coverage. Later, the A/E is sued over a detailing error in its drawings. How does that coverage respond?

options.A: It defends the A/E, since additional insureds share the named insured's rights
options.B: It excludes the error; the A/E's own professional liability policy responds
options.C: It covers the error up to the each occurrence limit, after the A/E's deductible
options.D: It covers the error only if the owner is also named as an additional insured

questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that naming the A/E as an additional insured does not expand the contractor's policy; it extends benefits only for the contractor's operations, and the acts, errors, or omissions of the owner or A/E are not covered. Errors and omissions coverage must come from the A/E firm's own professional liability policy, so any option in which the contractor's CGL defends or pays for the design error is wrong.

questions.question: The 'shotgun lawsuit' phenomenon, in which injury from construction operations draws the owner and A/E into litigation, is the rationale for which contract requirement?

options.A: Naming the owner and A/E additional insureds under the contractor's liability coverage
options.B: Requiring the contractor to purchase a claims-made general liability policy for the owner
options.C: Requiring a mutual waiver of subrogation among the owner, the A/E, and the contractor
options.D: Requiring the owner to provide builder's risk insurance covering all parties' interests

questions.explanation: Industry guidance describes how injury from the contractor's operations can pull the owner and A/E into costly litigation even when they are not responsible, and responds that the contract documents should require both to be named additional insureds under the contractor's liability coverage. Subrogation waivers address insurers' recovery rights after a paid loss, and neither a claims-made form nor owner-provided builder's risk addresses third-party injury suits.

questions.question: When a liability policy designates a firm by name as an insured, what does industry guidance say that firm becomes entitled to for a covered occurrence?

options.A: Reimbursement of its own repair costs for defective work it performed
options.B: Coverage for its own professional errors and omissions in design
options.C: Payment of its own property losses, including tools and equipment
options.D: Legal defense of such claims and payment of damages on its behalf

questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that a named insured is entitled to a legal defense for covered claims and to the policy's payment of damages on its behalf for legal liability arising from a covered occurrence. A liability policy does not pay to repair the insured's own defective work, does not cover professional errors (that requires professional liability insurance), and does not insure the policyholder's own property such as tools and equipment.

questions.question: On a project using AIA documents, where does industry guidance say the project-specific insurance dollar amounts are entered?

options.A: In the supplementary conditions, as modifications to A201
options.B: In Division 01, in a section on contract requirements
options.C: In the instructions to bidders, with bid security amounts
options.D: In the exhibit attached to the owner-contractor agreement

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the standard general conditions contain no insurance dollar amounts and that the supplementary conditions are normally the proper place for them, except that with AIA documents the amounts are added to the exhibit to the owner-contractor agreement. Division 01 and the instructions to bidders are not where industry guidance places coverage amounts.

questions.question: The owner returns a completed EJCDC C-052 to the A/E, but the umbrella liability limits are left blank and one auto limit looks inconsistent with the rest. What should the A/E do?

options.A: Insert the limits used on the owner's previous project
options.B: Ask the A/E's own insurance carrier to recommend limits
options.C: Return the form to the owner for completion or clarification
options.D: Fill in the limits suggested in the EJCDC guidance documents

questions.explanation: Industry guidance directs the A/E to send an incomplete or apparently incorrect form back to the owner for clarification or completion rather than guessing the owner's intent. The A/E is not the owner's insurance advisor and its liability insurance does not cover specifying insurance information, so supplying amounts from a prior job, its own carrier, or published guidance would be inappropriate.

questions.question: A specifier wants the owner's bonds and insurance decisions, made with its insurance advisor, recorded on a standard form for transfer to the A/E. Which EJCDC document is recommended for this purpose?

options.A: C-051, Letter to Owner on Bonds and Insurance
options.B: C-052, Owner's Instructions Concerning Bonds and Insurance
options.C: C-800, Supplementary Conditions of the Construction Contract
options.D: C-700, Standard General Conditions of the Construction Contract

questions.explanation: Industry guidance recommends EJCDC C-052, Owner's Instructions Concerning Bonds and Insurance for Construction, as the form documenting the owner's insurance information for the A/E, while EJCDC C-051 is a prototype letter the A/E can send to request that information. C-700 and C-800 are the general and supplementary conditions into which the information eventually flows, not the owner's instruction form.

questions.question: A draft owner-contractor agreement requires the contractor to hold the owner harmless even for suits based solely on the owner's own negligence. What type of clause is this, and what caution applies?

options.A: Broad form; such clauses are unenforceable in a number of states
options.B: Limited form; it protects the owner only when vicariously liable
options.C: Intermediate form; it applies only where both parties are negligent
options.D: Contractual liability form; it requires an owner's protective policy

questions.explanation: The glossary defines a broad form hold-harmless as one in which Party A holds Party B harmless even for B's sole negligence, and notes that broad form agreements are unenforceable in a number of states. The limited form covers only A's sole negligence, and the intermediate form covers A's sole negligence or the joint negligence of both parties.

questions.question: The owner will carry its own builder's risk program, and the general contractor wants protection against coverage gaps that program may leave. What policy does the contractor maintain for this purpose?

options.A: Owner's and contractor's protective policy
options.B: Installation floater on contractor property
options.C: All risks, difference-in-conditions policy
options.D: Reporting form builder's risk coverage

questions.explanation: The glossary defines an all risks, difference-in-conditions policy as one a general contractor or subcontractor maintains to fill gaps created when the owner, or the general contractor, carries its own builder's risk program. OCP covers the owner's liability for a contractor's work, an installation floater covers property being installed, and the reporting form is a builder's risk valuation method.

questions.question: A contractor with employees working on a project in Ohio must provide workers' compensation coverage. How is that coverage obtained in Ohio?

options.A: From the compulsory state fund, or as a self-insurer where allowed
options.B: From any licensed private carrier, using an other states endorsement
options.C: Through an owner-controlled program that wraps all project workers
options.D: Through the federal Longshore and Harbor Workers program

questions.explanation: The glossary lists North Dakota, Ohio, Washington, and Wyoming as monopolistic fund states, where an employer must obtain workers' compensation from a compulsory state fund or qualify as a self-insurer (allowed in two of them). Private carriers and wrap-up programs are not the route the glossary describes for these states, and the Longshoremen and Harbor Workers Act applies to maritime employment.

questions.question: Industry guidance names fire sprinkler systems, curtain walls, and sophisticated exterior claddings as building components the A/E often does not fully design or engineer. What primary reason does it give for delegating their design?

options.A: Their design is usually reserved to the authority having jurisdiction under a separate building permit
options.B: Their unique requirements are known mainly to the manufacturer, which routinely engineers the attachment
options.C: Their design typically falls outside the coverage of most A/E professional liability insurance policies
options.D: Their design must be completed by a separate prime contractor whom the owner retains directly

questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that these components are delegated because only the product manufacturer is familiar with their unique design requirements, or because designing and engineering the attachment to the facility is part of the manufacturer's normal service. Nothing in the text ties delegation to AHJ permitting, insurance exclusions, or an owner-held prime contract; the responsibility is assigned to the contractor through the specification section.
questions.source: delegated design and engineering as a part of submittals

questions.question: A specifier is writing a glazed aluminum curtain wall section in which anchorage design is delegated to the contractor's licensed professional. Per SectionFormat, where should the loads and other design parameters that professional must satisfy be specified?

options.A: In PART 1, within the Delegated Design Submittals article that describes the submittal
options.B: In PART 1, within the Quality Assurance article that lists the professional's qualifications
options.C: In PART 2, within the appropriate product articles such as Performance/Design Criteria
options.D: In PART 3, within the Installation article that governs the anchorage work itself

questions.explanation: The SectionFormat commentary says the Delegated Design Submittals article should describe only what the submittals are, without repeating the design criteria, which belong in the appropriate PART 2 articles, or the professional's qualifications, which belong under Quality Assurance. It also reserves the term Design Criteria for characteristics of a product whose design is assigned to the contractor. PART 3 installation articles cover execution, not design criteria.

questions.question: Under a delegated-design requirement, the curtain wall supplier's engineer prepares anchorage drawings and engineering calculations. How are these documents handled?

options.A: Sent through the contractor and reviewed by the contractor and A/E as a normal submittal
options.B: Sent by the supplier directly to the A/E's structural consultant, who seals them for permit
options.C: Filed with the authority having jurisdiction, with a copy sent to the A/E for its records
options.D: Delivered to the owner, who forwards them to the A/E along with the closeout documents

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the manufacturer or subcontractor answers a delegated-design requirement by submitting drawings and engineering calculations or certifications through the contractor, and both the contractor and the A/E review them as they would any typical submittal. Bypassing the contractor, routing the documents only to the AHJ, or deferring them to closeout would break the submittal chain the specification sets up.
questions.source: delegated design and engineering as a part of submittals

questions.question: Schedules placed within a specification section are conventionally located in:

options.A: PART 3 — EXECUTION
options.B: PART 1 — GENERAL
options.C: An appendix at the back of the project manual
options.D: PART 2 — PRODUCTS

questions.explanation: By convention, a schedule belongs at the very end of PART 3 — EXECUTION. It isn't really execution content, but placing it there gives it a consistent, easy-to-find home within the section.

questions.question: The specific-product example for ductile iron pipe cites two ANSI/AWWA designations. Which pair correctly matches the example?

options.A: ASTM A21.50 and ASTM A21.51 for ductile-iron pipe and its fittings
options.B: ANSI A117.1 and ANSI/AWI 0641 for the pipe's thickness and joints
options.C: ASCE/SEI 7 and ACI 350 for the pipe's loads and liquid containment
options.D: ANSI/AWWA C150/A21.50 and ANSI/AWWA C151/A21.51 for the pipe

questions.explanation: The ductile iron pipe example is identified by the designations ANSI/AWWA C150/A21.50 and ANSI/AWWA C151/A21.51. The other pairs substitute real but unrelated designations for accessibility, woodwork, structural loads, or concrete.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the document types typically available on a manufacturer's website?

options.A: Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) together with the products written installation instructions
options.B: Evaluation service reports and the product's published test reports
options.C: The authority having jurisdiction's signed building permit for the project
options.D: Building information model (BIM) objects and drawing-detail files

questions.explanation: Manufacturer sites typically offer catalogs, datasheets, installation instructions, SDSs, EPDs, HPDs, test and evaluation reports, BIM objects and details, guide specs, representative contacts, and continuing-education materials. A signed project building permit comes from the AHJ, not the manufacturer's website.

questions.question: Stating 'as required by code' in a specification is INADEQUATE because the specifier should instead:

options.A: Reference only the model-code title and let the contractor research the value
options.B: Defer the requirement to the AHJ to set during the building permit review
options.C: Identify the specific requirement, such as a particular R-value rather than a citation
options.D: Direct the manufacturer to certify whatever R-value the installed product happens to achieve

questions.explanation: 'As required by code' leaves the actual requirement unstated. The specifier should spell out the specific value — for insulation, a particular R-value — rather than just pointing at the code and leaving others to look it up.

questions.question: A design team selects a costlier thermal insulation for a building the owner will keep 10 years, justifying it because the better-insulated envelope:

options.A: Eliminates the need for any HVAC equipment in the conditioned spaces
options.B: Lowers the product's first cost below that of the competing insulations
options.C: It is mandated outright by the energy codes minimum prescriptive R-value table for walls
options.D: Allows a smaller HVAC unit and notable operating savings over the period

questions.explanation: The pricier insulation improves the envelope enough to permit a smaller, less costly HVAC unit and to deliver meaningful operating savings across the 10-year ownership. That is a life-cycle justification, not a first-cost one.

questions.question: When a design team is told simply to select the 'best' product, the guidance is that 'best' must be judged by:

options.A: The product with the single highest durability rating available
options.B: The priorities the owner has established for the project
options.C: The lowest first cost among the otherwise comparable products
options.D: The option the product representative recommends most strongly

questions.explanation: 'Best' is not a fixed quality — it can mean most durable, most available, or most economical depending on the situation. The team should define it according to the priorities the owner has set, rather than defaulting to durability, price, or a representative's recommendation.

questions.question: Wind load calculations for evaluating product suitability are typically performed in accordance with which referenced design document?

options.A: ACI 350 for environmental concrete structures
options.B: ANSI/AWWA C150 for ductile-iron pipe thickness
options.C: ASCE/SEI Standard 7 for minimum design loads
options.D: ASTM E84 for surface burning characteristics

questions.explanation: Wind loads used to judge product suitability are calculated using ASCE/SEI Standard 7, the minimum design loads standard. The other options govern unrelated subjects — concrete liquid-containment structures, ductile-iron pipe, and surface burning characteristics.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a project condition affecting product suitability?

options.A: Seismic risks
options.B: Exposure to corrosive gases
options.C: Project bid procurement method
options.D: Humidity and atmospheric pressure

questions.explanation: Suitability is judged against the physical conditions a product will face — things like temperature, humidity, wind, seismic activity, atmospheric pressure, and exposure to corrosive gases. How the project is bid and procured is a contracting decision, not a physical condition affecting whether a product performs.

questions.question: Why must manufacturer guide specifications be reviewed carefully by the A/E?

options.A: They can carry a bias toward one product and might state information inaccurately
options.B: They are copyrighted documents and can never be edited for a project
options.C: They are usually not arranged in the project manuals MasterFormat section numbering order
options.D: They are issued only in metric units rather than the project's units

questions.explanation: A manufacturer's guide specification is written to favor that manufacturer's product, so it can be slanted and may not present every requirement accurately. The A/E has to scrutinize it for that bias and for correctness before adapting it.

questions.question: When the A/E begins product research, the product representative is often consulted to:

options.A: Determine product details and product viability
options.B: Negotiate the project's construction budget
options.C: Issue code interpretations on behalf of the AHJ
options.D: Approve construction submittals

questions.explanation: Early in research, the A/E commonly turns to the product representative to pin down product specifics and confirm whether a given product is a workable fit. Representatives don't set budgets, interpret code for the AHJ, or approve submittals.

questions.question: How should a reference standard normally be incorporated into specifications?

options.A: By citing the standard's developer name, designation number, and title
options.B: By paraphrasing the standard's requirements in the A/E's own wording
options.C: By attaching the full standard as a numbered project-manual appendix
options.D: By copying the standards full text verbatim into the Part 2 articles of the section

questions.explanation: A standard is brought into a specification by pointing to it — naming its developing organization along with its designation number, title, or commonly used identifier. The full text is usually protected by copyright, so it is referenced rather than reproduced or paraphrased.

questions.question: When evaluating a product's fitness for a specific use, the FIRST step is typically to:

options.A: Contact the product manufacturer to request a physical product sample
options.B: Confirm that the product's first cost is within the project's set budget
options.C: Identify the project-specific performance and code requirements the product must meet
options.D: Check several competing product offerings that satisfy the very same generic product type

questions.explanation: Before a product can be judged fit for use, you have to know what it is being judged against. The first step is establishing the project-specific performance and code requirements; only then can any product be measured against them.

questions.question: In project delivery practice, the '4 Cs of effective project communication' are:

options.A: Concept, Construct, Confirm, Closeout
options.B: Clear, Concise, Correct, Complete
options.C: Communicate, Coordinate, Confirm, Compile
options.D: Clarify, Critique, Cooperate, Commit

questions.explanation: Effective project communication is summarized as four qualities, each starting with C: clear, concise, correct, and complete. Every communication — an RFI, a submittal, an addendum, a letter — should exhibit all four.

questions.question: An A/E is at the start of researching a wall-cladding system and has only the project's performance and design criteria in hand. In the standard sequence, what must be done BEFORE specific products can be researched and compared?

options.A: Request the AHJ's interpretation of how the building code applies to the assembly
options.B: Compile a preliminary list of named products and manufacturers that comply
options.C: Obtain budgetary quotes from at least three competing manufacturers for the estimate
options.D: Identify a generic product type that satisfies the design criteria and conditions

questions.explanation: Research moves from general to specific. The A/E must first settle on a generic product type that meets the design criteria and project conditions; only after that can named products be gathered and compared. Building a candidate list or collecting quotes are later steps, and an AHJ interpretation is not part of defining the generic type.

questions.question: Which description is a GENERIC product rather than a specific product?

options.A: Ductile iron pipe, 8-inch diameter, pressure class 150, with interior cement lining
options.B: Ductile iron pipe with restrained push-on joints per ANSI/AWWA C150/A21.50
options.C: Ductile iron pipe complying with ANSI/AWWA C151/A21.51 with exterior asphaltic coating
options.D: Ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main

questions.explanation: A generic description identifies only the product class and its use, such as ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main. The other choices are specific: they pin down diameter, pressure class, coatings, joint type, and standard designations, which is exactly what distinguishes a specific product from a generic one.

questions.question: A junior specifier pulls product data from a printed manufacturer catalog kept in the office library. The PRINCIPAL risk of that printed source is that it:

options.A: Cannot legally be cited because the catalog text is copyrighted by the maker
options.B: Is organized by trade name rather than by the project's MasterFormat numbers
options.C: Can contain inaccurate product data if it is not the most recent version
options.D: Omits Safety Data Sheets that might be required for the project's materials

questions.explanation: A printed catalog reflects only what was current when it was printed. If it isn't the manufacturer's latest version, the product data it shows may be out of date and inaccurate. That obsolescence risk — not copyright, organization, or missing SDSs — is the main concern with printed sources.

questions.question: During design, the team summarizes manufacturer product quotes primarily to:

options.A: Lock the contractor into a single manufacturer for each product
options.B: Satisfy the AHJ's permit-submittal requirements
options.C: Aid with estimating the project construction cost
options.D: Establish the warranty terms that will be enforced during construction

questions.explanation: Pulling together product quotes during design is a budgeting exercise — it helps the team estimate the project's construction cost. The quotes are not a way to sole-source a manufacturer, satisfy permit requirements, or fix warranty terms.

questions.question: Some online sources make finding construction product manufacturers easier by building online catalogs. These online catalogs are typically organized according to:

options.A: The AHJ's permit-classification numbering system for the project type
options.B: Alphabetical manufacturer name regardless of the product's trade section
options.C: MasterFormat, with hyperlinks to the manufacturers' own websites
options.D: The Construction Specifications Institute's UniFormat assembly groupings

questions.explanation: Online catalogs that aggregate manufacturers are usually arranged by MasterFormat and link out to each manufacturer's own site. That work-results structure, not UniFormat, alphabetical name, or an AHJ permit scheme, is how they are organized.

questions.question: An owner's overriding goal is the lowest possible capital cost. A high-initial-cost product option would carry markedly lower installation and maintenance costs over the building's life. The A/E will TYPICALLY:

options.A: Specify the high-initial-cost option because its life cycle cost is lower
options.B: Specify basic product options
options.C: Specify a life cycle costing methodology in the contract documents
options.D: Defer the decision to the contractor after award

questions.explanation: When the owner's stated priority is the lowest up-front cost, the A/E typically specifies the basic product options. The tempting trap is to chase the lower life cycle cost of the pricier option, but here the controlling goal is low capital cost, so basic options win.

questions.question: A specification states 'insulation as required by code' for an exterior wall. Why is this WORDING inadequate?

options.A: Codes may not be cited in project specifications at all without the authority having jurisdiction's prior written permission
options.B: It improperly shifts responsibility for determining code compliance from the design professional to the contractor
options.C: Reference standards rather than the building code are what actually govern the thermal performance of the wall
options.D: It fails to indicate the specific requirement; it is better to identify a specific R-value than to reference the code

questions.explanation: A phrase like 'as required by code' never states the actual requirement, leaving it vague. The specifier should name the specific value — for an insulated wall, a particular R-value — rather than just pointing at the energy code and leaving readers to look it up.

questions.question: Which party must be cognizant of WHEN the next version of an applicable code becomes effective, according to the AHJ?

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The specifier
options.C: The product representative
options.D: The owner's facility manager

questions.explanation: Staying aware of when the AHJ's next code edition takes effect is the specifier's responsibility, ensuring the documents reference the correct edition.

questions.question: Wind load calculations for evaluating product suitability to project conditions are performed according to which referenced standard?

options.A: ANSI/AWWA C151/A21.51, Ductile-Iron Pipe, Centrifugally Cast, for Water
options.B: ASTM E84, Standard Test Method for Surface Burning Characteristics of Building Materials
options.C: ASCE/SEI Standard 7, Minimum Design Loads for Buildings and Other Structures
options.D: ACI 350, Code Requirements for Environmental Engineering Concrete Structures

questions.explanation: Wind loads are determined under ASCE/SEI Standard 7, the minimum design loads standard. The distractors cover different topics entirely — ACI 350 for liquid-containment concrete, ASTM E84 for surface burning, and ANSI/AWWA C151 for ductile iron pipe.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the project conditions for evaluating product suitability?

options.A: Atmospheric pressure at the product's installed location
options.B: Seismic risks present at the installed location on the site
options.C: Exposure to corrosive gases, chemicals, or contamination
options.D: The procurement and bid method selected for the project

questions.explanation: Suitability is evaluated against physical conditions — the installed location, temperature, humidity, wind and solar exposure, seismic risk, atmospheric pressure, corrosive exposure, interior versus exterior use, space limits, and frequency of use. How the project is procured and bid is a contracting matter, not a product-suitability condition.

questions.question: A manufacturer's guide spec states 'Flame Spread 25 / Smoke Developed 195 per ASTM E84,' while the building code accepts 'Flame Spread 25 / Smoke Developed 450 per ASTM E84.' The risk of copying the tighter manufacturer value into the project spec is that it:

options.A: Violates ASTM's copyright on the published E84 test-method document
options.B: Limits the comparable products that could otherwise be specified
options.C: It can automatically create a proprietary, no-substitution specification
options.D: Conflicts with the energy code that the AHJ has adopted for the project

questions.explanation: The manufacturer's smoke-developed value (195) is tighter than the code-acceptable value (450). Writing the tighter number into the spec narrows the field of products that could otherwise qualify. It is not a copyright problem, an automatic proprietary spec, or an energy-code conflict.

questions.question: When reviewing a manufacturer's guide specification, the decision on whether 'No Substitutions' applies should be made by:

options.A: The contractor after the contract is awarded
options.B: The manufacturer who prepared the guide specification
options.C: The product representative as the trusted advisor
options.D: The owner and the designer for the specific project

questions.explanation: Whether to allow substitutions is a project-by-project judgment that belongs to the owner and the designer, not to the manufacturer who wrote the guide spec, the representative, or the contractor.

questions.question: A manufacturer offers a guide specification to relieve the A/E from writing a section. These guide specifications must be reviewed carefully to determine if they:

options.A: Are written entirely in metric units rather than the project's inch-pound units
options.B: Conform to the latest MasterFormat section numbering used in the project manual
options.C: Were reviewed and approved in advance by the AHJ for use on the project
options.D: Carry a bias for one product and whether they state the necessary information

questions.explanation: A manufacturer's guide specification can favor its own product and may not capture every necessary requirement accurately, so the A/E must review it for that bias and for completeness. Units, section numbering, and AHJ pre-approval are not the stated review criteria.

questions.question: During the process of obtaining a code modification, a product representative can assist the A/E by:

options.A: Providing technical assistance and an equivalent product to meet code
options.B: Guaranteeing in writing that the AHJ will approve the modification request
options.C: Issuing the code modification directly on the AHJ's behalf for the project
options.D: Assuming the A/E's professional liability for the design that is modified

questions.explanation: A representative can help the A/E pursue a code modification by offering technical support and suggesting an equivalent product that helps satisfy the requirement. Representatives cannot grant modifications, promise AHJ approval, or take on the A/E's liability.

questions.question: Which of the following is an ECOLABEL used for quickly conveying a product's sustainability performance?

options.A: ASCE/SEI Standard 7 for minimum structural design loads
options.B: The International Building Code published by the ICC
options.C: ANSI/AWWA C151 for ductile-iron pipe manufacturing
options.D: Underwriters Laboratories' GREENGUARD certification

questions.explanation: UL's GREENGUARD is an ecolabel; other examples include CRI Green Label Plus, FSC chain-of-custody certification, and Green Seal. ASCE/SEI 7 and the IBC are structural and building requirements, and ANSI/AWWA C151 is a pipe standard — none of which are ecolabels.

questions.question: An A/E wants to verify that wood products on a project come from responsibly managed forests using a recognized ecolabel. Which program provides that chain-of-custody certification?

options.A: Carpet and Rug Institute's CRI Green Label Plus emissions certification
options.B: Forest Stewardship Council's FSC Chain of Custody Certification
options.C: Underwriters Laboratories' GREENGUARD low-chemical-emissions certification
options.D: Green Seal's environmental certification for building products and materials

questions.explanation: The FSC Chain of Custody Certification from the Forest Stewardship Council is the ecolabel tied to responsibly sourced wood. CRI Green Label Plus addresses carpet emissions, GREENGUARD addresses low chemical emissions, and Green Seal is a broad environmental label.

questions.question: An A/E compares three insulating glass units against two criteria. Visible Light Transmittance (VLT): A = 69%, B = 61%, C = 66%. Winter nighttime U-value: A = 0.47, B = 0.29, C = 0.32. Using a standard product-versus-criteria evaluation method, which product best satisfies BOTH 'high transparency' and 'best thermal resistance'?

options.A: Product A for transparency and Product B for thermal resistance
options.B: Product C for both criteria
options.C: Product B for transparency and Product C for thermal resistance
options.D: Product A for both criteria

questions.explanation: High transparency means the highest VLT, which is Product A at 69%. Best thermal resistance means the lowest U-value, which is Product B at 0.29. No single unit wins both, so the answer pairs A for transparency with B for thermal resistance.

questions.question: A carpet-tile spec requires a Cut Loop pile. The submittal lists the construction as 'Multi-Level Pattern Loop' (face weight and density otherwise meet the spec). Using a product-versus-criteria evaluation method, the submitted product:

options.A: Achieves the criteria, because its face weight and pile density both comply
options.B: Achieves the criteria, since pile-loop construction is an aesthetic preference
options.C: Does NOT achieve the criteria, since the specified Cut Loop pile is not provided
options.D: It cannot be judged on the pile loop until the carpet tile is installed and then inspected

questions.explanation: The spec calls for a Cut Loop pile, but the submittal offers Multi-Level Pattern Loop construction. Matching face weight and density doesn't satisfy the different pile-construction requirement, so the product does not meet the criteria.

questions.question: In a code-versus-standard classification exercise, NFPA 1 (Fire Code) and NFPA 13 (Sprinkler Systems) are best characterized, respectively, as a:

options.A: Code and a reference standard
options.B: Reference standard and a code
options.C: Code and a code
options.D: Reference standard and a reference standard

questions.explanation: NFPA 1 is a fire code, so it functions as a code. NFPA 13 is an installation standard for sprinkler systems that becomes enforceable when a code references it, making it a reference standard. So the pairing is code and reference standard.

questions.question: A design team is a few credits short of a HIGHER sustainability rating and the project must at least meet a state-required minimum. In this situation, the appropriate action is to:

options.A: Proceed without further action, because the project already meets the minimum credits
options.B: Find credits close to being achieved, weigh cost/availability/time, and inform the owner
options.C: Lower the project's target rating to the minimum credits to avoid the extra cost
options.D: Tell the owner that achieving the higher credit rating is simply unattainable on this project

questions.explanation: The team should look at credits it has not yet pursued, identify those nearly within reach, weigh the cost, availability, and time each would take, and then present those findings to the owner to decide. Doing nothing, lowering the target, or declaring it impossible skips that analysis.

questions.question: A specification for a concrete structure requires compliance with American Concrete Institute (ACI) 350. Citing ACI 350 predicts that the structure is suitable to:

options.A: Carry the minimum live loads tabulated for assembly occupancy floors
options.B: Resist the design wind loads that are computed under the ASCE/SEI Standard 7 limits
options.C: Achieve a one-hour fire-resistance rating verified by an ASTM E119 test
options.D: Convey, store, or treat environmental liquids such as water and wastewater

questions.explanation: ACI 350 governs environmental engineering concrete, so a structure built to it is suited to convey, store, or treat liquids such as water, wastewater, and non-hazardous solid wastes. Referencing the standard is how that suitability is conveyed.

questions.question: Among the advantages of reference standards, the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) contributes to 'reduced conflict and duplication' primarily by:

options.A: Coordinating standards development and adopting the standards of its accredited members
options.B: Writing and publishing the model building codes that jurisdictions then adopt
options.C: Testing finished construction products and certifying the companies that then install them
options.D: Enforcing reference standards as mandatory once a product has been selected

questions.explanation: ANSI cuts down on overlap and conflict by coordinating how standards are developed and by accrediting and promoting the standards produced by its members. It does not write codes, test or certify products, or enforce standards.

questions.question: The International Building Code (IBC), which sets minimum building-system regulations using prescriptive and performance conditions, is published by the:

options.A: American National Standards Institute (ANSI)
options.B: American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)
options.C: National Fire Protection Association (NFPA)
options.D: International Code Council (ICC)

questions.explanation: The IBC is published by the International Code Council and establishes minimum requirements for building systems using a combination of prescriptive and performance-related conditions.

questions.question: In a classification exercise (code, reference standard, or both), 'NFPA 13 - Sprinkler Systems' is best classified as a:

options.A: Code, since 'NFPA' titles are always enforced as adopted building codes
options.B: Reference standard, since it is an installation standard adopted by codes
options.C: Neither, since sprinkler requirements come only from the IBC's own text
options.D: Federal regulation, since fire protection is governed at the national level

questions.explanation: NFPA 13 is an installation standard for sprinkler systems that becomes enforceable once a code adopts it by reference, so it is a reference standard. The NFPA label alone does not make a document a code.

questions.question: In the same classification exercise, 'NFPA 1 - Fire Code' is best classified as a:

options.A: A reference standard that becomes codified only when a building code happens to cite it
options.B: Voluntary ecolabel applied to fire-protection products on packaging
options.C: Manufacturer guide specification published by a trade-association group
options.D: Code, because it is adopted and enforced as the jurisdiction's fire code

questions.explanation: NFPA 1 is a fire code that a jurisdiction adopts and enforces, so it is classified as a code. That sets it apart from NFPA 13, which is an installation reference standard.

questions.question: Among the examples of ecolabels, the 'CRI Green Label Plus' mark is managed by the:

options.A: Underwriters Laboratories (UL) product-testing organization
options.B: Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) chain-of-custody program
options.C: Green Seal, an independent nonprofit organization that certifies environmental performance
options.D: Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI), the carpet industry's trade group

questions.explanation: Green Label Plus is administered by the Carpet and Rug Institute, the carpet industry's trade group. UL runs GREENGUARD, FSC runs its chain-of-custody certification, and Green Seal is its own separate ecolabel.

questions.question: An A/E wants an ecolabel that verifies wood products come from responsibly managed forests. Among the standard ecolabel examples, the appropriate mark is:

options.A: Forest Stewardship Council's FSC Chain of Custody Certification
options.B: The Carpet and Rug Institute's CRI Green Label Plus
options.C: Green Seal's environmental product certification mark
options.D: Underwriters Laboratories GREENGUARD certification for low-emitting interior products

questions.explanation: The Forest Stewardship Council's FSC Chain of Custody Certification is the ecolabel addressing responsibly sourced wood. The other marks are genuine ecolabels but cover carpet emissions, low chemical emissions, or general environmental criteria instead.

questions.question: Code requires an insulated skylight glass unit to have a safety-glass inboard lite. Of three offered units - (A) 1/4-in annealed; (B) insulated unit with a laminated outboard and a 1/4-in annealed clear lite; (C) insulating unit of a 1/4-in annealed lite and a 1/4-in heat-strengthened lite - how many units satisfy the safety-glass inboard-lite requirement?

options.A: None of the units, because skylights require fully tempered glass on both lites
options.B: Exactly two units, because heat-strengthened glass would also count as safety glazing here
options.C: All three units, because any insulated glass unit qualifies as safety glazing
options.D: Exactly one unit, because only the laminated-glass unit qualifies as safety glazing

questions.explanation: Among the three units, only the one using laminated glass qualifies as safety glazing for the inboard lite. Annealed and heat-strengthened glass do not count as safety glazing, so exactly one unit meets the requirement.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a GENERIC product type that must be identified before specific products are researched?

options.A: 8-inch ductile iron pipe, pressure class 150, with restrained push-on joints
options.B: Ductile iron pipe complying with ANSI/AWWA C150/A21.50 and C151/A21.51
options.C: Cement-lined ductile iron pipe with an exterior asphaltic protective coating
options.D: Ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main, before any detailed selection

questions.explanation: The generic description names only the product class and use — ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main — and must be settled before detailed selection. The other choices add size, pressure class, coatings, linings, joint type, and standard designations, which makes them specific rather than generic.

questions.question: An owner has just conceived the project parameters for a new fire station. The A/E's work of researching the products, materials, and systems the project needs is expected to result in which set of outcomes?

options.A: Define the owner's program, set the construction budget, and choose the project delivery method
options.B: Choose products from suppliers, determine product requirements, and design to incorporate them
options.C: Prequalify suppliers, establish allowances for unselected products, and write substitution procedures
options.D: Evaluate proposed equivalents, approve contractor substitutions, and review product submittals

questions.explanation: Industry guidance places this step after the owner conceives the project parameters; its result is to select products from suppliers, determine product-related requirements, and develop a design that incorporates the selected products. Program, budget, and delivery method belong to the owner's project conception, not to this step. Allowances, substitution procedures, and substitution or submittal review are procurement and construction activities, not the stated result of research and selection.
questions.source: introduction to product research and selection

questions.question: A specifier is recording who shaped product choices on a laboratory project. Which pairing of participant and basis of influence correctly describes input to product selection?

options.A: Owner or contractor: system products, based on applicable code requirements
options.B: MEP designers: aesthetic products, based on successful previous projects
options.C: A/E: aesthetic products and manufacturers, from past projects and research
options.D: Product representative: the final selection, based on design team discussions

questions.explanation: The architect/engineer typically steers the choice of aesthetic products and their makers, drawing on research and on products that performed well on earlier jobs. Owners and contractors contribute supplier preferences grounded in their own past experience rather than in code requirements, and MEP designers shape selections within their own systems using codes and prior experience. A product representative does not make the final call; that decision rests with the A/E, either independently or after discussion with the team.

questions.question: A courthouse's contract documents require the contractor to list the products and manufacturers its bid is based on. When is this list furnished, and how complete is it typically?

options.A: With each bid; often covering only key products
options.B: With each bid; covering every product to be furnished
options.C: After award; often covering only key products
options.D: After award; covering every product to be furnished

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says that when the contract requires such a list, bidders must include it when they submit their bids, and that the list is often only for key products and is not all-inclusive. It is not deferred until after award, and it is not a complete inventory of every product to be furnished.

questions.question: A school was bid on performance-based specifications listing several acceptable HVAC products, and the documents did not require bidders to list their products. Before award, the owner asks which HVAC units the apparent low bidder priced. How can the A/E find out?

options.A: Require the bidder to file substitution requests for the HVAC units it priced
options.B: Issue an addendum requiring all bidders to identify the HVAC units they priced
options.C: Tell the owner this cannot be learned until construction-phase product submittals
options.D: Ask the bidder in a post-bid interview which units its bid was based on

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that the A/E may ask the bidder or proposer in a post-bid/proposal interview which products the bid was based on, so the owner need not wait until product information is submitted during construction. The units priced are among the acceptable products, so no substitution request applies, and addenda change the procurement documents before bids are opened, not after.

questions.question: A specialty resin terrazzo system meets every performance criterion for a rural county courthouse, but the nearest stock of the manufacturer's repair materials and its nearest factory service technicians are 900 miles away. In evaluating the product, this finding bears most directly on:

options.A: The availability of workers skilled in that installation technique locally
options.B: The product's availability months later, when the project is under construction
options.C: The availability and cost of maintenance supplies and maintenance services
options.D: Whether standard colors meet aesthetic standards or custom colors are needed

questions.explanation: Industry guidance directs the A/E to consider the availability and cost of maintenance supplies, and the cost and availability of maintenance services offered by the manufacturer, during product evaluation; distant repair stock and service technicians are that concern. Skilled-labor availability, a product's availability once construction starts, and standard versus custom colors are other 8.5 factors, but the facts in this scenario do not involve them.
questions.source: industry conditions and availability of products

questions.question: A specifier is choosing between a domestic and an imported manufacturer of chlorine feed equipment for a water treatment plant. Country of origin is a sourcing consideration because it can affect:

options.A: Delivery time, manufacturer longevity, financial stability, and track record
options.B: Testing, distribution network, local representatives, and sustainability certifications
options.C: Availability of parts, installed cost, operating cost, and maintenance cost
options.D: Delivery time, testing, the availability of parts, and warranty service

questions.explanation: Industry guidance lists country of origin (domestic vs. imported) as a sourcing factor that can affect delivery time, testing, availability of parts, and warranty service. Manufacturer longevity, financial stability and track record, distribution network and local representatives, and sustainability certifications are separate items on the same sourcing list, not effects of country of origin. Installed, operating, and maintenance costs come from the final-selection aspects.

questions.question: After selecting a roof membrane, the A/E turns to the research gathered during product evaluation. That research is used to develop which written documents detailing the product's technical aspects?

options.A: Shop drawings, product data, and samples submitted for the A/E's review
options.B: Preliminary project descriptions, design narratives, or specifications
options.C: Manufacturer datasheets, product drawings, and budgetary quotes
options.D: Life-cycle cost analyses, value analysis reports, or bid forms

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says that after a product is selected, the A/E uses the research from product evaluation to develop written documents (preliminary project descriptions, design narratives, or specifications) detailing its technical aspects. Datasheets, product drawings, and quotes are information collected as inputs during research. Shop drawings, product data, and samples are construction submittals, and life-cycle cost analyses, value analysis reports, and bid forms are not among the documents industry guidance names.

questions.question: Which document section should typically govern the procedures for evaluating substitution requests?

options.A: The Conditions of the Contract, taken on their own
options.B: Division 00 procurement requirements issued for bidding
options.C: The applicable technical specification section for the product
options.D: Division 01 General Requirements, Section 01 25 00

questions.explanation: Substitution procedures are administered out of Division 01, most often through Section 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures, which sets out how requests are made and evaluated.

questions.question: A contractor submits a substitution request after the bid date. What is the A/E's primary obligation when evaluating it?

options.A: Forward salient characteristics to the manufacturer for its approval of equivalency
options.B: Determine whether the proposed product is equivalent in salient characteristics
options.C: Accept it as equivalent if its quoted price is lower than the specified product
options.D: Reject it because salient characteristics cannot be evaluated after the bid date

questions.explanation: The core of any substitution review is judging whether the offered product matches the specified one in its defining (salient) characteristics. The A/E performs that comparison; equivalency is not delegated to the manufacturer, and price alone never establishes it.

questions.question: In a design-build project where the design-builder hires the contractor, which procurement option is most commonly used?

options.A: The competitive-bid option, awarded to the low responsive bid
options.B: The competitive-proposal option, scored on stated criteria
options.C: The sealed-proposal option, opened publicly at a fixed time
options.D: The negotiation option, with a contractor they already know

questions.explanation: Design-builders most often select construction partners by negotiation, since they tend to engage firms with whom they have an existing working relationship rather than opening the work to competitive bidding.

questions.question: ASTM C150 covers ten cement types as embedded options. If the A/E does not specify the type, the consequence is that:

options.A: The authority having jurisdiction selects the cement type during permit review
options.B: The specification is rendered void for ambiguity until a type is designated
options.C: The selection passes to the contractor, who picks the cheapest of the options
options.D: The most stringent of the available cement types automatically applies instead

questions.explanation: ASTM C150's several cement types are options embedded in the standard. Leaving the type unspecified hands the choice to the contractor, who can be expected to select the least costly one.

questions.question: An owner requires a force-main system to withstand at least 250 psi. Because seals cannot be confirmed by visual inspection during design, the owner's assurance of compliance depends on:

options.A: The manufacturer's marketing literature describing the product line capabilities
options.B: A post-bid substitution request submitted by the contractor for the seal parts
options.C: Testing and code-required certifications showing compliance product to product
options.D: The architect/engineer's visual examination of a representative design sample

questions.explanation: A safety-critical feature like a 250-psi seal cannot be judged by eye. It must be evaluated and tested, with code-required certifications giving the assurance that compliance holds consistently from one product to the next.

questions.question: An owner wants a single point of cost responsibility but also wants the constructor's input during design without yet committing to a fixed lump sum. Which method and risk posture fits BEST?

options.A: Design-bid-build, where the constructor's price risk is fixed only at the bid opening
options.B: CM-as-agent, where the agent advises the owner but holds none of the cost risk
options.C: Multiple-prime, where each separate prime carries the cost risk for only its scope
options.D: CMAR, where the manager joins in design and later converts its input into a GMP

questions.explanation: CMAR provides preconstruction input plus one accountable party that later takes on cost risk through a guaranteed maximum price. A CM-agent carries no cost risk, and DBB fixes price only at bid opening.

questions.question: Under design-build delivery, design errors that surface during construction are MOST directly the financial responsibility of:

options.A: The owner, because the owner accepted the design at the bridging-documents stage
options.B: The A/E of record, under a separate prime agreement held with the project owner
options.C: The surety, which steps in to fund any design-related rework once a claim is filed
options.D: The design-builder, who holds both the design and the construction obligations

questions.explanation: In design-build a single entity is responsible for both design and construction, so the risk at the design/construction interface — including design errors found during construction — rests with the design-builder rather than being split as in DBB.

questions.question: A product meets a model code's 15-pound operating-force limit but exceeds a local jurisdiction's 5-pound limit for the same door. For counting compliant products, the governing figure is:

options.A: The 15-pound model-code value, since the model code is the more widely adopted document
options.B: Either limit at the A/E's discretion, because both are recognized consensus requirements
options.C: The 5-pound local value, as the more stringent of the two overlapping force requirements
options.D: Neither limit, because operating-force values do not bear on a product-compliance count

questions.explanation: When overlapping requirements differ, the stricter one governs. The 5-pound local limit is tighter, so only products that meet it count as compliant.

questions.question: Regarding time limits, the warranty provisions in standard AIA, EJCDC, and ConsensusDocs general conditions are correctly characterized as:

options.A: Fixed at exactly one year in every single case, mirroring the federal FAR warranty limitation
options.B: Carrying no stated time limitation, with duration set by project location and governing law
options.C: Fixed at two years in each document, running from the date of substantial completion
options.D: Expiring automatically on the date the owner takes beneficial occupancy of the project

questions.explanation: These standard general warranties state no time limit of their own; how long they run depends on the project's location and the law governing the contract.

questions.question: A section names a basis-of-design product and allows comparable products. A contractor proposes an equal whose different mounting depth would require rework of an adjacent assembly by another trade. The substitution provisions should make clear that:

options.A: the proposing contractor bears the cost of resulting changes to other work and coordination
options.B: the owner absorbs the redesign cost because the basis-of-design product created the conflict
options.C: the A/E must accept any product meeting the named product's published catalog cut sheet
options.D: adjacent-trade impacts are disregarded once the product meets the salient characteristics

questions.explanation: Substitution provisions put the burden on the party proposing the substitution both to show equivalence and to pay for any resulting changes to other work, redesign, and coordination. Meeting the salient characteristics is necessary but does not erase impacts on adjacent trades.

questions.question: Why should drawings avoid cross-references such as 'refer to specifications'?

options.A: Drawings and specs are complementary, so broad cross-references are discouraged
options.B: Drawings may not legally cross-reference any other contract document at all
options.C: Such cross-references are confidential and must be withheld from the contractor
options.D: Cross-references imply the specs take legal precedence over the drawings

questions.explanation: Drawings and specifications complement each other within one contract set, so sweeping pointers like 'see specifications' add little and are discouraged. Citing a specific section number, however, is acceptable.

questions.question: Why should equipment such as pumps or valves be identified on drawings by short generic names or codes (e.g., 'PRV-1')?

options.A: To satisfy MasterFormat section-numbering rules that apply to drawings
options.B: To simplify drawing changes by keeping descriptions in the specs
options.C: To assist the AHJ in enforcing code provisions during the plan review
options.D: To prevent contractors from proposing any unauthorized substitutions

questions.explanation: Short codes and symbols keep the detailed descriptions in the specifications, so if a product changes, fewer edits are needed on the drawings themselves.

questions.question: An A/E discovers that the manufacturer's roof warranty excludes damage from winds at 55 mph peak gust, but the code requires design for 70 mph sustained / 85 mph gust. What should the A/E do?

options.A: Accept the warranty as written, since the manufacturer's terms govern
options.B: Reduce the code-required wind design to match the warranty limit
options.C: Require the warranty be modified to meet code or select another product
options.D: Issue an addendum reducing the project's specified design wind loads instead

questions.explanation: Warranty limits have to be checked against code-required performance. A warranty that caps coverage below the code-mandated wind load is unacceptable, so the A/E must have it revised to meet code or choose a different product.

questions.question: MasterFormat division and section titles are intended to:

options.A: Assign scope of work to specific trade subcontractors on the project
options.B: Organize specification information, not to assign work to trades
options.C: Assign work to specific construction trades performing the labor
options.D: Establish the required construction sequence among the trades

questions.explanation: MasterFormat exists to organize how specification content is arranged. It is not a tool for dividing scope among trades, and subcontractor boundaries should not dictate how sections are structured.

questions.question: Which factor most directly establishes price parameters for product selection during value analysis?

options.A: The AHJ inspection schedule that is set for the project's review
options.B: The trade affiliation of the installer doing the work
options.C: The MasterFormat section title assigned to the product
options.D: Budget requirements and the product's maintenance costs

questions.explanation: The project budget together with a product's expected maintenance costs is what sets the price boundaries that guide selection during value analysis.

questions.question: ASTM C150 covers ten cement types. If the A/E does not specify the type, the selection is:

options.A: Made by the AHJ, which selects the cement type during the plan review
options.B: Determined by the testing laboratory based on its field sampling
options.C: Forfeited to the contractor, who tends to pick the cheapest type
options.D: Defaulted to Type I, which ASTM C150 designates as the standard

questions.explanation: When a standard contains internal options (such as the several cement types in ASTM C150), the A/E must pin down the choice. Leaving it open hands the decision to the contractor, who will usually take the least costly option.

questions.question: Which factor is LEAST appropriate as a basis for accepting a value-engineering substitution?

options.A: A lower purchase price even though it adds project coordination cost
options.B: Equivalent specified performance achieved at a measurably lower first cost
options.C: Equal aesthetic result with measurably reduced long-term maintenance cost
options.D: Comparable quality and performance with a shorter delivery lead time

questions.explanation: A cheaper price by itself cannot justify a product that no longer meets the required performance. Sound value analysis weighs quality, performance, budget, and schedule together, so a savings offset by added coordination cost is the weakest basis for acceptance.

questions.question: In value analysis, the 'value' of a building element is best understood as the relationship between:

options.A: The contractor’s profit margin and the initial purchase price
options.B: The function or performance it delivers and the life cycle cost to achieve that function
options.C: Its aesthetic appeal and the owner’s personal preference
options.D: The construction schedule duration and the labor hours required

questions.explanation: Value analysis improves value by maximizing the ratio of function (the performance an element must deliver) to the life cycle cost of providing it. The goal is the lowest total cost of ownership that still meets the required function—not the lowest first cost, and not aesthetics or schedule in isolation.
questions.source: value analysis and life cycle cost

questions.question: Which warranty term is generally the LEAST reliable basis for comparing two warranties?

options.A: Duration alone
options.B: Exclusions and limitations
options.C: Manufacturer's financial backing
options.D: Whether labor is covered

questions.explanation: Length of coverage is the term people compare most, yet it may matter least. Looking only at duration gives no way to weed out weaker coverage hidden in exclusions, conditions, or labor terms.

questions.question: Considering how project decisions affect total project cost over time, the ability to influence cost is GREATEST during which phase?

options.A: Bidding and the procurement phase of project work
options.B: Programming and the schematic design phase
options.C: Construction documents production phase
options.D: Construction phase, on the building site

questions.explanation: The leverage a decision has over total project cost is highest at the very start and drops off steeply as work proceeds. The earliest phases (programming and schematic design) are where choices shape outcomes most, while later changes cost far more to make.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, how should each prime contractor's scope be delineated graphically versus in writing?

options.A: Both the graphic limits and the binding scope wording appear on the drawings
options.B: Graphics may show separate contracts, but scope belongs in Div 01 and PART 1
options.C: Scope is fixed only by MasterFormat section titles, controlling trade work
options.D: Each prime marks its own scope limits on an independent record drawing set

questions.explanation: Drawings can show the limits of separate contracts graphically, but the binding written scope-of-work language belongs in Division 01 and in the PART 1 - GENERAL portion of the specification sections.

questions.question: An owner wants single-point construction-cost responsibility via a guaranteed maximum price while still getting major-trade input during design. Which method provides this and how?

options.A: CM as advisor, where the advisor binds the owner to the negotiated GMP
options.B: CMAR, where the manager holds the risk and gives a GMP after design input
options.C: Design-bid-build competitive bid, where the low bid becomes the fixed sum
options.D: Multiple-prime, where each prime guarantees a maximum price for its scope

questions.explanation: CMAR fits because the at-risk manager participates during design and then provides a guaranteed maximum price, giving the owner a single accountable party for cost. A CM-Advisor cannot bind the owner, and DBB sets price only after the documents are complete.

questions.question: Under the CM-Agent method, which is NOT a characteristic of the construction manager's position?

options.A: Guaranteeing and being directly responsible for delays and cost overruns
options.B: Acting as the owner's agent, with authority defined by the owner agreement
options.C: Entering into agreements only with the owner, not with any contractors
options.D: Making and rendering decisions binding on the owner within delegated limits

questions.explanation: A CM-Agent does not guarantee construction outcomes or bear direct responsibility for delays, overruns, and defects. It serves as the owner's agent, contracts only with the owner, and binds the owner within its delegated authority — so the guarantee of delays and overruns is the trait that does not fit.

questions.question: A contractor providing design-assist services and ultimately presenting a guaranteed maximum price during design is most characteristic of which arrangement?

options.A: The design-bid-build competitive bid option, in which price is fixed by sealed low bid
options.B: Multiple-prime delivery, in which the owner separately contracts each defined scope of work
options.C: Owner-build (force-account) delivery, in which the owner supplies its own construction labor
options.D: The design-bid-build negotiation option or CMAR, pricing incomplete information toward a GMP

questions.explanation: Having a contractor assist the A/E, price still-incomplete information, and offer a guaranteed maximum price is the hallmark of the negotiated DBB option, and design-assist with a GMP is likewise central to CMAR.

questions.question: A design-bid-build project switches from the competitive bid option to the competitive proposal option. How does Division 00 most accurately change?

options.A: Equivalent proposal forms and documents replace the bidding forms and documents
options.B: Many of the forms and documents in the procurement requirements become needless
options.C: Division 00 does not change in any significant way under these circumstances
options.D: Division 00 is replaced entirely by the Division 01 general-requirements set

questions.explanation: Moving to the proposal option means the bidding forms and documents in Division 00 give way to their proposal-based equivalents, rather than disappearing or being replaced by Division 01.
