questions.question: For a design-bid-build project procured under the competitive proposal option, which group of optional MasterFormat titles does industry guidance identify as applicable to that process?

options.A: Advertisement for Bids, Instructions to Bidders, and Bid Security Form
options.B: Request for Proposal, Instructions to Bidders, and Bid Form
options.C: Request for Proposal, Request for Qualifications, and Instructions to Proposers
options.D: Request for Proposal, Instructions to Proposers, and Notice of Award

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that MasterFormat includes optional titles suited to competitive proposals: Request for Proposal, Request for Qualifications, and Instructions to Proposers. The other sets either rely on bid-oriented titles such as Advertisement for Bids, Instructions to Bidders, Bid Form, and bid security, or substitute Notice of Award, a contracting form that industry guidance does not name among the proposal-process titles.

questions.question: An owner questions why the project manual for a competitive proposal procurement should include Instructions to Proposers when no formal bid opening will occur. Which benefit does industry guidance cite for including such documents?

options.A: They set procedures for clarifications, addenda, and a structured proposal form
options.B: They set the contract sum, retainage, and the payment application procedures
options.C: They stand in for the conditions of the contract during the negotiation period
options.D: They remove the need to issue any addenda during the proposal period

questions.explanation: Industry guidance explains that including documents such as Instructions to Proposers improves the proposal process by setting procedures for clarifications, addenda, and a structured proposal form. They do not set the contract sum or retainage, which are agreement matters, they do not stand in for the conditions of the contract, and they make addenda more orderly rather than unnecessary.

questions.question: While drafting Instructions to Proposers for a competitive proposal project, a specifier considers requiring each proposer to affirm that it visited the site and accounted for local conditions. What does industry guidance indicate?

options.A: Such a requirement is inappropriate, since site affirmations apply only to competitive bids
options.B: Such a requirement belongs only in the owner-contractor agreement after negotiations end
options.C: Such a requirement is appropriate, since it can mirror a traditional bid requirement
options.D: Such a requirement belongs in the Division 01 summary of work rather than in procurement

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that proposal-process procurement requirements can be similar to those of a traditional bid, giving the example of having the proposer affirm a site visit and consideration of local conditions. The affirmation is therefore not limited to competitive bids, and it is a procurement requirement rather than an agreement or Division 01 provision.

questions.question: On a design-bid-build project using the negotiated option, the owner negotiates the contract sum directly with the contractor and the A/E does not take part. What should the A/E do regarding the owner-contractor agreement form?

options.A: Prepare the agreement form and insert the negotiated amount once the owner reports it
options.B: Exclude the agreement from review, since the A/E was not a party to the negotiations
options.C: Wait until after award and then revise the conditions of the contract to match it
options.D: Request a copy to confirm it does not conflict with the conditions or Division 01

questions.explanation: Even when the A/E does not take part in negotiating the agreement, industry guidance says the A/E should ask for a copy of the agreement form to check for conflicts with the conditions of the contract and Division 01. Preparing the form or inserting the amount is not assigned to the A/E, ignoring the agreement leaves conflicts undetected, and waiting until after award defeats the purpose of coordination.

questions.question: Under the negotiated option, the negotiating contractor prepares the contracting forms, bonds, and certificates instead of the A/E. When the A/E reviews these forms, what does industry guidance identify as the focus of that review?

options.A: Confirming the forms are standard AIA or EJCDC documents
options.B: Confirming the forms add no A/E duties beyond the A/E agreement
options.C: Confirming the forms follow the A/E's office master format
options.D: Confirming the named surety is acceptable to the owner's insurer

questions.explanation: When the negotiating contractor prepares the contracting forms, bonds, and certificates, industry guidance directs the A/E to review them to be sure they do not add responsibilities beyond those in the A/E's own agreement. Industry guidance does not require the forms to be AIA or EJCDC documents, to follow the A/E's office format, or to be checked by the A/E for surety acceptability.

questions.question: Reviewing a proposed owner-contractor agreement for a negotiated project, the A/E finds that it says nothing about the contractor's required responses to the A/E's contract administration responsibilities. What is the A/E's best course of action?

options.A: Revise the agreement directly to add the missing obligations
options.B: Take no action, since the A/E agreement alone defines those duties
options.C: Notify the owner that the agreement leaves out those obligations
options.D: Ask the contractor directly to add the obligations to the agreement

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the A/E should tell the owner when a proposed agreement fails to address required responses to the A/E's responsibilities. The A/E is not a party to the owner-contractor agreement, so editing it directly or negotiating the gap with the contractor instead of raising it with the owner is not the course industry guidance gives, and taking no action leaves the A/E's role unsupported in the contract.

questions.question: During negotiations on a design-bid-build project, the owner and contractor modify several provisions of the general conditions. What does industry guidance direct the A/E to do?

options.A: Review the changes to see whether Division 01 needs revision
options.B: Remove the conditions of the contract from the project manual as superseded
options.C: Leave Division 01 unchanged, since negotiated changes do not affect it
options.D: Rewrite Part 1 of each Divisions 02-49 section to restate the new provisions

questions.explanation: Industry guidance treats the conditions of the contract as the foundation for Division 01, so when negotiation changes those provisions the A/E must check whether Division 01 needs revision. The conditions stay in the project manual to establish that basis, negotiated changes can affect Division 01, and restating the provisions in every product section would only create duplication.

questions.question: On a negotiated design-bid-build project, the contractor offers its own version of the conditions of the contract. Whose review should that version receive?

options.A: The contractor's legal counsel
options.B: The owner's legal counsel
options.C: The owner's insurance consultant
options.D: The contractor's bonding surety

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that if the negotiating contractor proposes its own version of the conditions of the contract, the owner's legal counsel should review it. The contractor's counsel represents the party that drafted the document, and an insurance consultant or surety is not named for this review.

questions.question: On a negotiated project, the owner-contractor agreement already sets out the payment application process and retainage. The owner's draft supplementary conditions restate the same retainage terms. What does industry guidance recommend?

options.A: Keep the terms in both documents to reinforce them for the contractor
options.B: Move the terms into the conditions and delete them from the agreement
options.C: Move the terms to Division 01 and delete them from the other two documents
options.D: Keep the terms in the agreement and do not repeat them in the conditions

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that insurance, bonds, and payments, including payment applications and retainage, may be covered in the owner-contractor agreement and should then not be repeated in the conditions of the contract. Duplicating them invites conflict, and industry guidance does not suggest stripping them from the agreement or relocating them to Division 01.

questions.question: On a negotiated project, the owner declines to share the owner-contractor agreement with the A/E, citing confidentiality. How does industry guidance say the conditions of the contract for the project manual should then be handled?

options.A: The A/E should publish unmodified standard AIA conditions as a placeholder
options.B: The A/E should leave the conditions of the contract out of the project manual
options.C: The contractor's counsel should expand Division 01 to replace the conditions
options.D: The owner and contractor should prepare suitable conditions for publication

questions.explanation: When the A/E cannot see the owner-contractor agreement, industry guidance says the owner and contractor should prepare suitable conditions of the contract to be published in the project manual. Publishing unmodified standard conditions risks conflict with an agreement the A/E has not seen, leaving the conditions out removes the basis for Division 01, and Division 01 cannot replace them.

questions.question: On a negotiated design-bid-build project, the specifier is coordinating Division 01 with the conditions of the contract. Which group of procedures does industry guidance name as possibly needing special coordination because they may be negotiated?

options.A: Progress schedules, substitutions, and warranties
options.B: Temporary facilities, field engineering, and cutting
options.C: Quality control, regulatory requirements, and mockups
options.D: Selective demolition, alterations, and protection

questions.explanation: Industry guidance lists payment procedures, construction progress schedules, submittals, substitutions, warranties, and contract closeout as negotiated procedures that may need special coordination between Division 01 and the conditions of the contract. Temporary facilities, field engineering, quality control, regulatory requirements, and demolition topics are not on that list.

questions.question: During negotiations on a design-bid-build project, the owner and contractor agree on a specific roofing system and price it accordingly. How does industry guidance suggest the specifier write the roofing section?

options.A: As a performance specification so that competing systems can still be offered
options.B: As a descriptive specification with more detail than for a bid project
options.C: As a proprietary specification, with some level of detail eliminated
options.D: As a reference to the negotiated price list in the owner-contractor agreement

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that when pricing and negotiations have settled on specific products, the section might be written as proprietary, which can remove some level of detail. A performance approach would reopen competition the negotiation already resolved, industry guidance describes negotiated specifications as otherwise similar rather than more detailed, and the agreement is not a substitute for the specification section.

questions.question: An A/E is scoping its services for a construction manager at risk (CMAR) project. Which task belongs to the construction manager rather than the A/E?

options.A: Preparing the Division 01 sections that all packages reference
options.B: Preparing the procurement documents for each subcontract
options.C: Preparing the Divisions 02 through 49 sections for each package
options.D: Preparing the drawings that are issued with each work package

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that with CMAR the A/E does not prepare procurement documents; the construction manager prepares them for each subcontract it intends to issue. Industry guidance does not shift Division 01, the Divisions 02 through 49 sections, or the package drawings to the construction manager; it directs the A/E to prepare specifications that secure accurate pricing and to work with the CM on package drawings and specifications.
questions.source: document variations for the construction manager at risk (CMAR) project delivery method

questions.question: A CMAR job will use fast-track scheduling. Industry guidance says the construction manager may then furnish procurement documents for each work package issued, comparable to the work packages of which method?

options.A: Design-build with bridging documents
options.B: Integrated project delivery (IPD)
options.C: Multiple-prime with CM as advisor
options.D: Negotiated design-bid-build

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says that when the construction manager uses fast-track scheduling, it may furnish procurement documents for each work package issued, comparable to the work packages used in IPD. Design-build, multiple-prime with a CM as advisor, and the negotiated design-bid-build option are not the comparison industry guidance draws.
questions.source: document variations for the construction manager at risk (CMAR) project delivery method

questions.question: An owner wants a contractor-side manager's input on cost and constructability while drawings are still being developed. How does industry guidance characterize CMAR in relation to that goal?

options.A: It does not fit; CMAR expertise begins only after design is complete
options.B: It does not fit; CMAR expertise is confined to the construction phase
options.C: It fits only when fast-track scheduling divides design into packages
options.D: It fits; CMAR provides professional management expertise during design

questions.explanation: Industry guidance describes CMAR as providing professional management expertise during the project's design, which matches an owner wanting construction input while drawings are being developed. The distractors place that expertise only after design or only in construction, or make it depend on fast-track scheduling, none of which states.
questions.source: document variations for the construction manager at risk (CMAR) project delivery method

questions.question: A specifier accustomed to design-bid-build starts a CMAR project. Regarding items normally within the A/E's responsibility in preparing the project manual, what should the specifier expect?

options.A: Decisions will often be shared with the owner and construction manager
options.B: The A/E will remain the sole decision-maker on all such items
options.C: The construction manager will become the sole decision-maker on them
options.D: The owner's attorney will make those decisions for the project manual

questions.explanation: Under CMAR, industry guidance notes the A/E will not necessarily be the sole decision-maker on items normally within its responsibility; those decisions are often shared with team members including the owner and construction manager. Industry guidance describes sharing, not a full transfer of authority to the CM or the owner's attorney, and not continued sole control by the A/E.

questions.question: In Division 00 for a CMAR project, which item is given as an example of a procurement form rather than a contract form or an owner-provided document?

options.A: Substitution request form
options.B: RFI form
options.C: Wage rates
options.D: Geotechnical data

questions.explanation: In the CMAR Division 00 description, wage rates are the example of a procurement form, while the substitution request form and RFI form are examples of contract forms. Geotechnical data is an owner-provided document, listed alongside information on existing hazardous materials.

questions.question: On a CMAR project, the construction manager adds its own subcontractor bid forms and subcontract documents to Division 00 of the project manual. What does industry guidance say should accompany that addition?

options.A: The table of contents should list each added item
options.B: The A/E should reformat each added item to its office standard
options.C: The added items should be bound as a separate volume
options.D: The owner should execute each added item before issue

questions.explanation: Industry guidance allows the construction manager to supplement Division 00 with its own subcontractor forms and documents, and states that when they are included the table of contents should list them. Industry guidance does not call for the A/E to reformat them, bind them separately, or have the owner execute them first.

questions.question: An A/E is estimating its specification effort for Division 00 on a CMAR project. Which expectation is consistent with industry guidance?

options.A: Heavy effort: the A/E prepares bid forms and instructions for every subcontract
options.B: Moderate effort: the A/E drafts the CM's standard subcontract agreement forms
options.C: Light effort: owner-provided data and a few forms, possibly added to by the CM
options.D: No effort: Division 00 is omitted entirely from CMAR project manuals

questions.explanation: Industry guidance expects little A/E preparation effort for Division 00 on CMAR: mainly owner-provided documents such as geotechnical and hazardous material data, a few procurement and contract forms, and possible CM supplements. The CM, not the A/E, prepares subcontract procurement documents and its standard agreement forms, and Division 00 is not omitted.

questions.question: On a CMAR project, the owner decides to prepare the procurement requirements for an early site-utilities package itself instead of the construction manager. How does this affect the A/E's coordination?

options.A: The A/E now coordinates that package with the owner only, not with the CM
options.B: The A/E is relieved of coordinating because the CM did not prepare them
options.C: The A/E must now prepare procurement requirements for the other packages
options.D: The A/E still works with the CM on the drawings and specifications

questions.explanation: Industry guidance makes the A/E's coordination with the construction manager independent of who writes the procurement requirements: the A/E and CM work together on the drawings and specifications each package needs. A different preparer does not redirect that coordination to the owner alone, end it, or make the A/E responsible for procurement requirements on the other packages.

questions.question: What is the stated purpose of the A/E working with the construction manager on the drawings and specifications to be included in CMAR work packages?

options.A: To ensure each package carries its own copy of Division 01
options.B: To ensure each package contains the required information
options.C: To ensure each package uses the CM's standard subcontract forms
options.D: To ensure each package is priced within the owner's budget

questions.explanation: The A/E works with the construction manager so that the work packages contain the information they need. Division 01 may be issued once as a stand-alone package rather than in every package, the CM's subcontract forms are a separate Division 00 matter, and budget control is not the purpose industry guidance gives.

questions.question: Midway through design, a CMAR team decides to issue one complete set of construction documents rather than a series of work packages. How does industry guidance treat the A/E's collaboration with the construction manager on drawings and specifications?

options.A: It ends, because it is required only when work packages are issued
options.B: It shifts to the owner, who coordinates single-set documents with the CM
options.C: It still applies, whether the work is issued as one set or as packages
options.D: It is replaced by a Division 01 section that defines single-set content

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the A/E should work with the construction manager on the drawings and specifications whether the documents go out as a single set or as a series of work packages. The coordination is not limited to packaged projects, does not shift to the owner, and is not replaced by a Division 01 section.

questions.question: Who usually prepares the agreement forms for subcontracts on a CMAR project, and what are they typically based on?

options.A: The A/E, adapting the standard owner-contractor agreement form
options.B: The construction manager, using its standard subcontract forms
options.C: The owner's attorney, using the owner's in-house legal forms
options.D: The construction manager, matching an owner-CM advisor agreement

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says that on CMAR projects the construction manager usually prepares the agreement forms, typically its own standard subcontract forms. Compatibility with an owner-CM agreement form is the point for the CM as advisor/agent option, and neither the A/E nor the owner's attorney is named as the usual preparer here.

questions.question: A specifier preparing the project manual for a CMAR project notes that the general conditions were settled in the owner-CM contract long before. Should a copy of the conditions of the contract be included?

options.A: No, because they were established before the project manual was prepared
options.B: No, because the CM's subcontract forms replace the general conditions
options.C: Yes, but only as a summary restated within Division 01 requirements
options.D: Yes, because subcontractors are bound to the same provisions as the CM

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that for CMAR the general conditions are already in place when the project manual is prepared, but a copy should still be included because subcontractors are bound by the same provisions as the construction manager. Their earlier establishment is not a reason to omit them, the CM's subcontract forms do not replace them, and a Division 01 summary is not what industry guidance calls for.

questions.question: A CMAR project will be issued in six work packages. Which approach to Division 01 does industry guidance describe for multiple work package projects?

options.A: Issue it once as a stand-alone package referenced by each later package
options.B: Publish the complete Division 01 again with every work package issued
options.C: Write a separate Division 01 tailored to the scope of each package
options.D: Omit Division 01 and rely on the CM's subcontract general conditions

questions.explanation: For projects with multiple work packages, industry guidance says Division 01 may be issued as a stand-alone package that each later package references, so it need not be published with every package. Writing different Division 01 versions per package conflicts with the statement that all specifications are subject to the same Division 01 requirements, and omitting Division 01 is not an option industry guidance offers.

questions.question: Division 01 for a multi-package CMAR project was issued as a stand-alone package. Work package 4 now needs a revision to a Division 01 section. How does industry guidance indicate the change can be issued?

options.A: By reissuing every earlier work package with the revision
options.B: Only in the conformed documents after all packages are out
options.C: Through a separate Division 01 revision package after award
options.D: Along with work package 4 when that package is released

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that if a later work package requires a Division 01 revision, the change can be issued with that work package. Reissuing every earlier package, waiting for conformed documents, or processing a separate post-award revision package is not the method industry guidance describes.

questions.question: The CM on a CMAR project suggests that the early site work package follow lighter general requirements than the later building packages. How does this compare with industry guidance?

options.A: It aligns; each work package may carry its own Division 01 requirements
options.B: It conflicts; every package is subject to the same Division 01 requirements
options.C: It aligns, provided the owner approves the reduced requirements in writing
options.D: It conflicts; site packages must follow the conditions of the contract alone

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says CMAR specifications are subject to the same Division 01 requirements whether issued as one set or as multiple work packages, so lighter general requirements for one package conflict with that guidance. Industry guidance lets a needed Division 01 revision travel with a later package, but that revises the common Division 01 rather than creating package-specific requirements; owner approval is not an exception industry guidance offers, and site packages are not limited to the conditions of the contract.

questions.question: On a CMAR project, the A/E is deciding how to approach the Divisions 02 through 49 sections. Which objective does industry guidance state the A/E's specifications should achieve?

options.A: Minimizing document length so packages can be released sooner
options.B: Transferring design responsibility to the trade subcontractors
options.C: Securing accurate pricing for each set or package
options.D: Limiting each work package to sections not previously issued

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the A/E should prepare specifications that secure accurate pricing, whether issued as a single set or as multiple work packages. Industry guidance does not frame the purpose as shortening documents, transferring design responsibility to subcontractors, or barring reuse of earlier sections; in fact later packages may reuse sections.

questions.question: Under CMAR delivery, which parties or factors does industry guidance say may influence the level of detail in the A/E's specifications?

options.A: The construction manager or the owner's project requirements
options.B: The trade subcontractors or the authority having jurisdiction
options.C: The bonding surety or the owner's insurance carrier
options.D: The low bidders' pricing or the product manufacturers

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that on CMAR projects the level of detail in the specifications may be shaped by the construction manager or by the owner's project requirements. Trade subcontractors, the authority having jurisdiction, sureties, insurers, low bidders' pricing, and product manufacturers are not the influences industry guidance names.

questions.question: A later CMAR work package needs the same cast-in-place concrete section that was issued with the foundation package. What does industry guidance indicate?

options.A: The section may not appear in any package after the one that first issued it
options.B: The section may be reused only after it is renumbered for the later package
options.C: The same section may be reused in the later package, under version control
options.D: The section may be reused only after the earlier package is withdrawn

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that some work packages may use the same sections as packages issued earlier, and points to its version-control guidance for managing them. Reuse is not prohibited, and industry guidance attaches no condition that the section be renumbered or that the earlier package be withdrawn.

questions.question: After all work packages for a CMAR project are issued, who might require that they be combined into one project manual, and for what reason?

options.A: The owner or construction manager, for convenience
options.B: The authority having jurisdiction, for permit records
options.C: The A/E, to satisfy its professional liability insurer
options.D: The contractor's surety, to define the bonded work

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the owner or the construction manager might require that all work packages be combined into one project manual for convenience once all packages are issued. Permit records, the A/E's insurer, and the surety are not the reasons or parties industry guidance identifies.

questions.question: When should the A/E on a multi-package CMAR project become aware that the packages may later be combined into a single project manual?

options.A: When the final work package is about to be issued
options.B: At the outset, before the first package is prepared
options.C: When the owner formally requests a combined manual
options.D: At substantial completion, as record documents begin

questions.explanation: Industry guidance advises the A/E to be aware of a possible combination of all work packages from the beginning, so the sections and drawings can be organized for it. Learning of it only when the last package goes out, when the owner asks, or at substantial completion would be too late to number and title sections consistently.

questions.question: Anticipating that the owner may later want all CMAR work packages merged into one project manual and drawing set, what should the A/E do from the start?

options.A: Issue each package with its own complete Division 01 so that packages can stand alone
options.B: Number each package's sections independently, restarting in every package
options.C: Defer assigning any section numbers until every package has been issued and priced
options.D: Organize similar sections by suitable numbers and titles; number drawings logically

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says that, knowing combination may be required, the A/E should organize similar specification sections using appropriate numbers and titles and give the drawings a logical numbering system from the beginning. Repeating a full Division 01 in every package is unnecessary, numbering each package independently works against a later merge, and deferring numbering does not prepare the documents for combination.

questions.question: An owner retains a construction manager who will not perform work as a contractor. The owner's agreement authorizes the CM to make decisions on the owner's behalf instead of only offering recommendations. Which designation fits this arrangement?

options.A: Construction manager as advisor (CMa)
options.B: Construction manager at risk (CMAR)
options.C: Construction manager as agent
options.D: Construction manager as constructor

questions.explanation: Industry guidance separates the two non-contractor CM roles by authority: the CM as agent stands in the owner's place and may decide for the owner, whereas the CM as advisor is retained to advise the owner throughout the project. CMAR and CM as constructor both put the CM in the contractor role, which this owner excluded.
questions.source: document variations for the construction management as Advisor/Agent management option

questions.question: An owner asks whether the construction manager as advisor/agent option is tied to a particular project delivery method and what kind of project it fits best. Which response matches industry guidance?

options.A: It applies with any delivery method and is best suited to single-prime projects
options.B: It applies only with design-bid-build and is best suited to multiple-prime projects
options.C: It applies with any delivery method and is best suited to multiple-prime projects
options.D: It applies only with design-bid-build and is best suited to single-prime projects

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that CM as advisor/agent provides management services to the owner and can be used with any project delivery method, and that it is particularly well suited to projects with multiple prime contractors. Options restricting it to design-bid-build or pairing it with single-prime projects as the best fit contradict recommended practice.
questions.source: document variations for the construction management as Advisor/Agent management option

questions.question: An owner using a construction manager as advisor elects fast-track scheduling with a single-prime contract and expects the A/E's document effort to shrink because the overall schedule will be shorter. What does industry guidance indicate is likely?

options.A: The A/E's document preparation time is likely to decrease in step with the reduced overall schedule
options.B: The A/E's document preparation time is unaffected because fast-track applies only to multiple-prime work
options.C: The A/E's document preparation time is likely to increase while the overall schedule is reduced
options.D: The A/E's document preparation time is likely to decrease because the CM produces the document packages

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says that with fast-track scheduling, on either a single-prime or a multiple-prime project, the A/E should expect to spend more time preparing documents even though the overall schedule shrinks; the documentation is staggered into separate bid/proposal packages. The A/E, not the CM, usually produces the document packages the CM identifies.
questions.source: document variations for the construction management as Advisor/Agent management option

questions.question: An A/E has two projects that both use a construction manager as advisor/agent: Project 1 is a single-prime competitive bid project, and Project 2 is divided into multiple prime contracts. Where should the A/E expect differences in project manual preparation?

options.A: Mainly on Project 1, since the CM option there replaces the single prime contractor
options.B: Equally on both projects, since CM involvement alters the manual whether contracts are single or multiple
options.C: On neither project, since the CM handles procurement outside the project manual
options.D: Mainly on Project 2, since the CM option there implements multiple-prime contracts

questions.explanation: Industry guidance ties project manual differences under CM as advisor/agent to its use for a multiple-prime project. For a single-prime project the manual may differ little or not at all from a typical bid or proposal project, so CM involvement alone does not drive the change.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project using a construction manager as advisor/agent, the specifier assumes the A/E will have the final word on every item that is normally its responsibility. What does industry guidance indicate?

options.A: Those decisions are often shared with team members such as the owner and the CM
options.B: Those decisions stay with the A/E, since the CM's role is limited to advising the owner
options.C: Those decisions shift to the CM, since it acts as the owner's agent on the project
options.D: Those decisions wait until the prime contractors' bids reveal the cost impacts

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says that, as with other delivery methods, the A/E is not necessarily the only decision-maker under this option; the owner and CM commonly share in those decisions. Sharing is not a transfer to the CM, the A/E does not keep sole control, and industry guidance does not defer these decisions until bids are in.

questions.question: For a single-prime project that uses the construction manager as advisor/agent option, industry guidance says the project manual may see little to no variation from which baseline?

options.A: A typical construction manager at risk project
options.B: A typical negotiated-contract project
options.C: A typical integrated project delivery project
options.D: A typical competitive bid or proposal project

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the project manual for a single-prime CM as advisor/agent project may vary little or not at all from that of a typical bid or proposal project. Industry guidance describes the negotiated option, CMAR, and IPD as each bringing their own project manual differences, so none of them is the baseline.

questions.question: An owner will hire a firm to manage a multiple-prime project as the owner's advisor or agent, without the firm acting as a contractor. Besides the AIA, EJCDC, and the ConsensusDocs Coalition, which organization does industry guidance name as a publisher of specialized standard contract documents for this option?

options.A: Design-Build Institute of America (DBIA)
options.B: Project Management Institute (PMI)
options.C: Construction Specifications Institute (CSI)
options.D: Construction Management Association of America (CMAA)

questions.explanation: Industry guidance names four publishers of specialized contract documents for the CM as advisor/agent option: AIA, EJCDC, ConsensusDocs, and CMAA. DBIA's documents address design-build, PMI publishes general project management standards, and CSI publishes formats and practice guidance rather than CM contract forms.

questions.question: For a multiple-prime project managed by a construction manager as advisor/agent, what does each bid/proposal package usually contain in Division 00?

options.A: Procurement requirements with a form fitted to the package's scope, with the conditions of the contract issued after all packages are awarded
options.B: Procurement requirements with a form fitted to the package's scope, plus contracting requirements including the conditions of the contract
options.C: Contracting requirements only, with a single bid form covering the entire project issued with the first package
options.D: A bid form covering the entire project, plus the construction manager's standard subcontract forms as the agreement

questions.explanation: Industry guidance describes each multiple-prime package as carrying both procurement requirements, with a bid/proposal form matched to that package's scope, and contracting requirements that include the conditions of the contract. Deferring the conditions, using one project-wide bid form, or substituting the CM's subcontract forms all depart from that description.

questions.question: A specifier proposes reusing the firm's standard design-bid-build Division 00 documents without change on a multiple-prime project where the owner has engaged a construction manager as agent. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Modify the procurement and contracting requirements to conform to this management option
options.B: Reuse them unchanged, since obtaining separate prime bids differs little from design-bid-build
options.C: Replace the agreement and conditions with the construction manager's standard subcontract forms
options.D: Keep them, but issue one bid form covering the combined scope of all the prime contracts

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that the procurement and contracting requirements must be modified to suit the CM as advisor/agent option, and specialized standard documents exist for it. Even though obtaining bids resembles design-bid-build, the documents still need adjustment. CM subcontract forms are the CMAR approach, and each multiple-prime package needs a bid/proposal form suited to its own scope.

questions.question: A construction manager as agent wants to start procuring the early prime contracts while design of later work is still underway and also wants to hold down reproduction costs. Which issuing approach does industry guidance associate with those advantages?

options.A: Issue full sets of procurement documents with every package
options.B: Issue full sets after design completion with scopes in Section 01 12 00
options.C: Issue partial documents describing only the package being procured
options.D: Issue the drawings in full sets and the specifications only in part

questions.explanation: Industry guidance credits partial packages with allowing procurement during ongoing design and usually lowering reproduction costs, at the price of bidders not seeing all related documents. Full sets let each bidder see everything but require a completed design, which defeats the CM's goal.

questions.question: A construction manager decides to issue full sets of procurement documents with every bid package on a multiple-prime project. Which pairing of advantage and disadvantage does industry guidance give for this approach?

options.A: Bidders can review all requirements affecting their price; the design must be complete
options.B: Packages can be issued while design continues; bidders may not see all related documents
options.C: Reproduction costs are usually lower; the design must be complete
options.D: Bidders can review all requirements affecting their price; scope gaps between the primes increase

questions.explanation: For full sets, industry guidance names the benefit that each bidder can examine every requirement that might affect its bid, and the drawback that the design has to be finished first. Issuing during design and lower reproduction cost are benefits industry guidance gives for partial packages, and it does not cite scope gaps as a drawback of full sets.

questions.question: When full sets of procurement documents go to every bidder on a multiple-prime project, industry guidance says the scope of work for each contract should be indicated where?

options.A: In the bid/proposal form or in Section 01 12 00
options.B: In the instructions to bidders or in Section 01 11 00
options.C: In the agreement form or in Section 01 31 00
options.D: In the supplementary conditions or in Section 01 14 00

questions.explanation: Because every bidder receives everything, industry guidance directs that each contract's scope be stated on the bid/proposal form or in Section 01 12 00, Multiple Contract Summary. Section 01 11 00 describes work under a single contract, and the other locations are not where industry guidance places the per-contract scope.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project using the construction manager as advisor/agent option, who usually prepares the agreement form for each bid package, and with what should it be compatible?

options.A: The CM; it should be the CM's own standard subcontract form for each trade
options.B: The A/E; it should be compatible with the owner-A/E agreement form
options.C: The CM; it should be compatible with the owner-CM agreement form
options.D: Each prime contractor; it should match that contractor's standard subcontract form

questions.explanation: Industry guidance assigns preparation of each package's agreement form to the CM and requires compatibility with the owner-CM as advisor/agent agreement. Using the CM's standard subcontract forms describes CMAR, and contractor-prepared subcontract forms describe IPD, so neither fits this option.

questions.question: General conditions for a multiple-prime project under the construction manager as advisor/agent option need special provisions for cooperation and mutual responsibility among the primes. Which CM service does industry guidance give as an example such provisions may require?

options.A: Reviewing and approving shop drawings for the primes in place of the A/E
options.B: Consolidating the primes' payment applications into one for the A/E to review
options.C: Certifying substantial completion for the primes on the owner's behalf
options.D: Guaranteeing a maximum price for the combined work of all of the prime contracts

questions.explanation: The example of a special provision is having the CM combine the multiple payment applications into a single application that the A/E reviews. Industry guidance does not move shop drawing approval or completion certification to the CM, and a guaranteed maximum price belongs to an at-risk arrangement, not an advisory or agency role.

questions.question: A specifier is drafting supplementary conditions for a multiple-prime project managed by a construction manager as agent. Which modifications do these supplementary conditions typically include?

options.A: The usual design-bid-build ones, such as insurance, bonds, payment applications, and retainage
options.B: Provisions coordinating the primes, with insurance and bond requirements relocated to Division 01
options.C: Provisions unique to CM delivery, since design-bid-build modifications do not carry over
options.D: Each prime's scope of work, with payment terms left to the individual agreement forms

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes the supplementary conditions for this option carry the customary design-bid-build modifications, naming insurance and bond requirements and the payment application and retainage process. The distractors wrongly limit the content or shift insurance, bonds, and payment matters elsewhere.

questions.question: The first of five prime-contract bid packages must be issued in three weeks, but the general conditions are still in draft. The CM suggests releasing the first package now and tailoring the conditions of the contract to each later package. What is the best course of action?

options.A: Release the first package without conditions and publish one set with the last package
options.B: Complete them early for the first package, then issue identical conditions with every package
options.C: Tailor the conditions of the contract to each package's scope, just as is done for Division 01 sections
options.D: Issue the conditions only with packages whose scope carries insurance or bond requirements

questions.explanation: Because the conditions of the contract are published with the first bid/proposal package, industry guidance calls for preparing them early, and it requires identical conditions in every multiple-prime package. Division 01 sections may vary by package, but the conditions may not, and withholding them from some packages contradicts the guidance.

questions.question: The construction manager is assembling a multiple-prime bid package for interior painting only. Which Division 01 requirement does industry guidance say should be included with every package, including this one?

options.A: Temporary facilities and controls
options.B: Product substitution procedures
options.C: Alternates
options.D: Field engineering

questions.explanation: Industry guidance identifies submittal procedures, product substitution procedures, and cleaning as common to all packages. Temporary facilities and controls, alternates, and field engineering are examples of sections to issue only with the packages they apply to.

questions.question: On a project with several prime contracts under a construction manager as advisor/agent, which Division 01 section should identify the participants' responsibilities, the construction documents packages, and site use?

options.A: Section 01 11 00, Summary of Work
options.B: Section 01 31 00, Project Management and Coordination
options.C: Section 01 14 00, Work Restrictions
options.D: Section 01 12 00, Multiple Contract Summary

questions.explanation: Industry guidance assigns participants' responsibilities, long-lead items, the document packages, and site use to Section 01 12 00 on multiple-prime projects. Section 01 11 00 is for work under a single contract, and the other sections address coordination and restrictions rather than this multiple-contract summary.

questions.question: A prime contractor on a multiple-prime project managed by a construction manager as agent submits shop drawings missing required information. Under Section 01 33 00, what normally happens?

options.A: The A/E checks it for completeness and returns it through the CM to the contractor
options.B: The CM checks it for completeness and returns it to the contractor to resubmit
options.C: The CM forwards it unchanged to the A/E, which then checks it for completeness
options.D: The owner checks it for completeness and returns it to the A/E for resubmittal

questions.explanation: Under this option industry guidance has the CM receive shop drawings, product data, and samples, check them for completeness, and either forward them to the A/E or send them back to the contractor to resubmit. The A/E is not the completeness gatekeeper here, and the owner has no role in that check.

questions.question: After the CM and the A/E inspect a multiple-prime project for substantial completion, how does Section 01 70 00 typically handle the inspection results?

options.A: Given to the owner for corrective action and to each responsible contractor for information
options.B: Given to the A/E for certification and to the CM for adjustment of the final payment
options.C: Given to each responsible contractor for corrective action and to the owner for information
options.D: Given to the CM alone, which decides whether the owner needs to be informed

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that results of the substantial completion inspection go to the respective contractors so they can correct deficiencies, and to the owner so it is informed. Reversing those roles, routing results only to the CM, or treating them as a payment adjustment is not what industry guidance describes.

questions.question: Two bid packages on a multiple-prime project each need miscellaneous metal, and their Metal Fabrications sections differ in content. How can the two sections be numbered and titled?

options.A: With Level 3 numbers such as 05 51 00 and 05 52 00, each with its own distinct title
options.B: With letter suffixes such as 05 50 00A and 05 50 00B, sharing a single title
options.C: With Level 2 numbers such as 05 50 00 and 05 60 00, sharing a single title
options.D: With Level 4 numbers such as 05 50 00.10 and 05 50 00.20, each with its own title

questions.explanation: The example gives each package-specific metal fabrications section a different Level 4 number and title, such as 05 50 00.10 for building envelope and 05 50 00.20 for interior construction. Level 3 numbers already denote other MasterFormat subjects, and letter suffixes or another Level 2 number are not the method industry guidance shows.

questions.question: The construction manager on a multiple-prime project prefers that one Metal Fabrications section be issued with every bid package. How does industry guidance indicate the portion belonging to each package should then be defined?

options.A: Keep the single section and describe each package's scope in Section 01 11 00
options.B: Keep the single section and describe each package's scope in Section 01 12 00
options.C: Keep the single section and define each package's portion as an alternate in Section 01 23 00
options.D: Keep the single section and describe each package's scope in the supplementary conditions

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that some construction managers use the same section for all packages and rely on Section 01 12 00, Multiple Contract Summary, to state what each package includes. Section 01 11 00 covers single-contract work, alternates serve a different purpose, and the conditions are identical across packages so they cannot carry package scope.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, the construction manager as agent asks the specifier to revise several technical sections so each prime contractor's responsibilities are unmistakable. How does industry guidance view the CM's involvement?

options.A: As appropriate, though the level of specification detail remains the A/E's decision alone
options.B: As appropriate; the CM may seek such changes and may influence specification detail
options.C: As misplaced; each prime's responsibilities belong in its agreement form, not the specifications
options.D: As premature; responsibilities are clarified by addendum only after bids are received

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the CM may request changes so the various contractors' responsibilities are clearly defined, and that the CM or the owner's project requirements may shape how detailed the specifications are. Keeping detail solely with the A/E, moving responsibilities into agreement forms, or deferring them to post-bid addenda does not match recommended practice.

questions.question: Under the CM as advisor/agent option, which parties does industry guidance identify as possibly requiring that all document packages be combined into one project manual and one set of drawings?

options.A: The owner or the A/E
options.B: The A/E or the prime contractors
options.C: The owner or the CM
options.D: The CM or the prime contractors

questions.explanation: Industry guidance names the owner or the CM as the parties that might call for combining every package into a single project manual and drawing set, for convenience. The A/E is expected to anticipate that possibility rather than impose it, and the prime contractors are not named.

questions.question: At the start of the construction documents stage on a multiple-prime project, the CM mentions the packages might later be merged into one project manual. What should the A/E do about specification section numbering?

options.A: Wait until all packages are issued, then renumber similar sections in the merged manual
options.B: Number each package's sections independently and add a cross-reference table later
options.C: Give every package identical Level 2 numbers and rely on the package name to distinguish them
options.D: Organize similar sections now using the appropriate level of numbers and titles

questions.explanation: Industry guidance wants the A/E to anticipate combination from the outset so that similar sections are organized with suitable number levels and titles. Deferring the work, patching it with a cross-reference table, or reusing identical Level 2 numbers would leave the merged manual disorganized.

questions.question: Under the construction manager as advisor/agent option, why might the separate bid packages be merged into combined documents, and how should the drawings be handled?

options.A: For convenience; the drawings should follow a logical numbering system from the start
options.B: For permit review; the drawings should be reissued with new numbers at combination
options.C: For legal precedence; the drawings should be bound behind the combined project manual
options.D: For record documents; the drawings should be renumbered after substantial completion

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the owner or CM might combine the packages simply for convenience and that the A/E should number drawings with a logical system so they fit together. Permit review, precedence, and record documents are not the reasons given, and later renumbering is what early planning is meant to avoid.

questions.question: On an integrated project delivery project, the owner, A/E, and contractor form a limited liability company and become its members. Which contractual arrangement is this?

options.A: Multi-party agreement
options.B: Standard tripartite arrangement
options.C: Single-purpose entity (SPE) agreement
options.D: Joint venture agreement between the A/E and the contractor

questions.explanation: Industry guidance lists three IPD arrangements; the one in which the owner, A/E, and contractor are members of an LLC is the single-purpose entity agreement. A multi-party agreement binds them in one contract without forming a company, the tripartite arrangement uses separate owner agreements, and a joint venture of only the A/E and contractor leaves out the owner.
questions.source: document variations for the integrated project delivery (IPD) method

questions.question: An owner wants integrated project delivery but insists on keeping one agreement with the A/E and a separate agreement with the contractor. Can this still be an IPD project?

options.A: No; integrated delivery forbids separate agreements and requires one multi-party agreement
options.B: No; integrated delivery requires the three parties to form a single-purpose entity
options.C: Yes; but only if the contractor also serves as construction manager as agent
options.D: Yes; this standard tripartite arrangement is one of the recognized IPD options

questions.explanation: Industry guidance recognizes a standard tripartite arrangement, with separate owner-A/E and owner-contractor agreements, as one of the three IPD contractual arrangements. Multi-party and SPE agreements are alternatives, not requirements, and industry guidance does not condition IPD on a CM as agent role.
questions.source: document variations for the integrated project delivery (IPD) method

questions.question: Regardless of the contractual arrangement chosen, industry guidance says integrated project delivery works in practice much like which approach?

options.A: Design-bid-build using competitive bidding and a single set
options.B: CM as advisor using multiple-prime contracts and full sets
options.C: CMAR using fast-track scheduling and multiple work packages
options.D: Design-build using bridging documents and a single package

questions.explanation: Industry guidance compares IPD in practice to construction manager at risk with fast-track scheduling and multiple work packages; documentation is staggered by package, and the A/E's preparation time usually grows even as the overall schedule shrinks. The other combinations describe different methods that industry guidance does not equate with IPD.
questions.source: document variations for the integrated project delivery (IPD) method

questions.question: On an integrated project delivery project, the A/E's specifier finds that decisions normally made by the A/E, such as product selections, are being made jointly with other stakeholders. How does industry guidance characterize this?

options.A: As improper, because the A/E alone makes such decisions for the project manual
options.B: As expected, because IPD is a collaborative process in which decisions are shared
options.C: As expected only under a single-purpose entity agreement, in which the parties share one company
options.D: As expected for Divisions 00 and 01, though technical section decisions stay with the A/E

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that in the collaborative IPD process the A/E may not be the only decision-maker on items that would usually be its responsibility, and those decisions are often shared with other stakeholders. Industry guidance does not tie this to one IPD agreement or exempt technical sections, and it does not treat shared decisions as improper.

questions.question: How much Division 00 preparation effort does industry guidance expect from the A/E on an integrated project delivery project?

options.A: Little, although owner-provided documents and some standard forms may be included
options.B: Little, since Division 00 is omitted from the project manual under IPD
options.C: Moderate, since the A/E drafts the multi-party agreement for the parties
options.D: Extensive, since the A/E prepares procurement requirements for every work package

questions.explanation: Industry guidance expects little A/E effort on Division 00 under IPD, but the division is not dropped: it may hold owner-provided documents, a few procurement and contract forms, and contractor-supplied subcontract documents. The contractor, not the A/E, may prepare procurement requirements for work packages, and industry guidance does not assign agreement drafting to the A/E.

questions.question: A specifier is assembling the project manual for an integrated project delivery project. Which group of items does industry guidance list as possibly included in Division 00?

options.A: Multiple contract summary, allowances, alternates, and testing laboratory services for each package
options.B: Warranties, operation and maintenance data, project record documents, and final cleaning requirements
options.C: Shop drawings, product data, samples, and the submittal procedures for each package
options.D: Geotechnical data, hazardous material information, wage rates, and substitution request and RFI forms

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says Division 00 on an IPD project may contain owner-provided items such as geotechnical data and existing hazardous material information, procurement forms such as wage rates, and contract forms such as substitution request and RFI forms. The other groups are Division 01 administrative and closeout topics or submittals, not Division 00 content.

questions.question: On an integrated project delivery project, the contractor adds its own forms and documents for subcontractors to Division 00. What does industry guidance say the project manual should do?

options.A: List the added forms and documents in the table of contents
options.B: Relocate the added forms and documents to Division 01
options.C: Have the A/E rewrite the added forms to match its own forms
options.D: Bind the added forms separately and omit them from the contents

questions.explanation: Industry guidance allows the contractor to supplement Division 00 with forms and documents that apply to subcontractors, and when they are included the table of contents should list them. Industry guidance does not call for moving them to Division 01, rewriting them, or excluding them from the contents.

questions.question: On an integrated project delivery project, who may prepare the procurement requirements for individual work packages, and what is the A/E's role?

options.A: The contractor may; the A/E works with it on drawings and specifications for each package
options.B: The construction manager may; the A/E reviews the work packages only after they have been issued
options.C: The A/E must; the contractor reviews each package for constructability before issue
options.D: The owner must; the A/E furnishes drawings but not specifications for each package

questions.explanation: Under IPD, industry guidance says the contractor may prepare procurement requirements for work packages, and whoever prepares them, the A/E collaborates on the drawings and specifications so each package has the needed information. The construction manager version comes from CMAR, and industry guidance does not make the A/E or the owner the required preparer.

questions.question: On an integrated project delivery project, how does industry guidance describe the agreement forms included in the project manual?

options.A: Usually prepared by the construction manager, using its standard subcontract forms
options.B: Usually prepared by the A/E, using standard owner-contractor agreement forms
options.C: Usually prepared by the construction manager, compatible with the owner-CM agreement
options.D: Usually prepared by the contractor, using its standard subcontract forms

questions.explanation: For IPD, industry guidance says the contractor usually prepares the agreement forms, which are usually its standard subcontract forms. The CM's standard subcontract forms describe CMAR, and CM-prepared forms compatible with the owner-CM agreement describe the CM as advisor/agent option.

questions.question: A specifier preparing the project manual for an integrated project delivery project asks whether to draft new general conditions for it. What does industry guidance indicate?

options.A: Yes; new conditions are drafted for each work package because packages are issued at different times
options.B: No; they are already set, and a copy is included since subcontractors are bound by them
options.C: No; the conditions are omitted because subcontractors are bound only by their subcontract forms
options.D: Yes; separate supplementary conditions are drafted to fit each subcontractor's scope of work

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that under IPD the conditions of the contract are set before the project manual is prepared, and since subcontractors are held to the same provisions as the contractor, a copy belongs in the manual. Drafting new or package-specific conditions, or leaving them out, conflicts with that guidance.

questions.question: An IPD team issued Division 01 as a stand-alone package that its later work packages reference. The fourth work package, for the building envelope, needs a change to a Division 01 closeout requirement. How can that change be handled?

options.A: Republish the complete Division 01 in every remaining package
options.B: Issue the Division 01 revision along with that work package
options.C: Place the revised requirement in Part 1 of each envelope section
options.D: Defer the change until the integrated agreement is amended

questions.explanation: Industry guidance allows a Division 01 revision that a later work package needs to be issued along with that package, so the stand-alone Division 01 stays the common reference. Republishing all of Division 01 in each package defeats the purpose of issuing it once, and scattering the change into product sections or waiting for an agreement amendment is not the approach industry guidance describes.

questions.question: A specifier new to IPD asks how the IPD method affects the general requirements portion of the project manual. What does industry guidance say about Division 01 on an IPD project?

options.A: It is largely superseded by the multiparty agreement and kept minimal
options.B: It is limited to Division 01 temporary facility and closeout requirements
options.C: It is written separately by each team member for its own scope
options.D: It follows the same Division 01 requirements as most other methods

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that IPD specifications are subject to the same Division 01 requirements that apply to most other project delivery methods. The collaborative agreement does not replace Division 01, industry guidance does not narrow it to temporary facilities and closeout, and it is a shared document rather than one authored piecemeal by each participant.

questions.question: An IPD team will issue Division 01 once as a stand-alone package that later work packages reference, issuing any Division 01 revisions with those later packages. Which topic does the IPD Division 01 discussion cross-reference for this approach?

options.A: Version control of previously issued and developing documents
options.B: Addenda procedures during each package's procurement
options.C: Conformed documents prepared after each package's award
options.D: Change order procedures during each package's construction

questions.explanation: Right after describing a stand-alone Division 01 and revisions issued with later packages, industry guidance cross-references its guidance on version control when working with multiple work packages. Addenda, conformed documents, and change orders are other document-modification topics, but they are not the reference industry guidance gives here.

questions.question: On an IPD project, besides the owner's project requirements, which party does industry guidance identify as possibly influencing the level of detail in the Divisions 02 through 49 specifications?

options.A: The construction manager
options.B: The design-builder
options.C: The contractor
options.D: The building official

questions.explanation: For IPD, industry guidance says the level of specification detail may be shaped by the contractor as well as by the owner's project requirements. The construction manager fills that role in the CMAR discussion and the design-builder in the design-build discussion, while the building official is not named as an influence on specification detail.

questions.question: An owner is starting a design-build project. Which set of documents would the owner, rather than the design-builder, typically prepare or issue?

options.A: The construction drawings, specifications, and their later modifications
options.B: Subcontract procurement documents and instructions to bidders
options.C: The RFP, conditions of the contract, and performance specifications
options.D: Shop drawings, product data, and samples for approval

questions.explanation: In design-build, the owner develops its project requirements or description and may issue an RFP, owner-design-builder conditions, technical or performance specifications, and design requirements. The construction drawings, specifications, and later modifications are produced by the design-builder after it negotiates its agreement, and subcontract procurement documents and submittals also originate on the design-builder's side.
questions.source: document variations for design- build delivery method

questions.question: On a design-build project, which statement best describes the construction documents prepared by the design-builder's A/E?

options.A: Contract status depends on the arrangements; usually sent to the owner for approval
options.B: Contract status depends on the arrangements; usually withheld from the owner until closeout
options.C: Always part of the contract; usually sent to the owner for approval
options.D: Never part of the contract; usually withheld from the owner until closeout

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says whether the design-builder's construction documents form part of the owner-design-builder contract depends on the contract arrangements, and that they are usually submitted to the owner for approval. Saying they are always or never part of the contract ignores that conditional language, and industry guidance does not describe withholding them from the owner until closeout.
questions.source: document variations for design- build delivery method

questions.question: An architect is retained by a design-builder to produce the drawings and specifications for a design-build office building. How does industry guidance characterize the architect's basic services?

options.A: Performed as the owner's agent rather than for the design-builder
options.B: Limited to preparing the owner's performance specifications and RFP
options.C: Exempt from the documentation principles that govern traditional project documents
options.D: Like a traditional contract's, though performed in the design-builder's interest

questions.explanation: The A/E working for the design-builder prepares the construction documents, and industry guidance says its basic services may resemble those under a traditional contract even though they serve the design-builder's interest. The owner prepares its own RFP and performance requirements, the A/E is not acting as the owner's agent here, and industry guidance says the same documentation principles still apply.
questions.source: document variations for design- build delivery method

questions.question: A county is procuring a design-build courthouse, and the selected design-builder will then obtain proposals from trade subcontractors. How does industry guidance allocate preparation of the procurement and contracting requirements?

options.A: Design-builder for both the design-build contract and the subcontracts
options.B: Owner for the design-build contract; design-builder for subcontracts
options.C: Owner for both the design-build contract and the subcontracts
options.D: Owner's A/E for subcontracts; design-builder for the design-build contract

questions.explanation: Industry guidance gives the owner responsibility for the procurement and contracting requirements used to obtain the design-build contract itself, while the design-builder prepares the requirements used to get bids or proposals from its subcontractors. Options that assign both sets to one party, or that bring the owner's A/E into subcontract procurement, do not match that split.

questions.question: In developer-led design-build, the design-builder hires a separate contractor to perform the construction. Which statement about procuring that construction contract matches industry guidance?

options.A: Any of the three design-bid-build options may be used; negotiation is most likely
options.B: Any of the three design-bid-build options may be used; competitive bidding is most likely
options.C: Only the negotiated option may be used, since design-builders use known contractors
options.D: Only competitive bidding may be used, since it protects the owner's budget

questions.explanation: Industry guidance states that when a design-builder contracts out the construction, as in developer-led design-build, any of the three design-bid-build options may be used, but negotiation is the most likely because design-builders tend to work with contractors they know. Competitive bidding is allowed but not described as the usual choice, and industry guidance does not restrict the design-builder to a single option.

questions.question: During which stage does a design-builder prepare its subcontract procurement requirements, including instructions to bidders?

options.A: The project delivery stage
options.B: The procurement stage
options.C: The design stage
options.D: The construction documents stage

questions.explanation: Industry guidance places the design-builder's preparation of subcontract procurement documents, such as instructions to bidders, in the construction documents stage. The project delivery stage is when the owner may already have selected the design-builder, and the procurement and design stages are not where industry guidance locates this task.

questions.question: How does industry guidance say the contract between an owner and a design-builder may be formed?

options.A: As a stipulated-sum contract from bids on complete construction documents
options.B: As a negotiated contract that results from the owner's RFP
options.C: As a cost-plus contract awarded by the owner's independent A/E
options.D: As a multiparty agreement among the owner, A/E, and contractor

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes the owner-design-builder contract may be a negotiated contract resulting from an RFP issued by the owner, with that selection possibly occurring during the project delivery stage. Bidding on complete documents does not fit because the design-builder produces the construction documents, the owner's A/E does not award the contract, and design-build gives the owner a single agreement with the design-builder rather than a multiparty agreement.

questions.question: A specifier consulting to a design-builder is assembling bid packages for the mechanical and electrical subcontracts. The owner's representative asks whether these bid packages will need a fundamentally different format. What does industry guidance indicate?

options.A: They must be written entirely as performance specifications
options.B: They should omit instructions to bidders because terms are negotiated
options.C: They may closely resemble documents for other delivery methods
options.D: They must be reviewed by the owner's attorney before issue

questions.explanation: Industry guidance observes that subcontract procurement requirements and construction documents in design-build might not vary significantly from those prepared for design-bid-build or other methods. Instructions to bidders are specifically named among the documents the design-builder prepares, and industry guidance imposes no all-performance format or owner-attorney review on these subcontract packages.

questions.question: Most standard owner-design-builder agreements are organized around which two phases?

options.A: Preliminary design phase and documents/construction phase
options.B: Proposal phase and design-build construction phase
options.C: Schematic design phase and design development phase
options.D: Bridging documents phase and construction phase

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that most standard design-build agreements are written for two phases: a preliminary design phase and a documents/construction phase. Proposal, schematic design, design development, and bridging are not the phase pair industry guidance identifies for these agreements.
questions.source: contract requirements — agreements and conditions of the contract

questions.question: Which group of organizations does industry guidance list as sources of standard agreements and conditions of the contract between an owner and a design-builder?

options.A: AIA, EJCDC, DBIA, and CSI
options.B: AIA, DBIA, ICC, and ConsensusDocs Coalition
options.C: EJCDC, DBIA, ASTM, and ConsensusDocs Coalition
options.D: AIA, EJCDC, DBIA, and ConsensusDocs Coalition

questions.explanation: Industry guidance names the AIA, the EJCDC, the Design-Build Institute of America, and the ConsensusDocs Coalition as publishers of standard owner-design-builder agreements and conditions. CSI, ICC, and ASTM publish formats, codes, and standards respectively, not design-build contract forms.
questions.source: contract requirements — agreements and conditions of the contract

questions.question: During negotiation of a design-build agreement for a data center, the design-builder proposes using its own general conditions developed for that building type instead of a standard form. What does industry guidance indicate?

options.A: Only standard AIA, EJCDC, DBIA, or ConsensusDocs forms may be used
options.B: Only conditions prepared by the owner's attorney may be used
options.C: It may use its own conditions tailored to a project type
options.D: Its general conditions must be bound as a separate section within Division 01

questions.explanation: Industry guidance lists standard AIA, EJCDC, DBIA, and ConsensusDocs forms but also acknowledges that a design-builder may have its own general conditions tailored to a specific project type. Industry guidance does not limit the parties to standard forms or to owner-attorney documents, and conditions of the contract are not bound in Division 01; most design-build agreements build the conditions into the agreement form itself.
questions.source: contract requirements — agreements and conditions of the contract

questions.question: On a design-build project, a roofing subcontractor submits shop drawings. Under the submittal procedure industry guidance describes for design-build, what happens next?

options.A: The A/E checks them first, then forwards them to the design-builder for distribution
options.B: The design-builder checks them, then sends them to the A/E or back to the subcontractor
options.C: The owner checks them, then returns them to the subcontractor through the design-builder
options.D: The A/E receives them directly from the subcontractor and sends a copy to the owner

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says shop drawings, samples, and product data in design-build are received and checked by the design-builder, which either distributes them to the A/E or returns them to the subcontractor for resubmittal. The A/E does not receive them first or directly from the subcontractor, and the owner gets a set of approved shop drawings rather than performing the initial check.

questions.question: Section 01 21 00 Allowances can be used on a design-build project to postpone some design decisions. Why does industry guidance advise keeping such unknowns to a minimum?

options.A: Design-build is selected partly because requirements are predictable
options.B: Allowances undermine the design-builder's ability to control cost
options.C: Allowances must be priced by the owner before the RFP is issued
options.D: Allowances prevent the owner from tracking substitutions

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that allowances actually help the design-builder keep accurate cost control when some products are unknown, but unknowns should be minimized because one reason for selecting design-build is that project requirements are reasonably predictable. Industry guidance does not tie allowances to RFP pricing or link them to substitution tracking.

questions.question: A design-build clinic is nearing completion. Under Section 01 70 00 for design-build, how is substantial completion handled?

options.A: The owner's A/E inspects and certifies the date to the design-builder
options.B: The owner inspects and gives the results to the design-builder to evaluate
options.C: The building official inspects and issues the certificate to the owner
