questions.explanation: When numbers define both size and quantity, write the quantity as a word and the size in figures (e.g., three 1/2-inch holes; five 2 by 4s).

questions.question: Which money and time references are written correctly?

options.D: $200 and 9 p.m.

questions.explanation: Omit unneeded zeroes in time and money references ($200, not $200.00; 9 p.m., not 9:00 p.m.).

questions.question: A quantity of less than one expressed as a decimal is written:
questions.explanation: For quantities less than one, place a zero before the decimal point (0.235).

questions.question: Under recommended capitalization practice, which word stays lowercase even when it refers to the specific project?

options.A: Work
options.B: subcontractor
options.C: Contractor
options.D: Project Manual

questions.explanation: Subcontract and subcontractor are not capitalized because they do not refer to a specific party defined in the agreement; Contractor, Work, and Project Manual are capitalized when used specifically.

questions.question: When referring to one of the three parts of SectionFormat, industry guidance capitalizes the word as:

options.A: PART, in all capitals
options.B: Part, except in Division 01
options.C: part, in lowercase
options.D: Part, with an initial capital

questions.explanation: Industry guidance lists PART (all capitals) when referring to one of the three parts of SectionFormat.

questions.question: How should each item in a list of subparagraphs end?

options.A: With a comma, except the last item
options.B: With a semicolon, adding "and" before the last
options.C: With no punctuation
options.D: With a period, showing no content is missing

questions.explanation: All paragraphs end with a period or colon; a parent paragraph ends with a colon, and each list item ends with a period to indicate no content is missing.

questions.question: Which series is punctuated the way industry guidance requires?

options.A: Clean walls, floors, & ceilings.
options.B: Clean walls; floors; and ceilings.
options.C: Clean walls, floors, and ceilings.
options.D: Clean walls, floors and ceilings.

questions.explanation: Use the Oxford comma - a comma after each item in a series, including the item before the conjunction.

questions.question: Why does industry guidance reject "in lieu of" in specifications?

options.A: It is an archaic adverb like "herewith"
options.B: It is a foreign-language expression
options.C: It implies an owner-approved substitution
options.D: It is a phrase with a missing object

questions.explanation: Do not use foreign language terms or expressions; incorrect: in lieu, correct: instead. Missing-object phrases (as directed) and archaic adverbs (herewith) are separate items on the list.

questions.question: "If materials are rejected, the contractor shall replace same at no additional cost." Which revision does industry guidance label as preferred?

options.A: Remove rejected materials and provide acceptable materials at no additional cost.
options.B: Replace any rejected materials at no additional cost.
options.C: If materials are rejected, replace with acceptable materials at no additional cost.
options.D: If materials are rejected, the Contractor shall replace them at no additional cost.

questions.explanation: Industry guidance: "same" should not be used as a pronoun. The second option is the "better" version; the preferred version uses remove and provide. "Any" is on the avoid list.

questions.question: In a streamlined specification, the explanatory statement in Division 01 or the supplementary conditions says a colon stands for:

options.A: "will," for actions of the owner
options.B: "as indicated on Drawings"
options.C: "and/or," when items are listed
options.D: "shall," "shall be," or "shall comply with," as the context requires

questions.explanation: The words shall, shall be, and shall comply with are included by inference where a colon is used within sentences or phrases.

questions.question: Streamlining is best suited to which content?

options.A: Narrative descriptions of the work
options.B: Statements of owner responsibilities
options.C: Lists of products, materials, and reference standards
options.D: Step-by-step installation instructions

questions.explanation: Streamlining is difficult to adapt to descriptions or instructions; it is used to list products, materials, reference standards, and other itemized specifications.

questions.question: "Store all millwork under shelter, etc." Which pair of specification language rules does this sentence break?

options.A: It names a party, and it uses "shall"
options.B: "All" is usually unnecessary, and "etc." is on the avoid list
options.C: It lacks the imperative mood, and it uses a symbol
options.D: It uses a foreign term, and it omits a colon

questions.explanation: The word all is usually unnecessary (Store millwork under shelter). Industry guidance lists etc. among words and expressions to avoid. "Store" is already imperative.

questions.question: Which wording does industry guidance show as preferred?

options.A: Within manufacturer's recommended time limit.
options.B: Within the time recommended by manufacturer.
options.C: Within the time limit as recommended.
options.D: Within the time recommended by the manufacturer thereof.

questions.explanation: Shorten sentences by using modifiers instead of prepositional phrases. "Within the time recommended by manufacturer" is correct; the modifier form is preferred.

questions.question: Which is the preferred version of "Tests shall be performed to determine strength and establish qualities"?

options.A: Tests shall be performed to determine strength and to establish quality.
options.B: Perform tests determining strength and to establish qualities.
options.C: Tests are to determine strength and establish quality.
options.D: Perform tests to determine strength and to establish quality.

questions.explanation: Parallel construction: the second option is correct but wordy; the preferred version is imperative and parallel. "Is to" is not recommended.

questions.question: A designation such as "ASTM C270" or "Section 01 42 19" in specification text should be:

options.A: Written without the internal space, as one continuous designation
options.B: Set in italics
options.C: Kept on one line with a non-breaking space
options.D: Enclosed in parentheses

questions.explanation: Industry standard designations and MasterFormat numbers should appear on the same line; use a non-breaking space to keep them together.

questions.question: Abbreviations used in a project should be defined:

options.A: Only in the supplementary conditions
options.B: On the drawings or in Division 01
options.C: In Part 1 of each section that uses them
options.D: In the instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: Abbreviations should be defined on the drawings or in Division 01, and should be used only on drawings and schedules where space is limited.

questions.question: In specification text, underlines should be:

options.A: Not used
options.B: Used only for defined terms
options.C: Minimized, like parentheses
options.D: Used for section titles

questions.explanation: Parentheses and quotation marks should be minimized or avoided; underlines should not be used.

questions.question: "Contractor shall install bathroom accessories which are to be purchased under an allowance." Which revision does industry guidance label as preferred?

options.A: Install bathroom accessories to be purchased under an allowance.
options.B: Install bathroom accessories, which are purchased under an allowance.
options.C: Contractor shall install the bathroom accessories purchased under the allowance in Division 01.
options.D: Install bathroom accessories purchased under allowances specified in Section 01 21 00.

questions.explanation: Which and other relative pronouns should be used sparingly. The second option is the "better" version; the preferred version is imperative and cites the allowance section.

questions.question: The "four Cs" for effective specification communication are:

options.A: Concise, correct, consistent, and complete
options.B: Clear, complete, correct, and coordinated
options.C: Clear, concise, complete, and correct
options.D: Clear, concise, consistent, and coordinated

questions.explanation: Specifications follow the four Cs - clear, concise, complete, and correct.

questions.question: A PPD describes a curtain wall under B2010.40 whose scope also covers aluminum-framed entrances, panic hardware, and low-E insulated glass. Those same entrances, hardware, and glass types also appear in storefronts and hollow metal doors elsewhere. How should this work be organized in MasterFormat sections?

options.A: All components in 08 44 13 Glazed Aluminum Curtain Walls, because the PPD describes a single system
options.B: All components in Section 08 44 00, following UniFormat's cross-reference for B2010.40
options.C: Framing in 08 44 13, entrances in 08 42 13, panic hardware in 08 71 00, glazing in 08 80 00
options.D: Framing and glazing in 08 44 13, with entrances and panic hardware together in 08 42 13

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that a curtain wall's framing, entrances, hardware, and glazing could share one section, but when the entrances, hardware, and glazing are also used by other assemblies such as storefronts or hollow metal doors, each goes to its own section: 08 44 13 for the framing, 08 42 13 for the entrances, 08 71 00 for door hardware, and 08 80 00 for glazing. Keeping them in one curtain wall section would force the other assemblies to rely on it for shared products.

questions.question: A schematic-design PPD describes element B2010 Exterior Walls as metal stud framing, glass-mat sheathing, a fluid-applied air barrier, rigid insulation, and brick veneer. At design development, the specifier begins the outline specifications in MasterFormat. How should she treat this PPD description?

options.A: As a resource whose components will likely be split among several specification sections
options.B: As the text of one exterior wall section, since the PPD already describes a complete assembly
options.C: As a superseded document, since PPD content is not carried forward into outline specifications
options.D: As an attachment to the outline specifications, so the UniFormat element numbers remain in use

questions.explanation: Industry guidance places the switch from UniFormat to MasterFormat at design development, when the PPDs prepared during schematic design serve as a resource for the outline specifications. It cautions that a PPD's system and assembly descriptions bundle materials, products, and components that will likely be specified in several sections, so one element usually spreads across multiple MasterFormat sections. The PPD is neither discarded nor attached to keep UniFormat numbers in use, and it is not copied whole into a single section.

questions.question: A specifier is about to draft the Division 01 sections for a public library. Which procurement and contracting document has the most influence on Division 01, and which Parts of other sections may it also affect?

options.A: 00 70 00 Conditions of the Contract; PART 1 and PART 3 of some sections
options.B: 00 70 00 Conditions of the Contract; PART 2 of most product sections
options.C: 00 52 00 Agreement Forms; PART 1 and PART 3 of some sections
options.D: 00 52 00 Agreement Forms; PART 2 of most product sections

questions.explanation: Industry guidance identifies 00 70 00 Conditions of the Contract as the document with the most influence on preparing Division 01, adding that it may also shape PART 1 (General) and PART 3 (Execution) provisions in some sections. Agreement forms are not singled out this way, and PART 2 (Products) is not named as an area the conditions influence.
questions.source: reviewing the procurement and contracting requirements

questions.question: On a phased school addition, the specifier wants to know which work packages are planned so she can decide the order in which to prepare sections. Which Division 00 document may provide this?

options.A: 00 31 32 Geotechnical Data
options.B: 00 31 13 Preliminary Schedules
options.C: 00 31 19 Existing Condition Information
options.D: 00 31 21 Survey Information

questions.explanation: Industry guidance notes that 00 31 13 Preliminary Schedules may identify project phasing for work packages, which lets the specifier plan the sequence for preparing sections. 00 31 32 Geotechnical Data is cited instead as the source for sections such as waterproofing, earthwork, and pavements, and industry guidance does not point to existing condition information or survey information for phasing.
questions.source: reviewing the procurement and contracting requirements

questions.question: A specifier is editing a stainless-steel fabrications section. It needs a No. 4 satin shop finish applied before delivery, and it also needs methods for touch-up finishing done in the field after installation. Per SectionFormat, where does each belong?

options.A: Both in the PART 2 Finishes article, which covers all of the section's finishes
options.B: Shop finish in the PART 2 Fabrication article; field finishing methods in PART 2 Finishes
options.C: Shop finish in the PART 2 Finishes article; field finishing methods described in PART 3
options.D: Shop finish in the PART 2 Finishes article; field finishing methods in PART 1 Field Conditions

questions.explanation: The SectionFormat commentary puts factory and shop finishes, along with materials for field finishing when the section covers them, in the PART 2 Finishes article, which lists Shop Finishing Methods as a subordinate title; field finishing methods are described in PART 3. Field finishing materials may sit in PART 2, but the methods do not. The Fabrication article covers shop fabrication and assembly, and PART 1 Field Conditions addresses ambient and existing conditions, not finishing methods.

questions.question: A specifier is coordinating the PREPARATION articles of individual sections with Division 01. Which requirement belongs in Section 01 71 00 Examination and Preparation?

options.A: Cleaning glazing channels and framing members just before the glass is set
options.B: Basic requirements for installing owner-furnished products in the work
options.C: Removing loosely bonded coatings from joint substrates before sealant work
options.D: Initial construction layout and surveying for the project

questions.explanation: Industry guidance assigns 01 71 00 the unique requirements for preparing for construction, such as initial construction layout, protection of adjacent construction, and surveying, plus the basic requirements for preparing to install products. Basic requirements for installing owner-furnished products go in 01 73 00 Execution instead. Readying a particular surface to receive one section's products, such as glazing channels or sealant joints, belongs in that section's PART 3 Preparation article.

questions.question: After issuing an addendum that revises six specification sections, the specifier must distribute and archive the revised sections. Which approach follows recommended version control?

options.A: Issue native word-processing files with tracked changes so bidders can see edits
options.B: Issue a neutral format such as PDF, secured against unauthorized modification
options.C: Issue only the changed pages, archiving superseded versions under the same file names
options.D: Issue editable files so the contractor can update the conformed set directly

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says revisions should be distributed and archived in a neutral format, such as PDF or an internet-based posting, with security features that keep the contract documents from being modified except by the expressly designated means. Editable native files invite uncontrolled changes, and reusing file names defeats the consistent naming protocol that version control needs.
questions.source: archive electronic files for version control

questions.question: At the close of a project, the specifier archives the project manual revision log along with the final documents. What is the main reason for archiving that log?

options.A: To help update the office master guide specifications with lessons learned
options.B: To give the contractor a basis for pricing change orders after contract award
options.C: To serve as part of the owner's record documents at substantial completion
options.D: To document each addendum for the bidders' acknowledgment on the bid form

questions.explanation: Industry guidance calls for archiving the revision log so it can be used to update office master guide specifications and capture lessons learned from the project. Change-order pricing, record documents, and bid-form acknowledgment of addenda are separate processes that the log is not intended to serve.
questions.source: archive electronic files for version control

questions.question: A specifier is setting up a project manual revision log template for the firm. Which set of entries should each record in the log capture?

options.A: Project name, section number and title, the editor's initials, and the file's last-saved time
options.B: Owner's project number, the addendum number, bidder acknowledgments, and the change's cost
options.C: Project name and number, section number and title, and a brief description of each change
options.D: Section number and title, the reviewing consultant's name, and the date the AHJ stamped it

questions.explanation: Industry guidance says the log should capture the project name and the owner's or A/E's project number, the specification section number and title, and a short description of the changes. Editor initials, save times, bidder acknowledgments, cost impacts, and AHJ stamp dates are not among the entries industry guidance lists.
questions.source: archive electronic files for version control
